issues.body:
## Problem

The transcript ruler marks only the newest sentence. The operator cannot see which part of the meeting is on screen. A hover grows only one tick, so a tick in a dense ruler is hard to hit. The ruler has no way to page through the transcript.

The reference is the message navigator of a chat app (video from the operator): grey ticks, the ticks of the visible messages in full ink, a dock-style magnification on hover, a preview card, and an arrow at the top.

## Decisions (agreed with the operator, 2026-10-13)

1. **Colour.** Ticks keep the colour of their speaker (`ui-design.md`: one tick per sentence, speaker colour, at least 3:1). The emphasis comes from length and thickness, not from opacity, so the 3:1 rule stays true.
2. **Visible range.** The ticks of the sentences on screen are longer and thicker. This replaces the "newest sentence" emphasis (`IsCurrent`). When the transcript follows the live edge, the emphasis is at the bottom of the ruler.
3. **Dock magnification.** The hovered tick is the longest. The two ticks on each side get progressively shorter.
4. **Arrows.** A chevron above the ruler and a chevron below it.
   - The up arrow brings the last sentence above the screen to the bottom of the screen. This is one page up, with no hidden sentence skipped.
   - The down arrow brings the first sentence below the screen to the top of the screen.
   - An arrow is disabled when nothing is off screen in its direction. The arrows reserve their space, so the ruler never reflows.

## Out of scope

- The preview card keeps its layout.
- Topic ticks (#34) are not changed.

## Tests

- `TranscriptRulerTests`: in-view flags, dock reach, page targets, arrow availability.
- `ColumnScrollWiringTests`-style test: scrolling marks the visible ticks; the down arrow moves the next unseen sentence to the top.

issues.body:
Part of #209. Found in the review of #224 (comment 4241406658).

## Problem

`WorkspaceStore` writes `workspaces.json`, `kanal-workspace.json` and `meeting.json` in place with `File.WriteAllText`. This causes two faults:

1. **A crash or a power loss during a write leaves a damaged file.** A damaged `meeting.json` is one source of the "record cannot be read" issue that spec #209 resolves. This ticket removes that cause.
2. **A concurrent reader can see a part of a file.** Since #224, a background scan reads these files while the UI thread can write them. The reader then reports a false issue for one scan. On Windows, a write can also fail while the scan holds the file open.

## What

1. Every store write goes to `<file>.tmp` in the same folder, is flushed to disk, and then replaces the target with `File.Move(tmp, file, overwrite: true)` (or `File.Replace` where that is safer on Windows).
2. A `.tmp` file that a crash leaves behind is ignored by the listing and replaced by the next write.
3. Reads keep their current behaviour.

## Done when

- Tests in `tests/Kanal.Core.UnitTests`: a write never leaves a part of the target; a left-over `.tmp` file does not show as an issue and is replaced by the next write; existing store tests stay green. TDD.
- `docs/PROGRESS.md` entry. A CHANGELOG bullet: "Kanal no longer damages a meeting record when the computer stops during a save."

Part of #209. Core only, no UI.

## What

1. `StoreProblemKind` gets finer kinds for meeting folders. Today all of them are `Unreadable`:
   - `RecordMissing`: a meeting folder holds no `meeting.json`.
   - `RecordDamaged`: `meeting.json` cannot be parsed, is empty, or misses fields.
   - `Misfiled`: the record's id does not match its folder name.
   `ListMeetings` reports these kinds. The subject is the **meeting folder** in all three cases (not the `meeting.json` path).
2. `WorkspaceStore.RecoverMeeting(workspaceId, folder)` → result that says `Recovered(MeetingRecord)` or `SetAside(newPath)` or a `StoreProblem`.
   - Valid only for a direct subfolder of the project's `meetings` folder. Anything else is refused.
   - Rebuild rules (spec #209, decision 7): id = folder name if valid; languages = source and translation languages in `transcript.jsonl`; created/started/ended from transcript timestamps and file times; title = `FreeTitle` of a caller-supplied base title (the host passes the localized "Recovered meeting yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm").
   - A damaged `meeting.json` is renamed to `meeting.json.damaged` first (suffix if taken). Never overwritten, never deleted.
   - If the id is invalid or no utterance is readable: move the folder to `<project>/kanal-set-aside/<folder name>` (numeric suffix on a clash).
3. `WorkspaceStore.ReidentifyMeeting(workspaceId, folder)` for `Misfiled`: rewrite the record's id to the folder name. Refuse if the folder name is not a valid id or if that id is already listed.

## Done when

- Tests in `tests/Kanal.Core.UnitTests` cover each kind, recover, set aside, the `.damaged` rename, name clashes, refusal outside `meetings`, and re-identify. TDD.
- No file is ever deleted by these operations (assert it).

Part of #209. Core only, no UI.

## What

1. `WorkspaceStore.RelocateWorkspace(id, newRootPath)`: point an existing project row to a new folder.

Implements decisions 14 to 17 of [ADR 0055](https://github.com/TONiiV/Kanal/blob/main/docs/adr/0055-speaker-attribution.md). Adds the diarization model catalog, the download state and the readiness state.

This PR adds no diarization inference. Issues #108 and #109 add it.

## Catalog

The catalog has one segmentation model and four embedding candidates. We read the sizes from the GitHub releases API. We recomputed every SHA-256 from the downloaded file on 2026-09-08. The four embedding hashes also match the upstream `checksum.txt`.

| id | role | size | licence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pyannote-segmentation-3-0` | segmentation | 6.6 MB | MIT |
| `3dspeaker-campplus-zh-en` | embedding | 27.0 MB | Apache-2.0 |
| `3dspeaker-eres2net-base-zh` | embedding | 37.8 MB | Apache-2.0 |
| `wespeaker-cnceleb-resnet34` | embedding | 25.3 MB | Apache-2.0 |
| `titanet-small` | embedding | 38.4 MB | CC-BY-4.0, attribution required (in `LicenseNote`) |

The catalog has no default embedding model. ADR 0055 decision 16 says that measured DER decides the default.

## Licence gate

The Rev Reverb models are in the same release as the segmentation model. Their licence forbids commercial use. The DiariZen weights are CC-BY-NC-4.0.

`ModelLicense` records whether a licence permits commercial use. `DiarizationModelInfo` rejects a licence that does not. If someone lists a banned model, the catalog throws on first use and the test suite fails. A mutation test confirmed the gate: with the check set to `true`, `ANonCommercialModelCannotBeAddedToACatalogAtAll` fails.

## Readiness

`DiarizationModelCatalog.Readiness` reads the disk. It returns `Ready` when a segmentation model and an embedding model are both present. Any other input returns `NotDownloaded`. It never throws.

The catalog reports only *not downloaded* and *ready*, as PR #126 does. `DiarizationModelDownload` owns *downloading* and *failed* for one file.

agent_prs.body:
把「这句话对应录音的哪一段字节」变成一个有人负责回答的问题。ADR 0055 的决定 9–11 与 7，`#63` 依赖本片。

## 问题

`docs/design/meeting-evidence.md` 从设计评审起就挂着同一条警告：ASR 的时间戳和 WAV 里的偏移，在暂停、重连、文件分段之后是否还对得上，没人验证过。而马上有两个功能要靠这个对齐——发言人归属要拿刚定稿那句话的采样，逐句回放要拿一小时前那句话的字节区间。各做一套，就会得到两套不一致的错。

## 建的东西

`Kanal.Core.Meetings.MeetingTimeline`，一个类，两种查询。

**计量单位是「已接受音频的字节数」，不是墙上的钟。** 这是本片唯一真正重要的决定。用时间是显而易见的选法，也是错的：操作员出去谈自己这边，`MeetingSession.PushAudioAsync` 把那一分钟拦在门口，一条按时间走的时间轴就得记得减掉这一分钟——而「记得减掉」正是暂停语义拒绝存在的第二个地方。只数会话真正收下的音频，这个缺口就根本不存在。`AudioAccepted` 本来就只为这些音频触发（录音器挂在上面就是这个原因），时间轴挂在同一件事实上，只是早一层。

**ASR 时钟是另一口钟，只在一个 ASR 会话内可信。** 重连就归零。`AsrClockRestarted()` 记下新的零点落在时间轴的哪里；关键是偏移在**句子第一次被看见时就钉住**，而不是每条 partial 都重新查一遍。不钉住的话，一次落在某句最后一条 partial 与它的 final 之间的重启，会把这句话往后挪整整一场会。

**两种查询，因为是两个问题。** `LocateInRecording` 给出文件路径加该文件 PCM 数据内的字节区间，对时间轴见过的任何句子都有效，是 #63 要用的；开会十分钟后才开的录音、磁盘满而中断的录音、重开成第二个文件的录音，每句话都拿到它说出来时真正在跑的那一段，落在段与段之间的句子拿到 `NotRecorded`。`TakeRecentAudio` 直接给采样，出自一个默认 60 秒的有界环形缓冲，是切片 4 逐句嵌入要用的。

## 我自己定的、工单留白的几处

- **老化出缓冲返回 `AgedOut`，是一个答案，不是异常，也不是一段看起来很合理、实际来自会议别处的字节。** 区间统一夹到「实际已接受的音频」以内——这一步正是让环形缓冲只剩一种失败可报（老化）而不是两种（还有「尚未写入」）。
- **`TEndMs == null`（partial，以及某些 provider 的 final）解析成「截至目前已接受的全部音频」，并标 `EndIsOpen`。** 一句话不可能结束在还没到达的音频之后，所以这是一个诚实的上界；标志位则挡住消费者把它当成测出来的结束时间。这类句子在下一次 `Observe` 之前不会自己长大。
- **由录音器告诉时间轴文件从哪个字节开始**，而不是在 view model 的调用处再算一遍：`MeetingRecorder` 本来就是唯一知道录音何时开始、也唯一知道一次失败的写入结束了它的地方。这也让这段逻辑落在 `Kanal.Core.UnitTests` 里可测。
- 公开面是 `Kanal.Core` 里的 `MeetingTimeline`；环形缓冲 `RecentAudioBuffer` 是 internal，只经由时间轴访问，因为它的线程安全依赖时间轴的锁。

## 没做的

- 没有把归属或回放做出来——那是切片 3、4 和 #63。
- 没有给 `Utterance` 或中继报文加任何字段。跨重连的消歧是在 transcript 到达的当下解析、按 id 记下来的，因此不需要把 epoch 写进 wire format，手机端和快照一个字节都没变。
- 没有动 `CHANGELOG.md`：本片不产生操作员看得见的行为。

## 在代码里发现的、与工单说法有出入的

1. **工单写「中继重连不影响映射」，但中继根本碰不到时间轴**——`IRelayPublisher` 只往外发文本，重连与音频路径无关。会毁掉映射的是 **ASR 会话**重启，测的也是这个。
2. **今天没有任何代码路径会重启 ASR 会话**：`MeetingSession.StartAsync` 第二次调用直接抛。所以 `AsrClockRestarted()` 目前只在开始时被调用一次。仍然直接测了它——真出现重启的那天，不是发现时间轴从来没处理过它的好日子。
3. **一个本片修不了的真问题，已写进 `docs/PROGRESS.md` 和 `meeting-eviden

issues.body:
实现 [ADR 0055](https://github.com/TONiiV/Kanal/blob/main/docs/adr/0055-speaker-attribution.md) 的**决定 9–11、7**。**#63 依赖本片。**

## 为什么先做这个

发言人归属和逐句回放要问的是同一个问题：**「这句话对应录音的哪一段字节」**。今天这个映射从来没有被验证过——`docs/design/meeting-evidence.md` 已经把它标成未验证：暂停间隙、重连、文件分段之后，ASR 的 `TStartMs`/`TEndMs` 与 WAV 里的偏移是否还对得上，没人知道。

两边各做一套的话，会得到两套不一致的错。

## 要做的

- 建立唯一的会议时间轴，ASR 时间戳与录音字节偏移在其上对齐，跨越暂停间隙、重连与文件分段。
- 有界的音频环形缓冲，从 `MeetingSession.AudioAccepted` 取——那个事件已经是暂停感知的（暂停时既不推给 ASR 也不落盘），归属自然继承同一语义。
- 定稿来得太晚、音频已经老化出缓冲的句子，标记为**未归属**，不猜。
- 顺手：`GladiaAsrProvider.Caps.Diarization` 从 `true` 改成 `false`。这个声明一直是假的——Gladia 的 `/v2/live` 请求体里根本没有 diarization 参数，那是预录接口才有的（2026-07-30 实测）。`FakeAsrProvider` 保留 `true`，用来测「provider 自带分离」那条路径不被误接管。

## 验收

- [ ] 任一定稿句子可解析出录音中的起止偏移
- [ ] 暂停恢复后时间轴不错位；暂停期间的音频不进入时间轴
- [ ] 中继重连不影响映射
- [ ] 音频老化出缓冲的句子返回「未归属」而非错误区间
- [ ] `Caps.Diarization` 反映各 provider 的真实能力

Closes #71. Batch 3 of #64, stories 46–50. Stacked on #77 (`feat/centre-toolbar`), which is stacked on #76.

## Screenshots

Headless Skia, 1320x760. Left to right: nothing connected, a room with points on the record, the speakers tab.

| No model connected | Points and decisions | Speakers |
|---|---|---|
| ![no model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TONiiV/Kanal/screenshots/pr-79/panel-no-model.png) | ![points](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TONiiV/Kanal/screenshots/pr-79/panel-points.png) | ![speakers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TONiiV/Kanal/screenshots/pr-79/panel-speakers.png) |

The whole window, points tab:

![window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TONiiV/Kanal/screenshots/pr-79/points.png)

## What the panel does

The right sidebar held one list — speakers plus the merge box. It now carries two tabs: **Points and decisions**, and **Speakers**, the second being what was already there. The tab header names the list, so the pane's own `SPEAKERS` heading and rule went with the move.

`MeetingInsights` (`Kanal.Core/Insights`) is a plain aggregate over `RoomState`, **not a provider interface**. #34 brings the model; an `IMeetingAnalyst` with one imaginary implementer would not give the panel anything to show today, and the ticket asks for the panel and its state, not the analyst.

## The two rules that make a candidate honest

- **An item that leads back to nothing said is refused, not shown.** `Record` filters source utterance ids against the room and drops the item entirely if none survive. The candidate state exists to stop a guess reading as a commitment — an item with no source behind it is that same failure with nothing left to check it against.
- **A decision arrives as a candidate; only a person makes it a commitment.** Kind and state render side by side, `Confirm` is present only while it is a candidate, and the supporting utterances print under the item, so "leads back to what was said" is something the operator reads rather than trusts.

Batch 1 of the delivery order in #64. Covers user stories 1-7 of `docs/specs/meeting-workspace.md`; the approved visual baseline is `docs/design/meeting-workspace.md`, with the prototype at `docs/design/meeting-ui.prototype.html`.

## What

Replace the current single-window composition with three full-height regions: a left workspace sidebar, a centre column carrying the toolbar and transcript, and a right assistant sidebar. Each sidebar collapses and expands independently, and its inner edge drags to resize.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Left, centre and right each occupy a declared layout region. Collapsing a sidebar must not let the transcript fall into a zero-width column — that was the prototype's failure mode and is explicitly out of bounds for the implementation.
- [ ] Either sidebar collapses and expands independently; all four combinations keep the transcript usable.
- [ ] A collapsed sidebar exposes an expand affordance on the corresponding side of the centre toolbar, and that affordance stays reachable at narrow widths.
- [ ] Dragging a sidebar's inner edge resizes it within a bounded range. The prototype's 180-480 px is a calibration start, not a cross-platform acceptance number.
- [ ] A chosen width survives collapse and re-expansion.
- [ ] Left and right header bars share the centre toolbar's height so the separators line up.
- [ ] No horizontal scrollbar and no wrapping toolbar at any window width the host supports.

## Testing

Per `CLAUDE.md`, pixel, layout and style assertions stay out of the suite. Verify from the host view model: collapse state, retained width, expand-command availability, and that the transcript region is present and non-zero in every sidebar combination. Alignment, long names and multi-script labels get separate visual acceptance.

## Out of scope

Sidebar *contents* — workspace selector, meeting list, points and decisions, speaker management — land in their own tickets. This one is the shell and its state.

agent_prs.body:
The P&L report was treating revenue as the raw credit total instead of signed movement, so a revenue debit reversal (refund / reversal) could remain visible as positive revenue and inflate net profit. This also affected expense/COGS reversals, where a negative movement should offset the period totals rather than being ignored.

- **Signed P&L totals**
  - Compute revenue as `credit - debit`, and expense/COGS as `debit - credit`.
  - Keep the reported total for each section in signed form so reversals, refunds, and partial offsets net correctly with the original period activity.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Added coverage for:
    - ordinary revenue/expense/COGS totals
    - full reversal to zero
    - partial revenue refund reducing net profit
    - negative totals when refunds exceed current-period activity
  - These cases lock in the accounting behavior expected in live UAT scenarios and prevent future regressions in the same path.

- **Accounting semantics**
  - Revenue and expense sections now reflect net signed movement across the reporting window rather than a simple sum of credits/debits.
  - This preserves the expected cash ledger and P&L reconciliation for refunded or reversed journal entries without altering audit records.

```ts
const impact =
  account.accountType === 'REVENUE'
    ? credit.subtract(debit)
    : debit.subtract(credit);

amounts.set(account.id, (amounts.get(account.id) ?? DecimalMoney.zero()).add(impact));
```

This keeps P&L totals aligned with the underlying posted journals and ensures a debit reversal against a credited revenue account nets to zero instead of showing as revenue remaining on the report.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #32

issues.body:
Confirmed through live browser UAT in the explicitly marked test workspace on 5 Nov 2026. A simulated RM1 Money In credits Sales Revenue (4100), then a simulated RM1 Money Out debits the SAME Sales Revenue account as a reversal. Both posted journals balance, use 2026-10-05, and fall within the report's 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-31 period. SQL verification shows Revenue debits RM1, credits RM1, net RM0; UAT cash ledger also nets RM0.

Observed: /reports/profit-loss still shows Revenue RM1, Expenses RM0, Net Profit RM1, including after a full page refresh.
Expected: Revenue RM0 and Net Profit RM0 for these two reversing entries. Reporting must aggregate signed movement (credits minus debits for revenue), including refunds/reversals, rather than summing only credits.

Repro references: UAT-IN-20261105-01 and UAT-REV-20261105-01. Descriptions are explicitly UAT ONLY; no actual payment occurred. Fix with regression coverage for revenue reversal, expense reversal and normal signed totals; verify live reconciliation before marking UAT complete. Do not delete financial audit records.

agent_prs.title: feat: integrate @warpcode/cloakenv as Hermes secret source plugin

issues.body:
### Problem Statement

Hermes currently supports secret-source plugins (see https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/secret-source-plugin#the-secretsource-abc) but there is no integration with our @warpcode/cloakenv secret provider. This limits our ability to use CloakEnv-managed secrets directly within Hermes.

### Proposed Solution

Implement a Hermes SecretSource plugin that delegates secret retrieval to @warpcode/cloakenv so Hermes can load secrets from CloakEnv. The plugin should:

- Implement the SecretSource ABC as specified in the Hermes developer guide
- Support the minimal lifecycle methods Hermes expects (initialization, fetch/get secret, and teardown)
- Accept configuration for CloakEnv (e.g., path, namespace, auth/token) from Hermes plugin config
- Cache secrets where appropriate and honor TTL/refresh semantics if supported
- Provide clear error handling and logging so Hermes operators can debug secret access failures

Example usage in Hermes config (conceptual):

```yaml
secret_sources:
  - type: cloakenv
    config:
      path: /services/my-service
      namespace: prod
      token: ${CLOAK_TOKEN}
```


### Alternatives Considered

Alternatives considered:

- Use an existing supported secret-source backend (e.g., HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) and sync CloakEnv secrets to it — introduces sync complexity and added operational overhead.
- Add custom pre-launch scripting to populate Hermes environment variables from CloakEnv — brittle and less secure than a plugin.

Implementing a dedicated plugin provides the cleanest, most maintainable solution.

### Additional Context

References:

- Hermes secret source plugin guide: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/secret-source-plugin#the-secretsource-abc

issues.body:
### Problem Description

The `merge_pull_request.sh` wrapper script in `.github/skills/github-cli/scripts/merge_pull_request.sh` unconditionally hardcodes `--squash --delete-branch`:

```bash
gh pr merge "$pull_number" --repo "$owner"/"$repo" --squash --delete-branch
```

This causes two key failure modes:
1. **Branch Policy / Ruleset Rejection**: On repositories where branch rulesets enforce restricted merge policies (e.g., `Protect main` requiring admin bypass for bot-authored commits or merge queue policies), `gh pr merge` fails with:
   ```
   X Pull request <owner>/<repo>#<pr> is not mergeable: the base branch policy prohibits the merge.
   To use administrator privileges to immediately merge the pull request, add the --admin flag.
   ```
   Currently, `merge_pull_request.sh` does not support an `--admin` parameter, requiring manual fallback to raw `gh pr merge` commands.
2. **Unsupported Merge Method**: If a target repository or branch disables squash merging (e.g., only allows merge commits or rebases), the hardcoded `--squash` flag fails. The script does not inspect allowed merge methods or allow callers to specify the merge strategy.

---

### Proposed Solution

Enhance `.github/skills/github-cli/scripts/merge_pull_request.sh` with the following capabilities:

#### 1. Auto-Detect Allowed Merge Methods
Query the allowed merge methods for the PR's target base branch before executing the merge:
- **Branch Ruleset Evaluation**: Query `gh api "repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{base_branch}"` and inspect `pull_request` rules for `parameters.allowed_merge_methods`.
- **Repository-Level Fallback**: If no branch ruleset specifies merge methods, fall back to `gh api "repos/{owner}/{repo}"` (checking `allow_squash_merge`, `allow_merge_commit`, `allow_rebase_merge`).

#### 2. Default Method Selection
- If `squash` is present in the detected allowed methods, default to `squash`.
- If `squash` is **not** allowed, default to the **first** allowed merge method in the de

issues.body:
## Scope

Website branch `c5c90ee4d947c120e6173188710a116743999ad5`; website fixes should target `website`, not `main`.

## Problem

The Cloning the Fork block clones `https://github.com/0x5t4l1n/owasp-hunting.git` with no destination argument, then instructs `cd hunting`. Git uses the repository basename owasp-hunting for this clone, so the second command does not enter the checkout.

## Reproduction

Open `/docs/installation/` and inspect or copy Cloning the Fork. The displayed commands are the clone URL followed by cd hunting. Run them from a clean directory without a pre-existing hunting directory to encounter the missing-directory failure.

## Expected behavior

Use the cloned directory name consistently, or provide an explicit destination argument matching the cd command. Review the surrounding directory layout text for the same mismatch.

## Observed behavior

The global HTML rule sets `scroll-behavior: smooth`. The reduced-motion media rule shortens animation/transition durations but does not override scroll behavior. In an emulated reduced-motion browser, `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` is true while the computed HTML scroll behavior remains `smooth`.

1. Enable reduced motion in OS/browser accessibility settings, or use Chromium reduced-motion emulation.
2. Open `/payloads/sql-injection/` and follow a table-of-contents anchor such as Mitigation.

Local evidence: preference=true, computed scroll-behavior=smooth. Marking 1 identifies the anchor navigation; the annotation panel records those measured values. A still screenshot does not prove animation duration or how a particular user perceives motion, and no such measurement is claimed.

Disable smooth scrolling when reduced motion is requested, including ordinary TOC and direct-fragment navigation. Preserve normal navigation and the recently fixed header offset. A regression check should verify the computed behavior with reduced motion both enabled and disabled.

## Observed behavior

On the `/payloads/` index page, category cards display a title and a short summary description. The summary paragraph has an inline style `maxWidth: "200px"` along with `overflow: "hidden"`, `textOverflow: "ellipsis"`, and `whiteSpace: "nowrap"`.

In typical desktop and tablet viewports, the grid card container width is ~293px or wider. Due to the hardcoded `200px` limit, descriptions such as:
- "Database query manipulation through unsanitized input" (scrollWidth: 296px)
- "Query manipulation in MongoDB, Redis, CouchDB" (scrollWidth: 264px)
- "OS command execution via user input" (scrollWidth: 201px)
- "Template engine exploitation and RCE" (scrollWidth: 201px)

are truncated with an ellipsis despite 60px–90px of empty space remaining between the text and the right arrow icon. Additionally, no `title` attribute or tooltip exists on the element, preventing users from reading the full text on hover or focus.

## Reproduction

1. Open `/payloads/` in a desktop or laptop viewport (>1024px width).
2. Inspect the first card under Injection ("SQL Injection").
3. Note that the description is truncated to "Database query manipulation through un..." while significant horizontal whitespace remains inside the card.

Remove the hardcoded `maxWidth: "200px"` constraint to let the description fluidly utilize available container space (e.g. `flex: 1` or `maxWidth: "calc(100% - 1.5rem)"`), and add a `title` attribute containing the full `item.shortDescription` so readers can view complete summaries.

issues.body:
Website baseline: `ac81655f4ac3aa1250023a3a9a5e3a93c00ac059` (`website` branch), checked locally on 2026-10-28.

## Observed behavior

When opening the search modal (`Search.tsx`), `defaultItems` intends to display 5 quick links:
```tsx
const defaultItems: SearchItem[] = SEARCH_INDEX.filter((item) =>
  ["Getting Started", "SQL Injection", "XSS", "SSRF", "Contributing"].includes(item.title)
);
```

However, in `src/lib/search-data.ts`, those vulnerability categories are titled:
- `"Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)"` (line 24)
- `"SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)"` (line 186)

Because `.includes(item.title)` uses exact equality, both `"XSS"` and `"SSRF"` fail to match. Consequently, the quick links list displays only 3 items ("SQL Injection", "Getting Started", "Contributing"), silently dropping two of the project's primary payload categories.

## Reproduction

1. Open the website home `/` or any page.
2. Click the search button in the header (or press `/`).
3. View the initial "QUICK LINKS" list in the modal without typing.
4. Observe that only 3 items are shown; XSS and SSRF are missing from the list.

Update `Search.tsx` to match the exact titles in `search-data.ts` (e.g. `["Getting Started", "SQL Injection", "Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)", "SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)", "Contributing"]`) or filter by unique item `id` (`"payload-xss"`, `"payload-ssrf"`) so that all 5 intended quick links are presented to the user.

issues.body:
On 2026-10-03 one aws apply for #1078 took three approvals, two of them refused on a plan mismatch (runs [37083701544](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/actions/runs/37083701544) at 01:07 UTC and [37085109594](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/actions/runs/37085109594) at 01:24 UTC). Two gaps in infra CI let that happen, and the second one also leaves applies that can be approved but can only fail. Both workflows are infra CI, so this is for docker-deployer.

## 1. Branches are not updated after a bot merge

[update-branches.yml](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/blob/a804ce206df23628fde65904bcefd1c769068e6a/.github/workflows/update-branches.yml#L3-L7) runs on push to main and on `*/30 * * * *`. It did not run at all from 23:10 to 02:14 UTC (3 h 04 min), while tofu's merge job merged 14 pull requests, among them #1071 (00:53), #1083 (01:18), #1080 (01:22) and #1078 (01:32). The next push runs, at 02:16 and 02:20, came from #1074 and #1088, which a person merged. #1087, merged by the bot at 02:25, again started none.

Why: the [merge job](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/blob/a804ce206df23628fde65904bcefd1c769068e6a/.github/workflows/tofu.yml#L445-L459) calls the tacos `merge` step without `github-token`, so `scripts/merge.sh` runs `gh pr merge` with `github.token`, and a push made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` starts no workflow. [lint.yml](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/blob/a804ce206df23628fde65904bcefd1c769068e6a/.github/workflows/lint.yml) and [zizmor.yml](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/blob/a804ce206df23628fde65904bcefd1c769068e6a/.github/workflows/zizmor.yml) miss these pushes the same way. The schedule does not cover for it: the cron fired 4 times in 12 h 34 min (13:40, 19:02, 23:10, 02:14 UTC) instead of about 25.

What this cost on #1078: both refused runs were the newest run of #1078 when approved, and both failed because another pull request's aws apply landed between the run's plan and its approval. Run 37083701544 planned at 00:50 and #1071 merged at 00:53
issues.title: ci: stale branches and stale waiting applies cost extra aws approvals

Fixes #1575.

Generation 169 (#1572) brought JsonConfig, which ships three tables (`globaljsonlinks`, `globaljsonlinks_target`, `globaljsonlinks_wiki`), but `schema_update_generation` stayed at 164, so update.php never ran and the tables do not exist.

Every view of a `Data:` page now fails with `Wikimedia\Rdbms\DBQueryError`: JsonConfig's `ArticleViewFooter` hook (`GJLHooks::onArticleViewFooter`) queries `globaljsonlinks` to list the pages that use the data, since `$wgTrackGlobalJsonLinks` defaults to true. Reproduced on `Data:연습장.tab`, `Data:연습장.chart` and the new `Data:` pages; `action=raw` and `action=parse` on the same pages still work, which matches a failure in the view footer only. The `LinksUpdateComplete` hook writes to the same table, so saving a page that uses a chart probably logs the same error after the response.

This rolls to generation 170 with `schema_update_generation = 170`, so the new fastcgi runs update.php as it starts.

Before approving, the plan should create `http-170` and `fastcgi-170` (live is 169).

During the 1.46 window (femiwiki/femiwiki#645) the step that posts a pull request's ```wikitext blocks to 페미위키:업데이트 failed with `https://femiwiki.com/api.php: The wiki is currently in read-only mode.` and exit 1 ([run 37091582201](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/actions/runs/37091582201), #1089). Keeping the apply green is right: production has already changed. What is missing is a signal where the pull request is read.

- [x] Make a failed post visible on the run and the pull request, e.g. a `::error` annotation and a job-summary line, or a separate check that fails (#1332)
- [x] Decide whether a read-only wiki should defer the post (retry later, or leave it for `post update` dispatch) rather than count as a failure: it counts as a failure, and the summary line says to run `post update` (#1332)
- [x] Check the change against a read-only failure, e.g. by `post-update.php --dry-run` or a stubbed API error: the `post-update` lint job runs it against a read-only stub wiki (#1332)

agent_prs.title: aws(IAM): drop unused KMS statement from WriteMysqlRootPassword

issues.body:
`data.aws_iam_policy_document.write_mysql_root_password` grants `kms:Encrypt` and `kms:GenerateDataKey` on `*` under a condition:

```hcl
condition {
  test     = "StringEquals"
  variable = "kms:ViaService"
  values   = ["ssm.${local.tokyo_region}.amazonaws.com"]
}
```

It names one region while the statement above it writes to two, `local.parameter_store_regions` being `[local.tokyo_region, local.seoul_region]`. That reads like a bug, and it is not: the write succeeds in Seoul anyway.

Measured on 2026-09-27:

```
ap-northeast-1  (no /mysql/servers parameter at all)
ap-northeast-2  /mysql/servers/5/root/password  SecureString  alias/aws/ssm  09:39 KST
```

The only such parameter that exists is in Seoul, written today by the `database` role, which is the role this policy is attached to. It works because `alias/aws/ssm` is an AWS managed key: its key policy grants use through the service, so the caller needs no `kms:Encrypt` of its own. The condition is therefore not gating the write it appears to gate.

So the statement is either dead or it is insurance for a customer-managed key that is not in use. Both are worth resolving rather than leaving a reader to work this out again:

- If it is dead, remove it, and the `parameter_store_regions` asymmetry goes with it.
- If it is kept as insurance against a future customer-managed key, it should list both regions, and say in a word why it is there.

This is a clarity question with no reader-visible effect, which is why it is not a fix in #920. Related: #872, the MediaWiki database password sitting in Parameter Store unencrypted, which is about a different parameter.

issues.body:
`memcached` carries an `autoheal` label and no health check, so the label has never done anything (#582). Either it gets a check or it loses the label.

Both replace the container. **What that costs, checked in the running image rather than assumed:**

`CookieSessionProvider::cookieDataToExport` writes the `Token` cookie only for a session that asked to be remembered:

```php
'Token' => $remember ? (string)$user->getToken() : false,
```

With that cookie, `provideSessionInfo` validates it against `user_token` in the database and rebuilds the session from nothing. Without it, `userInfo` stays unverified and only the session store can confirm the user, so an emptied store means anonymous.

| | on a memcached replacement |
|---|---|
| logged in with "keep me logged in" | nothing; the 180-day `Token` cookie rebuilds the session |
| logged in without it | **logged out** |
| anonymous sessions, edit and CSRF tokens in flight | lost |

So it is some users rather than everyone, and it is not free. Defaults, none overridden in LocalSettings.php: `ObjectCacheSessionExpiry` `60 * 60`, `CookieExpiration` `30 * 86400`, `ExtendedLoginCookieExpiration` `180 * 86400`.

**This no longer has to wait for a bump to ride along with.** The container was replaced on 2026-09-25 by #740, which gave memcached `-m 192` in a 248 MiB container and moved it off the journald log driver; it had been running on its own 64 MiB default. So the second row of that table has already been paid once today, and whatever is decided here can be applied without paying it again only if it lands before the next replacement, not because replacements have become free.

Timing a future one rather than taking it freely is the rule until femiwiki/femiwiki#466 puts sessions on `CACHE_DB`, which is what makes a memcached replacement cost nothing and is also what femiwiki/femiwiki#465 names as removing the expected logout at the Seoul cutover.

agent_prs.title: aws(CloudTrail): keep management events for a year

issues.body:
`aws cloudtrail describe-trails --include-shadow-trails` returns an empty list in `ap-northeast-2`, `ap-northeast-1` and `us-east-1` (2026-10-10), so there is no trail, single- or multi-region. Event history keeps 90 days of management events and nothing more (CIS AWS Foundations 3.1).

## Why it matters

- A leaked key or other change nobody made on purpose is often noticed late. Past 90 days there is no record of what was changed or when.
- Option 3 of femiwiki/femiwiki#514 (EventBridge on `AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress` to Discord) needs a trail: EventBridge only receives `AWS API Call via CloudTrail` events while a trail is logging ([docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-service-event-cloudtrail.html)).

It would not have explained femiwiki/femiwiki#555: that outage was the application hanging, which management events do not record.

## Fix

One multi-region `aws_cloudtrail`, management events only, delivering to a new S3 bucket with a one-year expiry. The first copy of management events is free, so the cost is S3. Measured 2026-10-15 from Event history: about 16k log files a month ($0.07), log file validation digests ($0.06), under 1 GB stored ($0.02), so about $0.2 a month, $0.8 at most. SSE-S3 rather than KMS; no Insights, data events, CloudWatch Logs or Lake.

agent_prs.title: ci(tofu): refuse to apply a pull request behind main

issues.body:
On 2026-10-10 the grafana apply of #1289 (a `tofu.yml`-only pull request) removed the `Most requests are failing` rule that #1286 had applied 20 minutes earlier. The rule then missed the generation 98 outage at 17:48-17:59Z (#1281). This is infra CI, so it is for docker-deployer.

## What happened (UTC)

- 17:08:46 run [38070537160](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/actions/runs/38070537160) starts for #1289 on merge commit `1fc9379`, whose base `ead35bd` is before #1286.
- 17:08-17:10 #1286 applies; 17:11:07 it merges (`f973143`).
- 17:10:23 #1289's `grafana plan` runs against the state #1286 just wrote, with code that lacks the rule, so the plan renames the rule's slot back to `One network is being refused far more than the rest` and drops one rule. Not empty, so `pending` lists grafana.
- 17:30:23 the grafana apply is approved. It checks out the same `pull/1289/merge` (`1fc9379`), dflook's re-plan matches the stale plan, and [the log](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/actions/runs/38070537160) shows `~ name = "Most requests are failing" -> "One network is being refused far more than the rest"`, `1 to change`. Applied 17:31:20.

`mergeable.sh` passed because main is not strict, and the plan-match check passed because both plans came from the same stale commit. Nothing compares the commit being applied with main's tip.

## Proposal

- In the apply job, before the apply: fail unless main's current tip is an ancestor of the checked-out commit, saying "main has moved since this plan; update the branch". The `workflow_dispatch` path applies a branch on purpose (rollbacks) and can skip it.
- Optionally, in `pending`: do not offer an apply for a workspace whose directory the pull request does not touch. A non-empty plan there is drift or a stale base, never something the pull request means to apply. #1289 would then have asked for no grafana approval at all.

#1090 and #606 cover keeping branches fresh; this is the check that holds when they lag.

agent_prs.title: feat(github): write infra's Actions secrets from 1Password

issues.body:
Every Actions secret in infra is set by hand today, and GitHub cannot read a secret back, so renaming or rotating one (#982) means finding the value wherever it was made. Keep the values in 1Password and let the `github` root write them as secrets, so 1Password is the one source and a rename or rotation is a pull request.

### Shape

The `github` root reads each item with the [`1Password/onepassword`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/1Password/onepassword/latest) provider (v3.3.1: an `onepassword_item` resource, data source and ephemeral resource) and writes it with `github_actions_secret`:

```hcl
data "onepassword_item" "aws_loki_password" {
  vault = "…"
  title = "AWS_LOKI_PASSWORD"
}

resource "github_actions_secret" "aws_loki_password" {
  repository  = "infra"
  secret_name = "AWS_LOKI_PASSWORD"
  value       = data.onepassword_item.aws_loki_password.password
}
```

No other root has to output anything; the `github` root reads 1Password directly.

### Before it can start

- **The `github` state gets encrypted.** `github_actions_secret` has no write-only argument, and its documentation says `value` lands in the state. The `github` root has no `encryption` block today, because femiwiki/femiwiki#607 chose it as the root whose state holds nothing sensitive. Add one the way femiwiki/infra#960 does for `aws` (`pbkdf2`, with a one-off `unencrypted` fallback), before the first secret is managed.
- **A 1Password service account, read-only on one infra vault.** The pull request plan reads the vault too, so anyone who can push a branch can read what the token can. That is the same exposure the repository secrets have today (the rule in #982), so the token must not reach any other vault. Service accounts cannot be given the built-in Personal or Private vault, and their vault access cannot be changed after creation.
- **The plan allows it, with a low ceiling.** The [rate limits page](https://www.1password.dev/service-accounts/rate-limits/) lists limits for the indi

agent_prs.title: docker(fastcgi): switch MediaWiki's caches to the pecl memcached client

issues.body:
Switch MediaWiki's main, parser and message caches to the C memcached client by setting three variables on the fastcgi container ([`docker/container.tf`](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/blob/e27425c604f706ef57cc99d4303ad6e88d0043ef/docker/container.tf#L149), next to `WG_MEMCACHED_SERVERS`):

```hcl
FW_MAIN_CACHE    = "memcached-pecl"
FW_PARSER_CACHE  = "memcached-pecl"
FW_MESSAGE_CACHE = "memcached-pecl"
```

For docker-deployer. Needed by femiwiki/docker-mediawiki#1303, which adds the extension and the value. Evidence and expected effect are in the pecl item of #1073.

## Before the apply
The image named in `docker/container.tf` must contain the extension. Otherwise the value throws, the new container never gets healthy and the old one keeps serving. The chain:
- [ ] femiwiki/docker-mediawiki#1303 merged (operator's review). It publishes php-fpm 1.7.0.
- [ ] Bump PR: mediawiki to php-fpm 1.7.0, merged and released as a new mediawiki version.
- [ ] Bump PR: femiwiki to that mediawiki version, merged. The femiwiki build then opens the infra image bump.
- [ ] The infra image bump applied. Check it with `docker exec fastcgi-<n> php -r 'echo phpversion("memcached");'`, which should print `3.4.0`.

The variables can go in the same apply as that image bump, so it takes one swap instead of two. Each swap currently gives readers about 30 s of 502s (#1121).

## What to expect
- The pecl client keeps every key under the prefix `pecl/`, so it starts from a cold cache: parser cache, message cache and WAN cache. issues.body:
Both Seoul hosts are t4g.small in unlimited mode, so CPU above the 20% baseline never throttles. It costs surplus credits at $0.04 per vCPU-hour (1 credit = 1 vCPU-minute) once the balance is 0. Nothing alerts on it. Today's flood and the 2026-09-29 to 09-30 run went unnoticed until someone looked. #1073 tracks the cost itself.

## What exists

- No CloudWatch alarm on CPU or credits (5 alarms in total, all in us-east-1: SES, Route53 pages, CloudFront).
- No Grafana rule on node CPU, only the `site` dashboard panel.

## Measurements (2026-09-26 to 2026-10-03)

- CloudWatch, docker (`i-0201969cfe38c574c`): `CPUCreditBalance` 0 and `CPUSurplusCreditBalance` pinned at 576 for at least the last 12 hours; `CPUSurplusCreditsCharged` 1,235 credits over the week, about $0.82. database-5: balance full at 576, nothing charged, CPU 2–12%.
- Node CPU, 1-hour average on `femiwiki-seoul`: 25–33% on normal days, single hours up to 38.7%. 39–83% for about 21 hours on 2026-09-29/30, and 41–85% in the 2026-10-02 outage.
- Hours where the 1-hour average stayed above 35% for the whole hour fall only in those two episodes. On normal days the highest was 34.1%.
- Credits charged per hour ≈ (CPU% − 20) × 1.2 on 2 vCPUs. At 08:00Z on 2026-10-03 this gave 23.1 for 39.2% CPU, against 23.5 that CloudWatch charged for that hour.

## Plan

A Grafana rule `CPU surplus credits are being charged` on node_exporter CPU: fires when a host's 1-hour average stays above 35% for an hour. That is about 18 credits an hour, against the usual 10. It says the CPU, credits per hour and dollars per day. Impact operators, so it opens a GitHub issue.

It costs nothing extra: node_exporter is already scraped and the rule runs in Grafana. A CloudWatch alarm on `CPUSurplusCreditsCharged` would also be free (5 of the 10 free alarms are used), but the hosts are in Seoul and the topic in us-east-1, so it would need a second SNS topic and subscription, and it would post to Discord, not GitHub.

## Outcome

#1107 applied

## Plan

A Grafana rule `Uncaught exceptions` in `grafana/rules-http.tf` counts fastcgi log lines with `"caught_by":"entrypoint"` (an exception that reached the visitor as an error page) or `"channel":"fatal"`, over the last hour, and fires above 5. It names the most frequent exception class and links Explore, where each line carries the request id and URL.

Not counted: the `error` channel (PHP deprecations and warnings, about 17,000 an hour since 1.46), the `PageViewInfo` channel (about 7,600 a week), `caught_by: other` (caught and handled), and `exception-json` (no `caught_by`).

issues.body:
Every CloudWatch alarm in `aws/` sends to one of two SNS topics, and every one of them reaches a person only because a subscription was made in the console years ago. There is no `aws_sns_topic_subscription` anywhere in `aws/`.

What depends on it: the Route 53 health check alarms, one per check, https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/blob/eb7a488b3a4a2c06aece36086c901c6603ccfec2/aws/cloudwatch.tf#L56-L73, the SES bounce and complaint alarms, and `Backup missing`. The delivery itself is the `DiscordNoti` lambda in femiwiki/lambda, which posts with the role mention and a 🟢 line on recovery: https://github.com/femiwiki/lambda/blob/601aa454e45367068350685cea16e336ca9eebaf/sns-discord/lambda_function.py#L130

The function is not in Terraform either. `aws/` holds its log groups in both regions, its execution role and policy, and the role femiwiki/lambda's Actions assume to deploy it, but not the function and not its subscription. That repository's workflow zips and updates the function; it does not create a subscription.

So if the subscription is removed, or the lambda is deleted, every alarm still resolves and fires and nothing arrives, and no plan in this repository says a word. The outage path is the one that matters most: it is one half of the deliberate doubling of monitoring, the other half being `Site down` in grafana, and the half that does not depend on Grafana's free plan.

The comment that explains the gap is out of date: https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/blob/eb7a488b3a4a2c06aece36086c901c6603ccfec2/aws/sns.tf#L1-L5 With the provider pinned at `~> 6.7`, `email` is a valid protocol, "partially supported": the subscription can be created, only the confirmation happens out of band, `pending_confirmation` reports whether it was confirmed, and an unconfirmed one cannot be deleted by Terraform. A `lambda` subscription has none of those caveats and is ordinary.

issues.body:
Files read off disk by [the file server](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/blob/dcd4d42e27ee8c3e620089d9425b77f9f7faf234/serving/Caddyfile) go out with `Content-Type`, `Etag`, `Last-Modified`, `Accept-Ranges`, `Server` and `Vary`, and no `Cache-Control`. A browser with no freshness to go on asks again next time and gets a 304, so the skin's icons cost a round trip per icon per page. Measured on 2026-09-29 from the response headers in the access log; `load.php` is not affected, it already sends `public, max-age=300, s-maxage=300`.

Most of these URLs carry a version hash, such as `icon-changes.svg?c01d1`, which is exactly the case `immutable` exists for.

Two things to settle first.

- **The same file is requested with and without its hash.** `logo-transparent-white.svg` came in both ways in the same window. A long `max-age` on the bare path would pin a stale logo until the browser's cache turned over, so the header has to depend on the query being there, not on the path.
- **Which trees.** The hits are under `/fw-resources`, `/resources` and `/skins`. Uploaded media under `/images` is a separate question: those paths carry no hash and a file can be overwritten in place.

Reader-facing either way, so it wants checking on a real page load rather than only in `caddy adapt`.

issues.body:
[`Logs are arriving faster than the plan allows`](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/blob/7fb8e94666c88e5c278a75e92f79832a0a393ea4/grafana/rules-threshold.tf#L148-L158) projects a month from a six-hour average and fires above **100 GB**. The free plan includes **50 GB**. So a steady pace anywhere between the two exhausts the plan with no alert at all: at 60 GB a month it runs out around day 25 and ingestion is dropped for the rest of the month, which is the silence-then-false-alarms state the rule exists to prevent. #725 introduced the 100 and did not say why.

It also reads only the pace, never the month so far. What decides whether this month exceeds is `grafanacloud_logs_instance_usage`, the accumulated GB, plus the days left. A quiet first half of the month buys real headroom that the pace alone cannot see, and a busy first half removes headroom the pace alone cannot see either.

Two things to settle:

- The number. The allowance itself is the obvious threshold, but a rule that fires on any pace over 50 GB is noisy when the month so far is nearly empty. A rule on what the month will land at, from usage so far and the current pace, fires when it actually matters.
- The summary hard-codes `로그의 92%는 Caddy 접근 로그입니다`. After #967 and #973 that share is wrong, and a fixed number in an alert body is the kind nobody revisits.

Measured 2026-09-30, after both cuts: 14 KB/s, about 37 GB a month, with 10.9 GB used in September. So there is headroom today and this is not urgent; it is the guard that was missing when the 2026-09-29 surge arrived.

issues.body:
#863 merged unapplied on 2026-09-26 23:24:30Z because a *skipped* `tofu gate` satisfied the required check.

1. The `tofu apply` review started a `pull_request_review` run of tofu.yaml. Its [`gate` job](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/blob/81c7ea425932e32b48b5eded9efe741e1ea853ce/.github/workflows/tofu.yaml#L145-L148) has `if: ... github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, so it was skipped, but it still reported a check run named `tofu gate`, with conclusion skipped.
2. The apply itself failed (the plan had drifted by an `etag`), so the pull_request run's `tofu gate` stayed failed and auto-merge waited.
3. Re-running that failed pull_request run reset its `tofu gate`. The skipped one from step 1 was then the latest `tofu gate` on the head, and GitHub counts skipped as passing, so auto-merge merged at once.

The plan jobs do not have this hole: a skipped matrix job reports its name unexpanded (`${{ matrix.workspace }} plan is empty`), which matches no required context. `tofu gate` is a literal, so any run of tofu.yaml that skips it reports the required name.

Proposed fix: give the gate a name only a pull_request run can carry, so a comment-, review- or dispatch-triggered run never reports `tofu gate`:

```yaml
  gate:
    name: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'tofu gate' || 'tofu gate (not for this event)' }}
```

Whether GitHub evaluates that expression for a skipped job or leaves it raw, the reported name is not `tofu gate`, so the required check can only be met by a pull_request run that ran the gate. A test: on a branch, skip the gate from a review-triggered run and confirm the PR's `tofu gate` stays failed and auto-merge stays blocked.

`uri @special_title query -oldid` and the same for `diff`, on `/index.php*` when the query's `title` is in the special namespace. Generation 16 because `FW_CADDYFILE` is create-only.

Run against the real rules, with the caddy the host runs:

```
?title=특수%3A로그인&oldid=123&diff=4   ->  title=%ED%8A%B9%EC%88%98%3A...
?title=Special%3AUserLogin&oldid=9      ->  title=Special%3AUserLogin
?title=페미위키&oldid=77                ->  title=%ED%8E%98...&oldid=77
```

An ordinary article keeps its `oldid`; that is the thing not to break.

It has to happen before `rate_limit` to be worth anything, and it does. `uri` compiles to a `rewrite` handler, and the adapted config orders them:

```
main    3 rewrite handlers
this    5, the two new ones {'query': {'delete': ['oldid']}} and the same for diff
order   vars, static_response x5, rewrite x4, rate_limit
```

`Special:RevisionDelete` and `Special:EditTags` do take revision ids, but as `ids[]`, not `oldid` or `diff`; `Special:Diff` and `Special:PermanentLink` carry theirs in the title. Nothing that reads these loses them.

**This stops refusing them, which is the half not to skip over.** Today those 408 match `expensive_requests`, so 364 of them draw a 429. Stripped, they match nothing, so they are neither counted nor refused: they render the special page. Renders go from about 19 an hour to about 204.

That is worth paying, because of what the bucket costs:

```
FW_EXPENSIVE_EVENTS = 60 per 10 minutes, shared by the whole site  =  360/hour
requests this removes from it                                      =  204/hour
```

Requests that cannot mean anything were taking more than half the budget real old-revision viewing draws on. The 185 extra renders an hour are a login page at 0.06/s against 4.6/s of traffic.

Verify after apply: no `oldid`/`diff` request with a special title reaches a 429, `oldid` on an article is untouched, and the `expensive` zone's refusals fall.

agent_prs.title: fix(ci): give the daemon wait a timeout, and close the session it opened

issues.body:
`.github/actions/docker-daemon` waits for the forwarded port like this:

```bash
for _ in $(seq 30); do
  curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:2376/_ping > /dev/null && exit 0
  sleep 1
done
echo "::error::the port forward did not come up"; cat /tmp/ssm-session.log; exit 1
```

The loop reads as a 30 second budget and is not one. `curl` carries no `--max-time`, so when the tunnel accepts the connection but nothing answers, the first iteration blocks for ever and the loop never reaches its second. The step cannot report the failure it was written to report.

Seen on 2026-09-27 in [run 36302514535](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/actions/runs/36302514535), the apply for femiwiki/infra#900: `docker-seoul apply` sat in `Run ./.github/actions/docker-daemon` for over sixteen minutes and was ended by the job's own `timeout-minutes: 20`, not by the loop. Nothing was applied, so production was untouched throughout.

The tunnel was not broken at the far end, which is what makes this a timeout bug rather than a connectivity one. Measured while the job hung: the daemon on `docker-seoul` was listening on `127.0.0.1:2376`, answered `/_ping` locally with `OK`, load average 0.28, and a second SSM port forward opened from a laptop to the same instance answered `/_ping` with `OK` as well. Only the runner's own session was dead.

`--max-time 3` on that `curl` makes the loop mean what it says, and turns sixteen minutes of a stuck job into a 30 second failure with `/tmp/ssm-session.log` in the output, which is the diagnosis this step was meant to produce.

The same shape is in the step below it, `curl -sf "http://$gateway:2376/_ping"` after `socat`, with no timeout and no loop.

`lint.yaml` runs tflint, shellcheck, rumdl, yamllint, parallel-lint and taplo. Nothing reads `serving/Caddyfile`, so a syntax error in it reaches production.

What makes that worse than a bad `.tf` file: `FW_CADDYFILE = file("../serving/Caddyfile")` is env on the **`http`** container, and only `fastcgi` carries `wait = true`. So the plan succeeds, `create_before_destroy` starts the new `http`, caddy refuses the config and exits, and the old generation is destroyed anyway. Caddy is the only thing listening on 443.

A check is cheap, because the image already carries the binary with all three plugins:

docker run --rm -v ./serving/Caddyfile:/tmp/Caddyfile:ro <femiwiki image> \
  caddy adapt --adapter caddyfile --config /tmp/Caddyfile
```

`caddy validate` is not usable: it goes on to provision the s3 storage module and fails on the endpoint it has no credentials for. `adapt` stops after producing the JSON, which is the part that catches syntax and unknown directives.

The image tag to run it against is the one in `docker-seoul/container.tf`, so the check tests the Caddyfile against the caddy that will actually read it, including a plugin bump changing a directive.

Found while preparing #902, which edits this file. I adapted both versions by hand and diffed the JSON to see the change was what I meant; that should not be a manual step.

The cap itself is not the problem: raising it would spend php-fpm workers on a revision crawl. What is wrong is that one bucket holds both the thing a reader clicks once and the thing a crawler enumerates without end.

**Measured on the last hour, 2026-09-27 08:00-09:00 UTC.**

Of 6,400 responses with status 429, 5,047 (79%) carry `oldid=`. Old revisions are also being served: 2,617 of them came back 200 in the same hour, so the demand is about 7,700 an hour and a third of it gets through.

The busiest was 137 and the top fifteen together were about half the total, so this is a crawl spread thin across many networks rather than one scraper. issues.body:
`fastcgi`'s healthcheck runs `fcgi-probe.php`, which asks php-fpm for `/var/www/livez` over `FCGI_URL` and never touches the database. So a generation whose `WG_DB_SERVER` points somewhere broken reports healthy, `create_before_destroy` drains the generation that worked, and the site loses its database with every check green.

This was named in the body of femiwiki/infra#833 as worth a ticket of its own and never filed. It matters again now: bringing ProxySQL to the Seoul app box puts a new hop in that path, and the only thing protecting the change is a hand-run pre-check, exactly as it was in Tokyo.

Two ways out, neither obviously right:

- The probe reads something that requires the database, for example a `SELECT 1` through MediaWiki's own load balancer. That makes the healthcheck fail when the database is down, which is honest but also means a database outage drains every container rather than serving errors from a live one.
- The probe stays as it is and the swap gains a separate gate that checks the new generation's database path before the old one is allowed to drain.

The second keeps a database outage from turning into an empty host, so it is probably the one, but it needs somewhere to live in `tofu.yaml` rather than in the container definition.

issues.body:
The `expensive` zone counts search, diffs, old revisions and history for everyone not logged in against one site-wide bucket (#1109, temporary by design). When crawlers spend it, the next logged-out reader who presses search is refused.

## Outcome

Two layers, applied in femiwiki/infra#714: a per `/24` bucket that keeps one client from spending everybody's, and the site-wide bucket raised back above ordinary demand as the backstop. The variables have since moved to `FW_` names (#737).

- `CADDY_EXPENSIVE_IP_EVENTS` (per `/24`): 15 per 10 minutes, which is 90 an hour. That is three and a half times the p95 `/24` in the worst hour measured, and a fifth of the smallest crawler in the head. A reader making a handful of searches is nowhere near it. The previous value, 100 per 10 minutes (600 an hour), sat 30% above the busiest `/24` in that hour, so it had never fired and could not.
- `CADDY_EXPENSIVE_EVENTS` (site-wide): back to 3000 per 10 minutes, above the 2,254 per 10 minutes measured as ordinary demand. It had gone 1500 to 3000 to 2000 to 1600 over two days, and each of those refused whoever asked next once crawlers had spent the bucket.

Not covered: a crawler that spreads thinly enough to stay under 90 an hour per `/24` while using many `/24`s. 143 `/24`s were above 5 an hour, so that shape exists; the site-wide bucket is the backstop for it, which is why it was raised rather than removed.

## The problem, measured

Over the nine hours to 2026-09-24 03:00 UTC, 2,254 expensive requests per ten minutes on average and 5,535 at the peak, against a bucket of 1500. In the hour to 02:55 UTC that meant 2,694 responses of 429, 9% of all responses, spread over 2,307 distinct addresses, none carrying a `femiwikiUserID` cookie. The peaks are also what leaves php-fpm without workers (#624).

## Per `/24` distribution

The incident hour, 21:00 to 22:00 UTC on 2026-09-24 (the 06:02 KST incident): 7,288 expensive requests (anonymous `search`, `diff` or `oldid` on `/index.php`)

Refs femiwiki/femiwiki#554.

infra#801 turned on `$wgReadOnly`. Its own apply then posted its note to 페미위키:업데이트, and the wiki refused with `https://femiwiki.com/api.php: The wiki is currently in read-only mode.` ([run 36217880590](https://github.com/femiwiki/infra/actions/runs/36217880590), job `docker apply`). I added it by hand (rev 345333).

`continue-on-error` is right on its own, because a failed note must not fail an apply that has already changed production. What is missing is any signal. Two cheap options, not mutually exclusive:

- Surface it. Add a `::warning::` or a line in the Discord message when the post step's outcome is failure, so the apply reads "Applied, note not posted".
- Catch up. On the next successful post, also post the merged docker PRs since the last one whose link is not on the page yet. #788 made the link the dedupe key, so this would not double-post. In this case infra#802, which lifted read-only, would have carried #801's note with it.

A read-only apply will always hit the first case, since it closes the wiki before the post runs.

agent_prs.body:
The REST MCP server decoded every response with `response.text`, which corrupts binary bodies such as GitHub workflow logs and artifacts (zip). It also followed redirects blindly, so the request went on to a different host (a signed storage URL). Per the issue discussion, redirects are now surfaced instead of followed.

All changes are in `api-rest-mcp.py`. A single `response` event hook on `raw_client` covers both the raw `HTTP_*` tools and the OpenAPI-generated tools.

- **Redirects**
  - `follow_redirects` is now `False`.
  - A 3xx response with a `Location` header and an empty body gets the body `Redirect to: <url>`.
  - Generated tools raise on non-2xx, so for them this arrives as `HTTP error 302: Found - Redirect to: <url>`.
  - Because the redirect target is never requested, `DynamicAuth` can't send the token to another host.
- **Binary bodies**
  - A response is treated as text if its content type is `text/*`, JSON, XML, YAML, form-encoded, GraphQL, or has a `+json`/`+xml` suffix. Anything else, or a missing content type, is treated accordingly.
  - A missing content type is treated as text.
  - Binary bodies are returned as base64 text.
  - The headers `X-Original-Content-Type` and `X-Content-Encoding: base64` are added.
  - `Content-Type` is rewritten to `text/plain`.
- **Size cap**
  - Responses are streamed and capped at 10 MiB (`API_MCP_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`).
  - A binary response over the cap raises an error, because a partial binary payload is unusable.
  - A text response over the cap is truncated with a marker.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_binary_responses.py` covers the redirect `Location`, an intact binary round-trip, and the size cap.

```python
# GET /repos/o/r/actions/runs/1/logs  ->  302 Location: https://storage.example/logs.zip
# body: "Redirect to: https://storage.example/logs.zip"
# GET <zip endpoint>  ->  body is base64 of the zip,
#                         headers["X-Original-Content-Type"] == "application/zip"
```

Not addressed:
- **OpenAPI
agent_prs.title: REST: return binary responses intact and surface redirects instead of following them

issues.body:
## Summary

Extend the REST MCP server (`api-rest-mcp.py`) so it can handle binary response bodies, not just text/JSON. Typical example: GitHub Actions workflow run logs and artifacts. The API answers with a `302` redirect to a signed storage URL, which then streams a `application/zip` payload.

This issue is to **evaluate whether this works today** and then **make the changes needed so that it does**.

## Current behavior (from reading the code)

- `raw_client` is created with `follow_redirects = True`, so redirects are followed transparently.
- The raw tools (`HTTP_GET` etc.) return `_response_result()`, which puts `response.text` into `body`. For a zip this decodes binary data as text, which corrupts it and is not usable by an MCP client.
- Tools generated via `FastMCP.from_openapi` go through the OpenAPI tool response handling. I have not verified how FastMCP handles non-JSON / binary responses there. Needs checking.
- The response is fully buffered in memory. Large artifacts and logs may be a problem.

## Questions to evaluate

1. **Does it work at all today?** Try e.g. `actions/downloadArtifact`, `actions/downloadWorkflowRunLogs`, `actions/downloadJobLogsForWorkflowRun` against the GitHub REST API, through both the generated tools and the raw `HTTP_GET` tool. What does the client actually receive?
2. **Is blind redirect following problematic?**
   - The OpenAPI schema may not represent it correctly. My assumption (to be verified against the real spec) is that these operations declare a `302` response with a `Location` header and no content, rather than a `200` with a binary body. If so, the generated tool's output schema does not describe what the client actually gets after the redirect is followed (a zip).
   - `DynamicAuth` only adds `Authorization` for the configured base host, which is good, because the redirect target is a different host (signed URL) and must not receive the token. Confirm this holds across the redirect hop, including for scheme and port
issues.title: REST: support binary response data (e.g. GitHub workflow logs / artifacts that redirect and stream a zip)

issues.body:
## Goal

Remove the `packageRules` entry in `.github/renovate.json` that restricts the `python` image in `Dockerfile.graphql` to `~3.12`, so Renovate can propose newer Python versions for the GraphQL image like it does for `Dockerfile.rest`.

## Background

The pin was added in #23 after Renovate bumped the GraphQL image to Python 3.14 (#14). It exists because `graphql-mcp` does not support newer Python:

- The original requirement in #1 said `graphql_mcp` "needs python 3.12 exactly, and nothing newer".
- Upstream `graphql-mcp` 2.3.1 declares `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.13"`, and so do its dependencies `graphql-api` and `graphql-http`. On Python 3.13, `pip install graphql-mcp==2.3.1` is refused.
- No documented reason for the upstream cap was found. I asked upstream: https://github.com/parob/graphql-mcp/issues/19

## Blocked on

Do not merge until upstream `graphql-mcp` (and `graphql-api` / `graphql-http`) lift the `<3.13` cap and a newer release is picked up in `requirements.graphql.txt`. Otherwise Renovate would propose a Python bump that cannot install.

## Acceptance

- The `packageRules` block for `Dockerfile.graphql` / `python` is removed from `.github/renovate.json`.
- The GraphQL image builds and passes CI on the newer Python version Renovate proposes.

  - name: youtube

    base_url: https://youtube.googleapis.com/

No assumption is made here about how credentials should be wired up; that's left to whatever mechanism the other API entries use.
- `name: youtube` is a guess at the desired identifier — happy to rename if there's a different naming convention intended.

agent_prs.body:
Every tool call over stdio transport was timing out, with the actual JSON-RPC responses only visible in `docker logs` instead of reaching the client.

**Root cause**

The `graphql-mcp` dependency (used by `api-graphql-mcp.py`) logs GraphQL resolver/query errors via bare `print()`, which writes to stdout. In `API_MCP_MODE=stdio`, stdout *is* the MCP JSON-RPC transport — any partial GraphQL error (common with real-world APIs like GitHub's) injects plain text into the protocol stream, corrupting it and causing the client to hang until timeout.

**Fix**

- Extended the existing `_patch_graphql_mcp()` monkeypatch in `api-graphql-mcp.py` to redirect `graphql_mcp.server`'s module-level `print` to `sys.stderr`, keeping stdout reserved exclusively for protocol messages:

```python
gs.print = functools.partial(print, file=sys.stderr)
```

**Tests**

- Added `tests/test_graphql_stdio_safety.py`: builds a local schema with a failing resolver, invokes the tool, and asserts stdout stays empty. Confirmed it fails without the patch (leaks the `GraphQL errors for ...` text to stdout) and passes with it.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #177

issues.body:
## Summary

`MicrosoftPowerBIMgmt.Profile` is declared as a required module, but no cmdlet in `src/` uses it. We should remove the dependency.

## Findings

- No calls to any `*-PowerBI*` cmdlet (`Connect-PowerBIServiceAccount`, `Get-PowerBIAccessToken`, `Invoke-PowerBIRestMethod`, `Resolve-PowerBIError`, etc.) anywhere in the repo.
- Authentication relies entirely on **Az.Accounts** (`Connect-AzAccount` / `Get-AzAccessToken` in `Connect-FabricAccount`).
- Cmdlets that hit the Power BI REST API (`Get-FabricAPIClusterURI`, `Get-FabricCapacityRefreshables`, `Get-FabricCapacityWorkload`, `Get-FabricWorkspaceUser`, `Get-FabricUsageMetricsQuery`, `Get-FabricDataset`, `Get-FabricDatasetRefreshHistory`, `Invoke-FabricDatasetRefresh`) do so via `Invoke-FabricRestMethod -PowerBIApi`, which just switches the base URL (`FabricTools.PowerBiApi.BaseUrl`) and does not use the module.
- No unit tests mock or depend on MicrosoftPowerBIMgmt.

## Implications

**Possible breaking change for users:** importing FabricTools currently also loads `MicrosoftPowerBIMgmt.Profile`, so commands like `Connect-PowerBIServiceAccount` become available as a side effect. Scripts relying on that will need an explicit `Import-Module MicrosoftPowerBIMgmt.Profile`. `Install-Module FabricTools` will no longer install it either (existing installs are unaffected).

**Benefits:**
- Faster install/import and lighter CI dependency resolution (`RequiredModules.psd1` pulls the full `MicrosoftPowerBIMgmt` package).
- Fewer assembly conflicts: `MicrosoftPowerBIMgmt.Profile` ships its own MSAL / Newtonsoft.Json versions, which are known to clash with Az.Accounts depending on load order.
- Drops a dependency on a module that sees little maintenance (pinned `1.2.1111`).

- [x] Remove `MicrosoftPowerBIMgmt.Profile` from `RequiredModules` in `src/FabricTools.psd1`
- [x] Remove `MicrosoftPowerBIMgmt` from `RequiredModules.psd1`

issues.body:
## Background

FabricTools currently contains a large and growing number of cmdlets (~300), developed over time by multiple contributors. These cmdlets vary significantly in terms of quality, testing coverage, stability, and production readiness.

At the moment, there is no explicit way to communicate:
- how mature a given cmdlet is,
- what guarantees (if any) it provides,
- or what is required to improve its quality level.

This makes it harder for:
- users to know which cmdlets are safe to use in production,
- contributors to understand expectations,
- maintainers to prioritize improvements.

---

## Proposal

Introduce a **formal Cmdlet Maturity Model** that categorizes each cmdlet into a clearly defined maturity level, based on objective and verifiable criteria.

The proposed maturity levels are:

| Level | Name |
|------:|------|
| 0 | Experimental |
| 1 | Prototype |
| 2 | Standardized |
| 3 | Unit Tested |
| 4 | Integration Tested |
| 5 | Production Ready |

Each level defines specific characteristics such as:
- adherence to PowerShell and FabricTools coding standards,
- presence and quality of comment-based help,
- parameter validation and error handling,
- unit and integration test coverage,
- CI enforcement,
- stability and backward compatibility guarantees.

---

## Goals

- Provide **clear expectations** for cmdlet quality and stability
- Make cmdlet maturity **transparent to users**
- Give contributors a **clear path for improving cmdlets**
- Improve overall consistency and maintainability of the module
- Enable future CI checks and quality gates

---

## Scope (Initial)

- Define and document the maturity model in the repository
- Agree on objective criteria for each maturity level
- Decide how maturity is represented (e.g. metadata, comments, docs)
- Mark existing cmdlets with an initial maturity level (best-effort)

---

## Out of Scope (for this issue)

- Refactoring all existing cmdlets to higher maturity levels
- Enforcing maturity levels via CI (

## Pull Request (PR) description

Fixes #228. `Invoke-FabricRestMethod` looped forever on paginated list responses. It built the next-page URL with the continuation token but sent the request to the original `$Uri`, so it fetched page 1 again, got the same token back, and repeated. Every list cmdlet whose results span more than one page was affected. Results that fit on one page were not, which is why this went unnoticed.

A second defect sat in the same lines: the token was always appended with `?`, so a URI that already has a query string (e.g. `items?type=Lakehouse`, `tables?maxResults=1`) would have become invalid once the first defect was fixed.

**Fix** (`src/Public/Invoke-FabricRestMethod.ps1`, 4 lines)
- Send the request to the next-page URL (`$apiEndpointUrl`) instead of `$Uri`.
- Append the token with `&` when the `Uri` already contains `?`.

No caller in the module adds a continuation token to the URI itself, so nothing ends up with the token twice. Retries after throttling (HTTP 429) still request the same page, because the token only changes when a page is successfully read.

### Problem description

`Invoke-FabricRestMethod` never sends the continuation token. When a list response has more than one page, it requests the first page again, gets the same `continuationToken` back, and loops forever, outputting page 1's items again on every pass. Every list cmdlet is affected once the results span more than one page. Results that fit on one page are unaffected, which is probably why this hasn't been noticed.

The loop builds the next-page URL but sends the request to the original `$Uri` (`src/Public/Invoke-FabricRestMethod.ps1`):

```powershell
$apiEndpointUrl = $Uri
if ($null -ne $continuationToken) {
    $encodedToken = [System.Web.HttpUtility]::UrlEncode($continuationToken)
    $apiEndpointUrl = "{0}?continuationToken={1}" -f $apiEndpointUrl, $encodedToken
}
...
$request = @{
    Headers = $requestHeaders
    Uri = $Uri              # <-- should be $apiEndpointUrl
```

A second defect sits in the same lines. The token is always appended with `?`, so a URI that already has a query string becomes invalid, e.g. `items?type=Lakehouse?continuationToken=...`. Affected callers include `Get-FabricItem -type`, `Get-FabricCapacityRefreshables` (`?$top=`) and any caller passing `maxResults`.

### Reproduction (mocked)

`Get-FabricConnection` with `Invoke-RestMethod` mocked to return 2 items plus `continuationToken = 'page2'` for the first request, and 1 item with no token when `continuationToken=` is in the URI:

  https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/connections
  https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/connections
  ... (stopped by a 5-request safety cap)
```

Expected: two requests (`/connections`, then `/connections?continuationToken=page2`) returning 3 items.

develop (after 0.33.0)

### Problem description

`Get-FabricCapacity` returns nothing even when the signed-in account has an active Fabric capacity. `Get-FabricDataPipeline` and `Get-FabricWorkspaceUser` have the same defect.

These cmdlets unwrap `.value` from the response a second time:

| Cmdlet | Line |
|---|---|
| `Get-FabricCapacity` | `src/Public/Capacity/Get-FabricCapacity.ps1:66`: `$capacities = (Invoke-FabricRestMethod @apiParams).Value` |
| `Get-FabricDataPipeline` | `src/Public/Data Pipeline/Get-FabricDataPipeline.ps1:74`: `$DataPipelines = (Invoke-FabricRestMethod @apiParams).Value` |

## Pull Request (PR) description

Fixes #163. `Invoke-FabricKQLCommand` didn't work: it failed with `Invalid URI: The hostname could not be parsed`, then `Cannot index into a null array`. This PR fixes the bug, aligns the cmdlet with the module's patterns, and adds `-ApiType` to `Invoke-FabricRestMethod` so it can call the Kusto API with the right token. The design is described in [this comment on #163](https://github.com/dataplat/FabricTools/issues/163#issuecomment-6751875824).

## Summary

The parameter that identifies the resource a cmdlet acts on can now also be passed by a generic name. Nothing is renamed, so existing scripts keep working.

| Parameter | New aliases |
|---|---|
| `<Noun>Id` | `-Id` |
| `<Noun>Name` | `-Name`, `-DisplayName` |

```powershell
Get-FabricLakehouse -WorkspaceId $ws -Name 'Sales'
Remove-FabricNotebook -WorkspaceId $ws -Id $notebookId
```

`<Noun>` is the cmdlet noun without the `Fabric` prefix. This means:
- **Parent parameters** such as `-WorkspaceId` on item cmdlets aren't aliased.
- **Cmdlets that take two IDs of different kinds** (e.g. `Add-FabricWorkspaceCapacity`) aren't affected.

## Changes

- **Aliases:** 104 cmdlets across 32 feature folders, with one commit per folder. The only source change is `[Alias()]` attributes. The existing `Name` alias on `Remove-FabricSQLDatabase` and `Remove-FabricWorkspace` now also includes `DisplayName`.
- **QA test:** `tests/QA/module.tests.ps1`, tag `ParameterAliases`. It enforces the convention for every exported cmdlet, so new cmdlets can't drift. It passes on all 228 cases.
- **Docs:** regenerated. The `docs/en-US` diff is only the new aliases and the `ms.date` stamps.
- **CHANGELOG:** the `## [Unreleased]` section is restored, with an entry for this change.

These 4 cmdlets already alias the parent `-WorkspaceId` as `-Id`. Moving that alias to the resource ID would change what `-Id` means for existing scripts, so they're listed as exceptions in the QA test:

Adds nine cmdlets that wrap the [Fabric Git REST APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/fabric/core/git), following the design agreed in https://github.com/dataplat/FabricTools/issues/48#issuecomment-6712983360.

| API | Cmdlet |
|---|---|
| Connect | `Connect-FabricGit` |
| Disconnect | `Disconnect-FabricGit` |
| Get Connection | `Get-FabricGitConnection` |
| Initialize Connection | `Initialize-FabricGitConnection` |
| Get Status | `Get-FabricGitStatus` |
| Commit To Git | `Invoke-FabricGitCommit` |
| Update From Git | `Invoke-FabricGitUpdate` |
| Get My Git Credentials | `Get-FabricGitCredential` |
| Update My Git Credentials | `Update-FabricGitCredential` |

## Design decisions applied
- **Provider type:** `-GitProviderType` is mandatory on `Connect-FabricGit`. It must match the parameter set used: Azure DevOps needs `-OrganizationName`/`-ProjectName`, GitHub needs `-OwnerName`. - **Automatic lookup:** if you don't pass `WorkspaceHead` or `RemoteCommitHash`, `Invoke-FabricGitCommit` and `Invoke-FabricGitUpdate` get them from `Get-FabricGitStatus`. `-NoAutoResolve` turns this off.

issues.body:
## Summary

Three cmdlets retrieve dataset refreshes. Two of them duplicate the third:

| Cmdlet | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [`Get-FabricDatasetRefreshHistory`](https://github.com/dataplat/FabricTools/blob/develop/src/Public/Dataset/Get-FabricDatasetRefreshHistory.ps1) | one dataset; supports `-Top` | ✅ **keep — the single cmdlet going forward** |
| [`Get-FabricDatasetRefreshes`](https://github.com/dataplat/FabricTools/blob/develop/src/Public/Get-FabricDatasetRefreshes.ps1) | one dataset; latest refresh only | ❌ delete |
| [`Get-FabricWorkspaceDatasetRefreshes`](https://github.com/dataplat/FabricTools/blob/develop/src/Public/Workspace/Get-FabricWorkspaceDatasetRefreshes.ps1) | all datasets in a workspace; loops over `Get-FabricDatasetRefreshes` | ❌ delete |

`Get-FabricDatasetRefreshHistory` already follows the module conventions:
- it calls `Invoke-FabricRestMethod` with hash splatting and `HandleResponse = $true`
- it uses `Write-Message` and `Confirm-TokenState`
- it doesn't depend on `MicrosoftPowerBIMgmt`
- it supports `-Top`

The only thing it's missing is the workspace-wide mode.

## Why the two old cmdlets should go

1. **Help text doesn't match the code.** They claim to return the refresh *history*, but only `$results.value[0]` (the latest refresh) is returned.
2. **The `Workspace` property is always empty.** It's set from `$w.name`, but `$w` is never defined.
3. **They depend on `MicrosoftPowerBIMgmt`.** They call `Get-PowerBIDataset` instead of going through the module's API layer.
4. **They don't follow the repo conventions:**
   - no hash splatting or `HandleResponse = $true`
   - `Write-Warning` instead of `Write-Message`

Inspired by Kevin Chant showing his PowerShell code to start a notebook (during SQLBits 2026).

The function should invoke a given notebook (by name or id) and (by default) wait for completion.
