Closes #2681 with no change in behaviour, per auth-ca's reading (0.20-p1-2681.md, plan 1), which auth-4d decided.

## Why there is no per-destination cap
- `outbound` resolves names a caller marks `outsideChosen` in a pool of its own: half the lookups, 2 by default. An outside party's slow names never hold the deployment's own.
- Within that share, one destination can fill it while it keeps sending requests; each lookup still stops at its deadline.
- The one caller with outside-chosen names today is `clients-cimd`. By default it fetches only from the hosts the operator's `allow` names (boot is refused with neither `allow` nor `allow-any-host`). So one destination can fill the share only where the operator set `allow-any-host`, which every start warns of, or wrote into `allow` a domain outsiders can add names under.
- A per-host cap is bypassed by varying names (`a.attacker.example`, `b.attacker.example`, …).
- A cap per registrable domain would work, but it brings the public suffix list, with its updates, into `outbound`, and it would slow legitimate tenants of one SaaS domain.

So the protection stays where the destinations are chosen, and the cards and the security model say so.

## Commits (one module each)
1. `outbound`: `lookups`' card says the outside share has no limit per destination, and that the caller that lets outsiders choose hosts (`clients-cimd`'s `allow`) is what keeps one from filling it. The package card was at its byte budget; the share is `lookups`' own.
2. `clients-cimd`: its card's fetch-limit line says the name lookups too have no per-host limit beyond the share, and when one host can fill them: `allow-any-host`, or an `allow` naming a domain outsiders can add names under.
3. `docs`: security-model's Outbound requests "Left to you" item for `allow-any-host` adds what that setting leaves one outside host able to do.

agent_prs.body:
Closes #2686 with no change in behaviour. The cards now say why the behaviour is what it is, as auth-ca's reading (0.20-p1-2686.md, plan 1) concluded and auth-4d decided.

## Why there is no change
An upstream may answer a refresh with the same access token. Both holders then:
- keep the earlier of the two ends (`upstreams`' `refreshedExpiry`);
- count the token's life from now (`obtainedAt`).

A refresh is due once half its life is spent and it is within `refresh-before` (30 s by default) of its end. Counting from now makes this a back-off. With a 1-hour token whose upstream always answers the same one:
- at 30 s left it refreshes;
- the next is due at 15 s left, then at 7.5 s, and it stops under a second;
- so the upstream is asked about five times before the end.

Counted from its first obtaining instead, as #2686 suggested, half the life would long be spent, so every request within the 30-second window would refresh. Only the rotation budget (24 an hour) and the lock would stop it. The issue's premise, "refreshes earlier than the original lifetime says", runs the other way. The two holders already agree, so there is nothing to move into `upstreams`.

## Commits (one module each)
1. `federation-grants`: `grant`'s card gets an invariant stating the back-off.
2. `federation-tokens`: `renewal`'s card says the same where it states the refresh's end.

## Checked
Guard and lint pass; cards only.

## 1. A reissue whose store answer is lost (card statement, no new record)

issues.body:
Two readers take stored values without checking their shape:

- **redis**: the rate-limit script's reply is converted with a bare `Number()` (`modules/store-redis/redis/src/redis-store.ts`, `numbers()`), with no integer check, so a malformed `resetAt` reaches rate-limit as `NaN` and becomes a `NaN` wait. rate-limit already treats an answer other than `counted` or `limited` as unavailable; the numbers inside a `limited` answer are not checked.
- **rate-limit**: a lockout's stored state is checked only to be an object (`modules/foundation/rate-limit/src/lockout.ts`, `stateOf`), so a `holdUntil` of the wrong type is read as it is.

No writer writes such values; both are hardening. Each is one module: redis checks the reply's numbers and answers unavailable otherwise; rate-limit checks the state's fields and reads a malformed state as unavailable, never as no hold.

agent_prs.body:
The authorization endpoint now accepts the `claims` request parameter (OpenID Connect Core §5.5) for standard claims.

## Behaviour

- A claim the parameter names is released beyond the scope, in the ID token or at userinfo. Only claims whose scope the client is allowed and the user agreed to are released.
- With `value` or `values`, a claim that does not match is held back.
- A `sub` value other than the signed-in user's is answered with `login_required`.
- Discovery says `claims_parameter_supported: true`.

## Where it lives

- `claims-selection` decides what each request asked for and keeps it for the request's code, its refresh family and each access token. It joins `code-grant`, so `combinations` composes it with its store template, `claims-selection-store`.
- `authorize` reads the parameter in an internal module of its own, for OpenID Connect requests only, and checks a requested `sub` before any acr refusal.
- `oidc` contributes each claim's scope and reads the selection pinned to each code it redeems.
- `refresh` and `userinfo` keep and apply the selection of a refresh family and of an access token. A token exchange keeps the subject token's constraints.

## Configuration: `claims-selection.mode` is required

- The setting takes `off`, `draining` or `on`. When it is unset, boot is refused with a message that names the choice.
- When upgrading one instance at a time, set `off` on every instance until all of them run 0.19, then set `on`.
- A generated app reads the mode from `CLAIMS_SELECTION_MODE`, and its `.env.example` sets `on`.

## Conformance

The interop-oidf deviation for the essential-claims plan, the `deviates: D-2` mark on oidc-core-5.5-a, and decision D-2 are removed. The suite's plan is expected to pass.

Upgrade notice: U-0.19-59 (docs/migration.md).

Closes #2356

The OpenID Foundation conformance suite's Basic plan test `oidcc-claims-essential` asks for the standard claim `name` as essential through the `claims` request parameter (OpenID Connect Core §5.5) and expects it from UserInfo. o3co reads only `auth_time` and `acr` from the `claims` parameter today, so the test ends in a WARNING (`EnsureUserInfoContainsName`).

Support for standard claims in the `claims` parameter is planned for 0.19: claims are returned only within the scopes the client is allowed and the user consented to, with value constraints applied, and carried through refresh with permission re-checked.

Until that lands, the interop-oidf expected entries record `oidcc-claims-essential` as a known noncompliance pointing to this issue, so the OIDF CI job can run for every other test. The entry is removed by the change that adds claims-parameter support.

A grant with a lifetime ceiling, such as a revocation-latency bound, had no way to tell whether the operator's `tokens.access-token-lifetime` exceeded it. The kernel hands each module only its own section, and `Tokens` did not offer the value. issues.body:
A grant with a lifetime ceiling cannot make boot fail when the operator's `tokens.access-token-lifetime` exceeds that ceiling: no module but `tokens` can read the lifetime, and `issue` only caps or replaces it.

## What 0.18.1 does

- The kernel gives each module only its own section (`modules/foundation/kernel/README.md:5`).
- `Tokens` exposes no lifetime. `issue`'s limits take `notAfter`, which caps the expiry, and `lifetimeSeconds`, which replaces the section's lifetime (`modules/oauth/tokens/src/contract.ts:106-110`). Unchanged on `develop`.

Tried on an app generated by `@o3co/create-auth-provider@0.18.1`, with a grant module of our own whose ceiling is 900 s:

- `tokens.access-token-lifetime = 1800s`, grant passing `notAfter = now + 900 s`: boot succeeds, and every token is silently capped at 900 s.
- `tokens.access-token-lifetime = 300s`, grant passing `lifetimeSeconds = 900`: the grant's value replaces the operator's, and the token lives 900 s.

Neither path tells the operator their lifetime setting does not hold.

## Why a consumer needs it

provin.auth's DID grant refuses boot when the access-token lifetime exceeds `revocationLatencyBoundSec`, and for the `LEGACY_DID_LOGIN@1` contract when it exceeds `legacyMaxTtlSec` (rule `auth.legacy.did-login`). On 0.15 the grant read the lifetime from the configuration it was built with. On 0.18 it has two choices, both worse:

- cap with `notAfter`: a misconfiguration boots and is hidden;
- carry a lifetime of its own and pass `lifetimeSeconds`: operators keep two lifetime settings in step, and `tokens.access-token-lifetime` silently stops applying to this grant.

The need is not specific to DID: any grant whose tokens must stay within a revocation-latency or policy bound has it.

## Asked

A way for a grant's lifetime ceiling to be checked at boot against the lifetime `tokens` will apply, refusing boot with both values named. For example:

- `Tokens` exposes the configured access-token lifetime, read at build time,

In 0.18 an environment variable is read only where the app's HOCON writes `${?VAR}` (`modules/foundation/kernel/src/config.ts:19-37`; `docs/migration.md:114`). A generated app binds only the handful of keys in its `config/application.conf`. Nothing looks at the other variables in the environment, so every 0.17 variable left in a deployment's environment or secret store is ignored without a word. The setting it used to control then takes its 0.18 default.

issues.body:
`create-auth-provider <target> <package>...` (the listed app) writes an app that cannot boot until the operator adds the modules the listed ones require. Boot names those modules one layer at a time.

## Reproduction (`@o3co/create-auth-provider@0.18.0-rc.3`)

```
create-auth-provider app @mod/token-endpoint @mod/tokens @mod/clients @mod/client-allowance @mod/issuer @mod/subject-revocation @mod/subject-tokens
next: cd app && pnpm install && pnpm start
```

The app gets the listed modules, plus `tokens-store`, `subject-revocation-store` and `log-stdout`. With the required configuration written, five boots followed, each refusing a further layer:

1. `refused issuer|token-endpoint|tokens: no module provides http.site`, `tokens: no module provides keys`, `clients: no module provides secret-hash.checkers`, `tokens-store|subject-revocation-store: no module provides store`
2. after adding http, keys, store, secret-hash: `refused tokens: no module provides sender-binding`
3. after adding sender-binding: `refused token-endpoint: no module provides audit`
4. after adding audit: `refused http.routes:POST /oauth/token: uses a policy no module applies: rate-limit.requests-per-source`
5. after adding rate-limit: boots.

`tokens` needed `keys` and `http.site` in round 1, but its `sender-binding` need surfaced only in round 2.

The README says the listed app assembles "the modules asked for … with the wirings and bridges `combinations` adds by default" (`modules/scaffold/create-app/README.md`). It does not say that what those modules require is left to the operator. The printed `next:` line suggests the app runs.

## Asked

One of:

- have the listed app add the modules its listed ones require, as it adds wirings and bridges; or
- refuse generation, or print the missing providers, naming them.

Either way, boot should name every unmet requirement at once, not one layer per boot.

issues.body:
## Version

`v0.18.0-rc.3` (`@o3co/auth-provider-oauth` `discovery` / `authorize`; `@o3co/auth-provider-upstream-login` `idp-oidc`).

## What happens

- The authorization response already includes `iss` (RFC 9207).
- The discovery metadata does not advertise `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: true`.
- `idp-oidc` checks that metadata flag of its upstream. When one 0.18 instance federates with another 0.18 instance, the downstream logs `idp-oidc.iss_not_required` at every boot, although the upstream does send `iss`.

## Why it matters

- Relying parties (including another 0.18 instance) cannot learn from metadata that `iss` is sent, so they cannot require it, and the mix-up defence of RFC 9207 is weaker than it could be.
- A warning at every boot for a correct setup trains operators to ignore warnings.

## Suggested direction

- Advertise `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: true` in the discovery document whenever `authorize` sends `iss`, and test that the two stay in step.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Generate two apps with `npx @o3co/create-auth-provider@0.18.0-rc.3`: an upstream (`--pattern simple-web`) and a downstream (`--pattern sso-federated`) whose `federation.idps.up` points at the upstream.
2. `GET <upstream>/.well-known/openid-configuration`: no `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported`.
3. Boot the downstream: `idp-oidc.iss_not_required` is logged. A code-flow redirect from the upstream does contain `iss`.

issues.body:
## Version

`v0.18.0-rc.3` (`@o3co/auth-provider-oauth` `authorize`; `@o3co/auth-provider-upstream-login` `federation`).

## What happens

- When a fresh login is needed, `authorize` makes a `reauth` record and sends the browser to `authorize.login-page`, adding only `redirect_to` (`modules/oauth/authorize/src/flow/flow.ts:82-90`). `prompt`/`max_age` stay inside the `redirect_to` URL.
- The federation start honours freshness only from its own query string, `prompt=login` and `max_age` (`modules/upstream-login/federation/src/round-trip/round-trip.ts:166-184`; card: "start: `redirect_to`, `prompt` (only `login` is passed on), `max_age`"). It passes them on to the upstream (`idp-oidc/src/upstream.ts:184-188`).
- So when the login page is the federation start (the natural setting for a deployment whose only login is one upstream, `--pattern sso-federated`), or when a login page forwards only `redirect_to`, the upstream is never asked to re-authenticate. An upstream that still has a session answers at once, with its old `auth_time`.
- The local session's authentication time is taken from that `auth_time` (`federation/src/round-trip/login.ts:72, 91-96`). Back at `authorize`, the record is taken but the session is not fresh. `authorize` refuses only when the time is unknown, and otherwise sends the browser to the login page again (`flow.ts:96-99`), which starts the same round trip.

Observed (sso-federated pattern; `authorize.login-page` = `<origin>/session/oauth/federation/<idp>`; the upstream is another 0.18 instance that still has the user's session):

- Upstream login more than 30 s before (default `clock-skew = 30s`), then `/oauth/authorize?…&prompt=login`. This produces a redirect loop:
  ```text
  302 /oauth/authorize [prompt=login]
  302 /session/oauth/federation/up [redirect_to=…]          ← no prompt
  302 <upstream>/oauth/authorize                            ← no prompt
  302 /session/oauth/federation/up/callback
  302 /oauth/authorize [prompt=login, reauth=…]

issues.body:
## Summary

The current signing key pair can be supplied from the environment
(`KEY_STORE_LOCAL_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH`, `KEY_STORE_LOCAL_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH`,
or the inline `..._KEY` variants). The verification-only keys used during
rotation, `key-store.local.previousKeys`, cannot. Please add an env-bound way
to provide them.

Observed on `@o3co/create-auth-provider` 0.17.0 (tag `v0.17.0`).

## Current behaviour

- `templates/standalone/config/reference.conf` (`key-store.local`) binds
  `algorithm`, `kid`, `secret`, `privateKeyPath`, `publicKeyPath`,
  `privateKey` and `publicKey` to `KEY_STORE_LOCAL_*` variables. It binds
  nothing for `previousKeys` / `previousSecrets`, and says to "add the one
  matching your algorithm in your own layer".
- `docs/operator-runbook.md` (section "6. Key rotation") states: "There is no
  env binding for `previousKeys` / `previousSecrets` -- they are written in
  your HOCON layer."
- `packages/core/src/keys/factory.mts` (`narrowPreviousKeysArray`,
  `createLocalKeyStore`) reads `config.previousKeys` as an array of
  `{ kid, publicKey | publicKeyPath, expiresAt }`. Each entry's
  `publicKeyPath` is read from disk, but the list itself, with its kids and
  expiry dates, has to be in the config files.
- The only overlay mechanism is `config/{CONFIG_ENV || NODE_ENV}.conf`, which
  must live inside the composition's own `config/` directory
  (`templates/standalone/src/configPath.mts`, `resolveConfigPaths`;
  `src/app.mts`). There is no variable that names an additional HOCON file
  elsewhere.

## Use case

In container deployments, secrets are delivered as environment variables at
start-up and written to an in-memory file system before the provider starts.
The image is built once and the `config/` files baked into it cannot carry
per-deployment values.

The rotation order we follow is: publish the new public key (JWKS cache TTL +
token lifetime) -> switch signing to the new key -> keep the old public key for
verification until tokens signed with it
issues.title: Allow `key-store.local.previousKeys` to be supplied from an env var / file path (rotation without rebuilding the image)

issues.body:
provider 0.18 and policy-verifier 0.16 read the same HS256 secret string as different key bytes. A deployment that gives both the same string gets tokens the verifier rejects.

## What each reads

- **provider 0.18** reads `keys.signing.secret` as hex when it is whole bytes of hex, else as strict base64, and uses the decoded bytes (`v0.18.0-rc.3:modules/foundation/keys/src/signing/ring.ts:39-46`, `modules/foundation/keys/src/secret/secret.ts:11-14`).
- **policy-verifier 0.16.1** always uses the string's UTF-8 bytes (`o3co/auth.policy-verifier v0.16.1:packages/server/src/jwt/builtinKeyResolversModule.mts:68-71`).

Tried on an app generated by `@o3co/create-auth-provider@0.18.0-rc.3`, with `keys.signing.secret` set to a random 64-character hex string:

- The issued token's HS256 signature matches the hex-decoded 32 bytes.
- It does not match the string's UTF-8 bytes, which is what policy-verifier 0.16.1 checks it against.

## Consumer workaround

Give the provider the hex of the verifier's string's UTF-8 bytes. Hex rather than base64, because the provider reads hex first. The verifier's string must then clear both entropy checks:

- the provider's: at least 32 bytes and 8 distinct byte values;
- the verifier's: the shortest of its UTF-8, hex and base64 readings is at least 32 bytes (`packages/server/src/config/secretEntropy.mts:84`).

Neither README states this.

## Asked

One of:

- state the conversion in both READMEs; or
- give the provider (or the verifier) an explicit way to read the secret as the other does, chosen in configuration rather than guessed from the value.
issues.title: keys: provider 0.18 and policy-verifier 0.16 read the same HS256 secret as different key bytes

## Version

`v0.18.0-rc.3`, `docs/migration.md`.

## What changed (not in the migration guide)

The JSON on standard output changes shape in 0.18, for process logs and for the audit trail alike. The migration guide covers renamed events (`introspection.unavailable`, `http.unavailable`, `upstream-handoff.*`) and renamed settings (`logging.level` → `kernel.logging.level`). It does not describe the lines themselves.

| | 0.17 (standalone template defaults) | 0.18 |
|---|---|---|
| Process log line | pino envelope: numeric `level` (`30`, `40`, …), `time`, `name: "provider"`, `msg` (`templates/standalone/src/logger.mts`, v0.17.0) | `{"level":"info","at":<epoch ms>,"event":"<name>", …fields}`: `level` is a **string**, `event` replaces `msg`, no `name` or `time` (`modules/log-sinks/log-stdout/README.md`) |
| Audit line (`audit-stdout` / default sink) | pino envelope with `name: "audit"`, `msg: <event type>`, the event nested under `audit` (`timestamp`, `type`, `subject`, `clientId`, `ip`, `userAgent`, `details`) | `{"kind":"<event>","at":<epoch ms>,"subject"?:…,"attributes":{…}}`: no `level`, no `name`, no `msg`. Fields move into `attributes` (`client`, `source`, `grant_type`, …) (`modules/audit-receivers/audit-stdout/README.md`) |
| Telling the two apart | `name` (`provider` / `audit`) | Presence of `level` (log) vs. its absence (audit) |

Observed from a generated app:

```json
{"level":"info","at":1792502666577,"event":"http.listening","port":18080}
{"kind":"token.issued","attributes":{"client":"svc-client","source":"127.0.0.1","grant_type":"client_credentials"},"at":1792502671322}
```

## Why it matters

Log pipelines commonly route and alert on these fields: a filter on `name == "audit"` to send the audit trail to a separate store, `level >= 40` for warnings, `msg` for alert names, `audit.type`/`audit.clientId` for dashboards. After an upgrade, all of them stop matching without error. In particular, the audit trail is no longer separated from process logs by an existi

- 补充插件 mock、回归测试和 [cobalt 配置/部署指南](docs/cobalt-download.md)，并更新 README 与本地启动文档。

Closes #371

- **711 项后端相关测试通过**：覆盖新增 cobalt 客户端/配置/凭据/会话/纵向集成，以及原下载器、插件注册/选择/预检、任务快照、执行器、探测和编排兼容性。

issues.body:
<!-- openhands-development-plan:v1 -->

## 中文技术方案

### 问题理解
`drive-service` 的 `postPythonUpload` 当前使用无限超时的 HTTP 客户端，并且上传文件流没有贯通传输上下文。Python API 无响应或上传过程中触发暂停/取消时，sidecar 可能长期阻塞，用户无法可靠终止导入。

### 预计修改模块或文件
- `drive-service/internal/config/config.go`：增加 Python 导入请求的独立超时配置及安全默认值。
- `drive-service/config.example.json`、`drive-service/README.md`：暴露并说明配置项。
- `drive-service/internal/transfer/manager.go`：使用带 context 的 HTTP 请求，为 multipart 文件复制增加取消检查，并应用 Python 请求超时。
- `drive-service/internal/config/config_test.go`、`drive-service/internal/transfer/manager_test.go`：覆盖默认配置与取消路径。

### 核心实现思路
保留现有流式 multipart 上传，使用 `http.NewRequestWithContext` 让 `client.Do` 响应传输上下文取消；将 `PythonTimeoutSeconds` 与 Drive API 的 `RequestTimeoutSeconds` 分离，默认 1800 秒并对非正值回退默认值；文件复制按有限缓冲分块，在每次读取前检查 context，出现取消或读写错误时关闭 multipart writer 并传播错误。

### 关键数据流与调用关系
传输 worker 创建的 context → `postPythonUpload` → multipart pipe 的文件复制 goroutine与 HTTP request → Python `/api/tasks/upload`。取消信号同时终止请求和后续文件流，超时由 HTTP client 兜底，响应体继续由现有逻辑关闭。

### 兼容性考虑
旧配置文件缺少新字段时自动采用 30 分钟默认值；既有 `request_timeout_seconds` 语义不变；不改变 Python API 路径、认证头或成功响应处理。

### 测试方案
运行 `go test ./...`（工作目录为 `drive-service`），重点验证配置默认值、已取消 context 的上传失败，以及现有 transfer/drive/oauth/httpapi 测试；再运行仓库现有 Python 测试作为回归检查（若依赖已就绪）。

### 主要风险
multipart 写入 goroutine 与 HTTP 请求取消之间可能出现资源关闭时序问题；超时过短会影响大文件导入，因此默认值保持 30 分钟并允许配置。将通过专项测试和完整 Go 测试检查泄漏、错误传播及兼容性。

### 本次不处理范围
不修改 Python 端上传接口、不改 Drive 下载超时、不改任务状态模型或取消后的服务端任务清理语义，不处理其他 Issue 或无关重构。

_此评论由 OpenHands AI 代理代表用户生成。_

agent_prs.title: Fix FFmpeg dual pipe deadlock on large stderr output

issues.body:
## 一、问题描述
建议级别：严重

现象：音频提取或字幕烧录执行 FFmpeg 时，如果 FFmpeg 向 stderr 写入大量错误输出，后台任务可能永久卡住，任务状态一直停留在 EXTRACTING 或 BURNING，线程池 worker 也无法释放。

触发条件：输入文件损坏、编码器失败或其他场景导致 FFmpeg 产生超过操作系统管道缓冲区容量的 stderr 输出，同时 stdout 的 `-progress pipe:1` 仍等待更多进度行。

期望结果：持续消费 stdout 和 stderr，FFmpeg 退出后及时更新任务为 FAILED，并释放子进程、管道和 worker。

实际结果：`_run_ffmpeg` 与 `run_ffmpeg` 逐行读取 stdout，只有 `proc.wait()` 返回后才读取 stderr；当 stderr 管道写满时，FFmpeg 阻塞在写 stderr，父进程继续等待 stdout，双方互相等待，任务无法完成。

用户影响：单个异常媒体即可长期占用一个流水线 worker；并发触发多个此类任务后会耗尽线程池，后续任务无法执行，用户只能重启服务恢复。

## 二、相关配置
- 环境：Python 后台服务，FFmpeg 子进程，默认流水线线程池。
- 代码证据：`src/core/audio_extractor.py:136-200` 的 `_run_ffmpeg` 通过 `Popen(..., stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE)` 创建双管道，并在 `for line in proc.stdout` 完成、`proc.wait()` 返回后才读取 stderr；`src/core/ffmpeg_utils.py:87-145` 的 `run_ffmpeg` 存在相同读取顺序。
- 入口：`src/core/audio_extractor.py:114` 的 `extract_audio` 调用 `_run_ffmpeg`；`src/core/subtitle_burner.py:148-156` 的 `burn_subtitles` 调用 `run_ffmpeg`；二者均由任务后台流水线触发。
- 触发链：异常 FFmpeg 输出大量 stderr → stderr OS pipe 填满 → FFmpeg 停止写入并无法退出 → 父进程等待 stdout/`wait()` → 任务状态不再推进。
- 实际后果：worker 长时间占用，多个任务可造成后台队列停滞；这是资源耗尽级别影响。

## 三、修复建议
- 根因：父进程未并行消费 FFmpeg 的 stdout 与 stderr，且在 `wait()` 后才读取 stderr。
- 建议：使用 `communicate()`（必要时结合实时进度的独立 stderr/stdout 读取线程或合并输出管道）确保两个管道持续被消费；保留进度解析，并在超时/取消时可靠终止进程、关闭管道、回收进程。
- 验证：在临时测试中启动一个同时产生大量 stderr 和进度 stdout 的可控子进程，调用两条 FFmpeg 执行路径，断言函数在子进程退出后返回/抛出，而不是卡住；测试不得调用真实模型、付费 API 或线上服务。

agent_prs.title: Protect read and download endpoints with SUBTRANS_API_TOKEN

issues.body:
## 一、问题描述

现象：读取类接口 `GET /api/tasks`（任务列表）、`GET /api/tasks/{task_id}`（任务详情）、`GET /api/tasks/{task_id}/source`（源视频）、`GET /api/tasks/{task_id}/download`（成品视频）、`GET /api/tasks/{task_id}/subtitle`（字幕）均未挂载任何鉴权，甚至连可选的 `require_api_token` 依赖都没有。这意味着即使管理员设置了 `SUBTRANS_API_TOKEN`，这些接口仍然对所有人开放。

默认部署以 `--host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000` 启动，任务列表会返回每个任务的源 URL、状态、进度等元数据，下载接口直接以 `FileResponse` 返回用户已下载的视频与字幕文件。任何能访问该端口的客户端都可枚举任务并下载媒体内容。

触发条件：
- 默认部署（`uvicorn --host 0.0.0.0`），服务端口对网络可达（README 推荐安装后直接开放 8000）；
- 任意客户端 `GET /api/tasks` 即可枚举任务，`GET /api/tasks/{task_id}/download` 或 `/subtitle` 即可下载媒体内容。

期望：媒体文件与任务元数据应受鉴权保护；实际：完全公开，`SUBTRANS_API_TOKEN` 对读取接口无效。

## 二、相关配置

- 环境：Linux / Python 3.10–3.12，FastAPI + `FileResponse`。
- 部署：`docs/quick-start-linux.md:188` systemd `ExecStart` 使用 `--host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000`；`docs/quick-start-linux.md:251` 说明 token 仅保护“会修改数据的 API”，读取接口不在保护范围内。
- 代码证据：
  - `src/handler/tasks.py:374` `list_tasks`：`@router.get("")` 无 `dependencies=[Depends(require_api_token)]`。
  - `src/handler/tasks.py:393` `get_task`：同样无鉴权。
  - `src/handler/tasks.py:515-530` `download_source_video`：`FileResponse(path, ...)` 无鉴权。
  - `src/handler/tasks.py:532-570` `download_video`：`FileResponse(path, media_type="video/mp4", ...)` 无鉴权。
  - `src/handler/tasks.py:572-593` `download_subtitle`：`FileResponse(path, media_type="application/x-subrip", ...)` 无鉴权。
  - `src/handler/deps.py:52-63` `require_api_token`：仅挂在写入类接口上，且未设置 token 时直接放行。

## 三、修复建议

- 根因：读取/下载接口缺失鉴权，`SUBTRANS_API_TOKEN` 的可选鉴权机制未覆盖这些端点。
- 建议：
  1. 为 `list_tasks`、`get_task`、`download_source_video`、`download_video`、`download_subtitle`（以及对应 `HEAD` 探测接口）统一挂载鉴权；并在默认安装中默认启用，或至少在部署文档/安装器中给出强制开启的明确引导。
  2. 下载接口改用不可猜测、带鉴权的临时链接，或统一走受保护的下载端点。
- 验证：配置 `SUBTRANS_API_TOKEN` 后，不带 token 请求 `GET /api/tasks` 与 `/api/tasks/{task_id}/download`，断言返回 401（幂等、不触外部服务）。

## 背景
Subtitles-AI 启动时跑 `scan_missing_terminal` 把磁盘产物已丢失的 SUCCESS 任务降级为 MISSING,以保证列表/详情不再暴露失效下载链。但 **disk_failure / volume_migrated / user_cleaned 三种原因在异常路径上混为一谈**,启动日志和任务记录看不出"为什么降级"。

## 现状缺口
`src/handler/tasks.py:167-173`:
```python
data_root_unavailable = not data_path.exists()
if not data_root_unavailable:
    try:
        data_path_unavailable = not any(data_path.iterdir())  # ← iterdir() 在多种 OSError 下被吞
    except OSError:
        data_root_unavailable = True
```
`data_dir` 被替换为同名文件 / 权限变更 / mount 暂时不可读 / 文件系统损坏 都会抛 `OSError`,**异常实例和 errno 被全部丢弃**,直接走 tasks.py:198-201 的 fallback,批量把所有 SUCCESS 任务打成 `DOWNGRADE_REASON_VOLUME_MIGRATED`(success_count > 1)或 `UNKNOWN`。**真实的磁盘损坏(应标 DISK_FAILURE)被掩盖**,用户在 UI 看到 30 个 MISSING + VOLUME_MIGRATED,无法判断"换个 mount 就能恢复"还是"硬盘坏了"。

## 建议方案
1. 把 `except OSError as e:` 拆成 `NotADirectoryError`(→ USER_CLEANED)、`PermissionError`(→ DISK_FAILURE)、`OSError` 含 errno(EIO/ENXIO/ESTALE → DISK_FAILURE,其它 → UNKNOWN)三档
2. `logger.warning("scan_missing_terminal data_dir 异常: errno=%s msg=%s", e.errno, e)` 让启动日志可追溯
3. `TaskRecord.downgrade_errno` 新字段持久化 errno,前端 hover MISSING 任务时展示原因

issues.body:
## 背景
`POST /api/storage/cleanup` 用 TokenBucketRateLimiter 做 IP 级限流(`capacity=10, fill_rate=10/60`),目的是防止清理接口被滥用。但在多标签页 / 内网高频访问场景下,限流自身的 GC 逻辑反向放行,导致节流彻底失效。

## 现状缺口
`src/handler/storage.py:55-72`:
```python
def check(self, ip: str) -> bool:
    now = time.time()
    with self._lock:
        if len(_buckets) > 1000:
            self._buckets = {
                k: (t, ts) for k, (t, ts) in self._buckets.items() if now - ts < 120  # ← 兜底 GC
            }
        tokens, last_time = self._buckets.get(ip, (float(self.capacity), now))  # ← 命中失败 IP 重置为满桶
        delta = now - last_time
        tokens = min(float(self.capacity), tokens + delta * self.fill_rate)
        ...
```
当 `_buckets` 超过 1000 项时,**所有 120 秒前的条目被清空**,被清空的 IP 下次访问走 `self._buckets.get(ip, (capacity, now))` → **直接拿到满桶 token,fill_rate 完全没归零** → 限流被绕过。

**场景**:内网 1500 客户端同时打 `/api/storage/cleanup`(用户清理任务时多标签页点 N 次),触发 `_buckets` 清空 → 旧 IP 列表全部重新从满桶开始 → 接下来 60 秒每 IP 可打 10 次 → 节流彻底失效。

## 建议方案
1. **删除"满载清空"分支**:Token Bucket 容量本身有限,1k 个 IP × 10 token = 上限,不需要兜底重置
2. 改成真正的 fixed window counter:每分钟最多 N 次,边界才 reset,语义清晰且无歧义
3. 如果要保留 LRU,用 `collections.OrderedDict` + `popitem(last=False)` 主动驱逐最久未用,而非按时间窗硬切

## 完整分析报告
/Users/wenzhengfeng/.hermes/cron/reports/repo-product-analyst-with-issues/Subtitles-AI/PROJECT_ANALYSIS.md
issues.title: [Product Analysis] TokenBucketRateLimiter 满载清空后 fill_rate 未归零,cleanup 限流失效

A `bazel_dep` bump in this repo still widened `dx test --affected` to `//...`. The module graph diff from #14858 was in place, but four checks fired on changes they could not be affected by:

- **`patch_cmds`.** Bazel does not apply `patch_cmds` edits to `MODULE.bazel`, so they cannot change the graph. They no longer widen.
- **Patch hunks whose statement start is outside the hunk.** An example is grpc's `pip_parse_no_310.patch`, which edits inside a `[pip.parse(...) for ...]` comprehension. dx now finds the hunk in the module's cached registry `MODULE.bazel`. issues.body:
`dx check --affected` / `dx test --affected` widen to `//...` for most edits to `MODULE.bazel`, `MODULE.bazel.lock`, `.bzl` files used by module extensions, and `.bazelrc` files.

Example: #14841 only added a `dev_dependency = True` `go_deps` usage with `module` tags and a `use_repo` for actionlint, but the affected planner selected `//...`, because only `bazel_dep` version strings were allowed to narrow.

Goal: select the users of the repos that an edit actually changes, and keep widening to `//...` for anything dx cannot attribute (deny by default):

- `MODULE.bazel` (and included segments): diff at call level. Tag and `use_repo` edits select that extension's repos, `go_deps.module` tags select the changed Go repos, `use_repo_rule` calls select their repo, override and `bazel_dep` edits select the module's repos. Comments and formatting select nothing.
- `MODULE.bazel.lock`: changed extension entries select that extension's repos.
- `.bzl` loaded by a root module extension or repository rule: select that extension's repos instead of `//...`.
- `.bazelrc`: edits that only touch comments, layout, or flags without build effect select nothing.
- Still `//...`: `register_*` edits, removed deps or `use_repo` names, hidden or patched module graphs, unknown calls.

issues.body:
Pull requests and the merge queue run what users run, on every OS, from `ci.yml`. No separate `pr-check.yml`.

- `check (<platform>)`: `dx check --affected` on linux_x86_64, linux_arm64, macos_arm64, windows_x86_64, windows_arm64.
- `coverage (<platform>)`: `dx coverage --affected --report lcov=lcov.info` on the same five; uploads `coverage-<platform>` for 7 days. No `--min-coverage`.
- Both run on `pull_request`, `merge_group` (base: the queue's base sha), schedule and dispatch.
- Every other `ci.yml` job (determinism, cross builds, analysis scaling, dogfood, coverage-cells, ...) runs only on schedule and dispatch. The old `gate` job is gone.
- `.github/rulesets/main.json` requires the 10 `check`/`coverage` contexts and adds a squash merge queue (ALLGREEN, build 5, merge 1-5, wait 1 min, timeout 120 min).
- Delete `pr-links.yml`, `api-label.yml`, `producers_bin --pr-links` and `--pr-check`, the `api` label and the `Closes`/`Part of`/`No issue` body-line rule.
- Land with `gh pr merge <n> --squash --auto`.

Closes #14609.

## What changed
- `HookKind::Git` (`dx worktree hook git`). It reads the `<old> <new> <ref>` lines that git passes to `reference-transaction` and refuses with exit 2 under the `dx.primary` rule. It refuses only:
  - `HEAD` and `ORIG_HEAD` while the main checkout holds its own lock on them. `git worktree add` writes the new worktree's `HEAD` through the main checkout's hook, so the lock is how the two are told apart.
  - `refs/stash`.
  - The main checkout's own branch.
  The message is `dx: refused: no git update of <ref> in the main checkout <path>. Work in a slot: tools/dx worktree add <branch>` (`cli/worktree/src/primary.rs`, `cli/exec_worktree/src/lib.rs`).
- `dx worktree add` writes the hook only into `.git/hooks` of the main checkout, or into a `core.hooksPath` from the local config that lies inside `.git`. When `core.hooksPath` is set in any other config or points outside `.git`, it writes nothing and warns with `git_hook_skipped`. It keeps a hook without dx's marker line and warns the same way (`ops.rs`, `primary::guard_git`). The hook holds the main checkout's path and passes in any other repository. It runs only that checkout's `tools/dx`, and when that dx gives no `no git update of` refusal it lets git go ahead, for example when the dx is old or missing.
- The git hook and the edit guard fail open: when git cannot read `dx.primary` or tell the checkout, as for a push into the repository or an edit under `.git`, they pass.

issues.body:
`dx worktree add` installs a git `reference-transaction` hook so commit, checkout, switch and reset are refused in the main checkout (#14607). Agent hooks refuse edits there.

## Work
1. Add `HookKind::Git`. Install at `git rev-parse --git-path hooks/reference-transaction` when absent or dx-owned. Refuse only `HEAD`, `ORIG_HEAD`, `refs/stash` and the main checkout's own branch. Message: `dx: refused: no git update of <ref> in the main checkout <path>. Work in a slot: tools/dx worktree add <branch>`.
2. Guard matcher in `setup.rs` becomes `Bash|Edit|Write|NotebookEdit`. `hook.rs` refuses file paths inside a protected main checkout.
3. Agent instructions block (`agents.rs`): add "Never build, edit or commit in the main checkout."

## Tests
- Real-git tests in `cli/worktree/src/tests.rs`: `dx worktree add`, `git worktree add`, slot commits and fetch still pass; main-checkout commit/switch/reset refused.

## Docs
- Hooks tables in `worktree.md` and `init.md`.

Closes #14607

The first `dx worktree add` sets `dx.primary` to `protected` and prints one notice. Once `dx.primary` is set, dx refuses Bazel work in the main checkout with exit 2 and JSON code `main_checkout`. In `protected` mode it refuses everyone. In `open` mode it refuses only agent sessions. Only read-only commands still run: `status`, `worktree`, `completion`, `config` (not `config override`), `--help` and `--version`. Every other command is refused before dx writes anything. `dx run` is refused before it builds.

dx fails closed. An unknown `dx.primary` value counts as `protected`, and a git error refuses with the reason. `GIT_CONFIG`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` and `git -c` do not change what dx reads. `CI=true` does not skip the check: CI never runs `dx worktree add`, so `dx.primary` stays unset there.

- `AGENT_ENVS` moves from `dx_adopt` to `dx_process` and gains `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `QWEN_CODE`, `AUGMENT_AGENT` and `COPILOT_CLI`.
- `dx worktree hook bazel -- <args>` applies the same rule to a single Bazel call. In a slot it also refuses the `clean` subcommand, and so does `dx clean --bazel`. Startup options with a separate value, such as `--output_base /x`, are skipped when finding the command.
- `tools/dx` and `tools/dx.cmd` ask the launcher copy of dx, then the `bazel-bin` dx, then git before the self-build, honour exit codes, and refuse when `dx.primary` is set or unreadable and no dx can answer. `worktree --help` runs without a build.

issues.body:
After `dx worktree add`, dx and the `tools/dx` launcher refuse Bazel work in the main checkout. This works for every agent, not just Claude.

## Behaviour
- The first `dx worktree add` sets `git config dx.primary protected` (when unset) and prints one notice.
- No checks when `dx.primary` is unset or `CI=true`.
- Main checkout: `git rev-parse --git-dir` equals `--git-common-dir`.
- `protected`: everyone is refused there. `open`: only sessions with an agent env var are refused.
- Agent env vars: `CLAUDECODE`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `CURSOR_AGENT`, `GEMINI_CLI`, `QWEN_CODE`, `AMP_CURRENT_THREAD_ID`, `AUGMENT_AGENT`, `OPENCODE`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `AI_AGENT`.
- Still allowed in the main checkout: `dx worktree|completion|explain`, `--help`, `--version`.
- Refusal exits 2: `dx: refused: no Bazel in the main checkout <path>. Work in a slot: tools/dx worktree add <branch>` (JSON code `main_checkout`).
- The `clean` subcommand in a slot is refused: `dx: refused: bazel clean in a slot drops its warm outputs and does not fix a stale cache. Rerun with --noremote_accept_cached, or release this slot and add a fresh one.`

## Work
1. New `cli/worktree/src/primary.rs` holds the rule. Move `AGENT_ENVS` (`cli/adopt/src/defaults.rs:10`) into a shared crate and extend it.
2. `cli/worktree/src/ops.rs` `lease_locked` sets `protected` when unset.
3. `cli/cli/src/exec.rs` refuses every command outside the allowed list.
4. New `HookKind::Bazel` (`hook.rs`): `dx worktree hook bazel -- <args>` checks the main checkout and refuses `clean` in a slot. `main.rs` and `exec/worktree.rs` accept trailing args.
5. `tools/dx` and `tools/dx.cmd`: `worktree hook` with no built dx exits 0. Before a self-build of `//:dx`, run the built copy's `hook bazel -- build //:dx`; on exit 2, skip the build and run that copy. `tools/dx worktree --help` must not build.

## Tests
- unset/protected/open × agent var × CI matrix.
- exec refusal; `dev_launcher.rs`: `worktree --help` runs without building.

## Doc

Closes #14261

The rules_android Desugar worker JVM died at startup on Windows (`EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION` in `jvm.dll` on windows_x86_64, `NoClassDefFoundError: java/lang/Object` on windows_arm64), so `//android/tests/fixtures/testonly_apk:testonly_targets_analyze` failed to build there.

What the evidence runs on this branch showed:
- The JDK is complete on disk, both in `external/rules_java++toolchains+remotejdk21_win*` and in the `desugar_java8.exe.runfiles` tree (`lib/modules`, `jvm.dll`, `classes.jsa`, `JAVA_VERSION="21.0.12"`). No hs_err file is written (run 45073421784).
- The `desugar.exe` java launcher, started as a plain process with the worker's runfiles env and the same `-Xms8g`, boots the JVM and reaches `Desugar.main` on both hosts (run 45074248831).
- The build passes on both Windows hosts with `--strategy=Desugar=local` (run 45075430333) and with `--noworker_sandboxing` (run 45075503593).

So the crash comes from the Windows worker sandbox, not from the JDK or the launcher.

Changes:
- `tools/bazelrc`: the correctness preset adds `build:windows --noworker_sandboxing`, regenerated into `.dx/bazelrc/correctness.bazelrc`.
- `evidence.yml`: when the task fails, a new step prints any `hs_err_pid*.log` under the output base or TEMP (and copies it to `jvm/` in the artifact), lists the `bin/java` each desugar, d8 or dex launcher's runfiles name with `jvm.dll`, `classes.jsa`, `lib/modules` and `JAVA_VERSION` next to it, and starts the desugar launchers once as plain processes. issues.body:
Follow-up of #14181. That PR pins build-tools and platform-tools for macos_arm64 and windows_x86_64 (windows_arm64 runs the x64 archives under emulation) for the `@dx_androidsdk` app SDK only. The `@dx_android_sdk` packaging hub stays on linux_x86_64 through a packaging host list.

## Where
- `android/private/sdk/repos.bzl`: the packaging host list that #14181 adds, read by `build_tools_repositories()`, `build_tools_no_match_error()` and the `platform_tools` entry of `package_repositories()`.
- `android/private/sdk/repos.bzl:657-702` `build_tools_build`: Linux layout only (`extracted/zipalign`, `extracted/lib64/libc++.so`).
- `android/private/sdk/repos.bzl:721-736` `platform_tools_build`: `extracted/adb`, no `adb.exe`.
- `android/private/sdk/repos.bzl:548-550` `package_no_match_error`: hard-codes linux_x86_64.
- `android/README.md` "Backend": APK assembly needs the Linux x86_64 SDK host.

## Fix
- Give `build_tools_build` and `platform_tools_build` a host argument: `.exe` names and `lib64/libwinpthread-1.dll` on Windows, `lib64/*.dylib` on macOS.
- Drop the packaging host list so the hub selects every pinned host, and map windows_arm64 to the windows_x86_64 repos.
- Run the `android_check`, `android_sign` and `android_apk_set` tests on macos_arm64, windows_x86_64 and windows_arm64 with `/evidence`, and update the README host lines.

No test proves that an action built twice gives the same output. The only hits for "deterministic" in test code are two serializer unit checks (`core/tests/execution_tests.bzl:10`, `core/quality/real_pipeline_tests.bzl:1083`).

- `tools/testing/nested` (the one nested-Bazel harness, `docs/design/nested-tests.md`).

- Rules with their own packers and launchers: `cli/archive`, `deploy/private`, `appimage/private`, `msix/private`, `android/private/packaging`.

## Fix

- Add one nested test, `//tools/testing:determinism_test`, on the shared harness.
- It builds a fixed target list twice in two output bases with no disk or remote cache, writes `--execution_log_compact_file` each time, and compares the output digests per action.

- State the measured time in the PR, as `docs/design/tests.md` section Speed requires, and keep the test inside the per-test budget.

- `bazel test //tools/testing:determinism_test` passes on main, sandboxed and offline.

Its `env_execute` runs `env -i` from PATH, and the nested harness sets PATH to `/dx_no_path`:

agent_prs.body:
Closes #14475
Part of #11387

On Windows, Dart's `File.copySync` won't copy from a link. `runtime/bin/file_win.cc` `File::Copy` calls `GetType(old_path, follow_links=false)`. Anything other than `kIsFile` sets `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`, and Dart reports that as `PathNotFoundException ... path = <source>`. We start Bazel with `--windows_enable_symlinks`, so the DartModule worker's inputs are links. rules_dart 0.9.1 `DeclaredView.stage` copies each input with `File(f).copySync(at)`, so every module compile failed. The tool reads the same package config right before staging, so the file does exist. The copy failed only because the source is a link.

- `patches/rules_dart/windows_copy_links.patch`: on Windows, copy from `File(f).resolveSymbolicLinksSync()`. Upstream main still has the old line.
- `MODULE.bazel`, `patches/rules_dart/BUILD.bazel`, `patches/README.md`: list the patch. Consumers hit the same bug, so the README row ends with `Consumer fix: #11387`, the issue that lets consumers work without root patches.

Tested: `//patches:update_readme_test`, `//patches:headers_test`, `//patches:render_unit_test`, `//patches:upstream_unit_test`, `//dart/tests/runtime:greet_test` and `//dart/tests/runtime:launcher_test` passed on linux_x86_64 with `--lockfile_mode=error`. `@rules_dart//dart/private/tools:kernel_tool` builds with the patch.

Follow-up of #10073. `cuda/private/toolchain/hub/BUILD.bazel` is public (`package(default_visibility = ["//visibility:public"])`) and has no `private-visibility` allowlist line, so `//tools/testing:language_skeleton_test` reports it on main. The hub owns the CUDA `toolchain_type`, which layout.md puts at `@rules_dx//cuda:toolchain_type`. The type can't simply move to `cuda/BUILD.bazel`: that file loads `//cuda/private:defs.bzl`, which loads `@rules_cuda`. - `patches/rules_cuda/toolchain_type_alias.patch:9` (alias `actual`).

- Move the three `cuda_component_library` targets into a `cuda/private` package. Keep `@rules_dx//cuda:cublas`, `:cufft` and `:curand` as public `alias`es in `cuda/BUILD.bazel`, the way `ocaml/BUILD.bazel` aliases `//ocaml/private/...`. Then `cuda/BUILD.bazel` loads no rules_cuda `.bzl`.

# Pull Request

## Changes

I diffed one `.so` and one `_iface` from the two output bases of `//tools/testing:determinism_check`. I reproduced it on `linux_x86_64_musl` with `--features=fully_static_link`. GHC writes two sandbox paths into the outputs:

- **`.so` RUNPATH**: it keeps `/…/sandbox/linux-sandbox/<n>/execroot/_main/external/+haskell+dx_haskell_toolchains__linux_x86_64_musl/dx_closure/lib`. That dir holds musl's libc, libm, libdl and libgmp, so cc_wrapper's `shorten_rpaths` keeps it. New `patches/rules_haskell/cc_wrapper_origin_rpath.patch`: on Linux, cc_wrapper rewrites an absolute rpath under the execroot to `$ORIGIN/<relpath>`.
- **`.hi`/`.dyn_hi`**: GHC force-includes the rts `ghcversion.h` and records its absolute sandbox path. New `patches/rules_haskell/cabal_ghcversion_relpath.patch`: cabal_wrapper reads the header's dir with `ghc-pkg field rts include-dirs` and passes `--ghc-option=-ghcversion-file=<path relative to the package dir>`.

Both patches are added to the `rules_haskell` patch list in `MODULE.bazel`, `patches/rules_haskell/BUILD.bazel` and `patches/README.md`. No actions are exempted from the check.

## Upstream

Both patches carry `Upstream: none (upstream-ready, not sent yet: #14473)`; agents get 403 filing in tweag/rules_haskell, so the owner files it under #14473.

issues.body:
Found by the release dry run for #14363. Run https://github.com/devhusdk/rules_dx/actions/runs/44876826441 fails `tools / hackage (nixfmt, linux-arm64)`. The build passes, then `//tools/testing:determinism_check` reports `32 nondeterministic actions`. All 32 are `HaskellCabalLibrary` outputs in `bazel-out/aarch64-fastbuild-ST-*`: 18 are `_install/lib/libHS<pkg>-<ver>-ghc9.10.3.so` and 14 are `_install/<pkg>-<ver>_iface` directories, in packages such as ansi-terminal, hashable, megaparsec, nixfmt and scientific. The `nixfmt-exe-nixfmt` binary is not in the list.

#14237 added the check, and this run is its first on this leg. The hlint and ormolu linux-arm64 legs stopped earlier on #14379, and the haskell linux legs stopped on #14371, so they are likely to hit the same failure next.

## Where
- `.github/workflows/release-tools.yml:459-475` (hackage `flags` and the `determinism_check` call)
- the `haskell_cabal_library` actions for `@haskell_nixfmt_hackage` (they build shared libraries even under `--features=fully_static_link`)

## Fix
- Diff one `.so` and one `_iface` pair between the two output bases that `determinism_check` writes under `--out`, and name the source of the difference.
- Then make those actions deterministic. Either stop building the shared libraries in the musl `fully_static_link` configuration or pass the GHC flags that remove the difference. Do not exempt the actions from the check.
- Proof: the `hackage (nixfmt, linux-arm64)` leg of a `release.yml` dry run passes.

Part of #14209.

Closes #14476

On the `launch-heavy` linux_x86_64 leg only:
- Adds a 16 GB swap file on `/mnt` before the Julia tests.
- `--show_progress --show_progress_rate_limit=60` overrides `--noshow_progress`, so the log shows the running action.
- A background loop logs `free -m` (memory and swap) and `df -h / /mnt` every 30s on Linux.

The other legs are unchanged.

The first dispatch with only the monitor, run 44909287351 (job 136861445889), showed the cause. One action ran alone: `JuliaSysimage //julia/tests/fixtures/hello/app:hello_standalone`. It filled 15.8 of 16 GB of RAM while `/` stayed at 42%, and then the runner shut down with exit 143. A CPU cap cannot help a single action, so this PR adds swap.

issues.body:
`launch-heavy` linux_x86_64 has not passed once since #13727 added the job. The runner dies in "Run the Julia standalone and tool tests":

| run | job | time | annotation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 44857005940 | 136701446709 | 12m | exit code 143, "runner has received a shutdown signal" |
| 44862650657 | 136719272182 | 12m | exit code 143 |
| 44863631155 | 136722337626 | 46m | "hosted runner lost communication with the server" |
| 44873161495 | 136751974276 | 57m | "lost communication" |
| 44892308210 | 136810573837 | 12m | exit code 143 |

The last lines in the log are `INFO: From Compiling src/runtime_intrinsics.c` and `... [for tool]` from `+dx_pins+julia_src`. After them there is no output for about 11 minutes, because the step passes `--noshow_progress`, and then the shutdown follows. So the source-built libjulia-internal (#14192) compiles twice locally, once for the target and once for the exec configuration, together with the LLVM-header C++ objects and the sysimage. A 4-vCPU, 16 GB `ubuntu-latest` runner likely runs out of memory under that load. The other four legs pass: linux_arm64 and macOS use the stock library. The runner dies before the exec-log upload step, so nothing reaches the remote cache and every run starts cold.

## Where

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1139-1178`: the `launch-heavy` job and its linux_x86_64 leg on `ubuntu-latest`.
- `julia/private/runtime/julia_src.BUILD.bazel:295-363`: `runtime_c`, `runtime_cxx` and `libjulia_internal_objects`, which compile against `@julia_src_libllvm//:headers`.
- `julia/private/runtime/BUILD.bazel:46-62`: `source_julia` and `source_toolchain`, which make every Linux x86_64 Julia action use the source build.

## Fix

- Find out which resource runs out. Dispatch ci.yml on a branch where the linux_x86_64 launch-heavy step first starts `(while sleep 30; do free -m | sed -n 2p; df -h / | tail -1; done) &` and drops `--noshow_progress`, so the log shows the running actions and the memory and disk use before the shutdown

issues.body:
Follow-up of #10073. About ten `private-visibility` allowlist lines cover targets that rules_dx legacy macros use as `select()` keys or as `target_compatible_with` values in consumer packages. Bazel checks the visibility of those labels against the consumer package, so a `dx_private_dep_rule` forwarder can't fix them. That forwarder works only for deps.

## Where

- Platform-support select keys built by `compatible_with()` (core/platform_support.bzl:23): `rules_dart_platform` (dart/private/BUILD.bazel), `rules_flutter_platform` (flutter/private/BUILD.bazel), `rules_julia_platform` (julia/private/BUILD.bazel), `rules_perl_platform` (perl/private/BUILD.bazel).
- Coverage and toolchain select keys: `windows_coverage` (kotlin/private/BUILD.bazel, read in kotlin/private/kwargs.bzl:54), `coverage_*` (swift/private/BUILD.bazel), and `msvc`, `clang_cl`, `msvc_opt`, `libstdcxx`, `libstdcxx_ready` and `browser_linux_x86_64` (rust/private/BUILD.bazel, read in rust/private/defs.bzl:30-38).
- Explicitly public constraint values: `unsupported` (qt/private/BUILD.bazel, read in qt/private/cells.bzl:19). `unsupported_value()` (core/cells.bzl:19) hard-codes `//visibility:public`, so the same problem exists in every `<lang>/private` package, even though the text check doesn't flag it.

## Fix

Choose one mechanism and use it for all of these targets:
1. Move the settings and constraint values into one public, non-`private/` package, such as `//core/platforms/<lang>`. Then point the `.bzl` labels and the `language_skeleton_allowlist.txt` lines at the new location. This needs few changes, but the labels become reachable API.
2. Convert the wrapper macros that build these selects into symbolic macros. Bazel then checks visibility at the macro definition, so the targets can stay in `private/`. This is the bigger migration because it touches every `dx_wrap*` caller.

Option 1 is the recommended choice unless the symbolic-macro migration is already planned. Then delete the matching allowlis

Part of #14076. The java, csharp, dart, haskell and swift lock resolvers read a pinned tool from runfiles through `$(rlocationpath ...)` env vars (`DX_MAVEN_JAVA`, `DX_MAVEN_RESOLVER`, `DX_DART`, `SWIFT`, ...), so they cannot simply become `dx <lang>_lock`. The java one also runs a rules_dx `java_binary` (`:resolver`, the rules_jvm_external Maven resolver) that every consumer compiles. The PR for #14076 roots the java resolver in the java guard and allowlists `java/private/tools/lock:lock` and `:resolver`.

## Where
- `java/private/tools/lock/BUILD.bazel` (`resolver` java_binary, `lock` rust_binary, `TOOLS_ENV`), `java/private/tools/lock/src/resolve.rs` (`Tools::from_env`)
- `csharp`, `dart`, `haskell`, `swift`: `<lang>/private/tools/lock/BUILD.bazel` (`data`/`env` on `rust_binary(name = "lock")`) and `src/main.rs`
- `cli/launcher/defs.bzl` (`dx_subcommand`), `cli/prebuilt/tools.bzl` (`TOOLS`, `_jar`)
- `tools/testing/consumer/prebuilt_guard_allowlist.txt` (the java resolver lines)

## Fix
- Give `dx_subcommand` a `data` list and a `path_args` dict (flag to label). Each entry becomes an `arg=<flag>` plus `path=<runfiles key>` launcher line, so the resolver gets absolute paths as flags and needs no runfiles library.
- Each resolver takes those flags instead of the rlocation env vars, moves onto `dx <lang>_lock` and drops its `rust_binary`.
- Ship the Maven resolver deploy jar as a registry jar tool (`_jar("maven_resolver", "@rules_dx//java/private/tools/lock:resolver", "com.github.bazelbuild.rules_jvm_external.resolver.maven.MavenMain")`) and pass the hub jar to `dx java_lock`.
- Drop the java resolver allowlist lines.

issues.body:
Follow-up to #13326. `rust_test` forwards `shard_count` (`core/wrapper.bzl:75`), but rules_rust 0.75 test binaries ignore `TEST_SHARD_INDEX` and never touch `TEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE`. With Bazel 9's default `--incompatible_check_sharding_support`, any sharded `rust_test` fails, and without that flag every shard runs the whole suite. #13326 works around this for `//cli/cli:dx_cli_test` with static `test_groups` (one compiled binary, one forwarder per libtest filter group). Real sharding would balance itself and needs no hand-kept filter lists. Upstream bazelbuild/rules_rust#3774 (`experimental_enable_sharding`) is still unmerged.

## Where
- `rust/private/defs.bzl:208` (`_rust_forward_test`) and `:344` (`rust_test`): the forwarder symlinks the upstream binary and has no shard support.
- `core/wrapper.bzl:75` (`dx_forwarded_test_kwargs`): forwards `shard_count` unchecked.
- `tools/coverage/collect/src/lib.rs:296`: the collector passes `TEST_BINARY` to llvm-cov as an object. A shard runner as the test executable would become that object and drop the crate's coverage.

## Fix
1. Add a small Rust shard runner (testonly tool) that:
   - lists tests with `<bin> --list --format terse`;
   - keeps index `i` where `i % TEST_TOTAL_SHARDS == TEST_SHARD_INDEX`;
   - touches `TEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE`;
   - execs `<bin> --exact <names...>` (batched for argv limits on Windows).
   `_rust_forward_test` uses it when `shard_count > 1`.
2. Let the collector take the coverage object from an env var the forwarder sets, such as `DX_COVERAGE_TEST_BINARY`, instead of `TEST_BINARY`. Ship it in the next `@dx_prebuilt` release.
3. Add analysis tests in `rust/tests/defs_tests.bzl` and a sharded fixture test that runs on Linux and Windows.
4. Move `//cli/cli:dx_cli_test` from `test_groups` to `shard_count`, then deprecate `test_groups`.

issues.body:
Blocked on: bazel-contrib/rules_ruby#435 and a rules_ruby release carrying it (latest is v1.0.0-rc2).

**Problem**
`patches/rules_ruby/reproducible.patch` makes the Ruby toolchain repository rule return `repository_ctx.repo_metadata(reproducible = True)`, so Bazel can reuse the toolchain from the repository cache. To make that true it deletes the code that sets `BUNDLE_BUILD__PSYCH` and `BUNDLE_BUILD__OPENSSL` for portable Ruby. Those variables point at the unpacked `dist/` directory with an absolute path (`str(repository_ctx.path("dist"))`), and the path is written into the generated `BUILD` through `{env}`. An absolute path makes the repo machine-specific, which is why upstream does not mark it reproducible. Deleting the variables removes a feature: compiling the `psych` and `openssl` gems against the libyaml and openssl that portable Ruby ships, under `--incompatible_strict_action_env`. Upstream would not take the patch as written.

Consumers do not get this patch today (#2283). rules_dx pins `0.28.0`; BCR has `0.29.0`, `1.0.0-rc1` and `1.0.0-rc2`, and upstream main is newer than all of them (`ruby/private/download.bzl` changed by 27 lines since `v0.28.0`).

issues.body:
Blocked on: https://github.com/aspect-build/rules_py/pull/1665

Part of #4821.

## Problem
`aspect_rules_py` writes `py_cc_toolchain` without `sys_platform` or `platform_machine`. rules_python then derives SOABI `cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu` on every target. `py_extension` names the module from that SOABI. On Linux arm64, macOS and Windows the file name is wrong and `import` fails.

## Where
- `@aspect_rules_py//py/private/interpreter:repository.bzl:259-263` (`py_cc_toolchain(...)` template)
- `@rules_python//python/private:py_cc_toolchain_rule.bzl:40-62,99-108` (platform tag and SOABI default)
- `MODULE.bazel:876-883` (`aspect_rules_py` pin and patch list)
- `patches/aspect_rules_py/BUILD.bazel`, `patches/aspect_rules_py/windows_venv.patch` (existing patch pattern)

## Fix
- Add `patches/aspect_rules_py/py_cc_toolchain_platform.patch`. In the template, pass `sys_platform` (`linux`, `darwin`, `win32`) and `platform_machine` (`x86_64`, `aarch64`) from the interpreter's platform triple. Pass `libc = "musl"` for musl triples.
- List the patch in `MODULE.bazel` after `windows_venv.patch`, and export it in `patches/aspect_rules_py/BUILD.bazel`.
- Add an analysis test under `python/tests/` that reads `PyCcToolchainInfo.soabi` for linux x86_64, linux aarch64, darwin arm64 and windows x86_64 target platforms. Expect `cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu`, `cpython-312-aarch64-linux-gnu`, `cpython-312-darwin` and `cp312-win_amd64`.
- Open the upstream issue and PR in aspect-build/rules_py, with a regression test. Link both here.

## Done when
- The analysis test passes. `tools/dx test --affected` is green.

issues.body:
Follow-up to #14404 (Kotlin) and #14402 (Scala). After those, the JVM quality aspects still load `@rules_android`, so a Java-only consumer running `dx check` needs the rules_android archive. That blocks #14357, which wants Java consumers to stop fetching rules_android at all.

## Where
- `java/private/quality/jvm_check.bzl:3` loads `@rules_android//providers:providers.bzl` for `AndroidIdeInfo`. Lines 15-16 name the Android SDK toolchain type and the Android kinds. Lines 26-50 hold `JvmAndroidSdkInfo`, `jvm_android_sdk_aspect` and `android_sdk_jars`. Line numbers are from the #14412 branch.
- `java/private/quality/jvm.bzl:6` loads these names. `:86` puts `jvm_android_sdk_aspect` in `real_jvm_lint` `requires`, and `:150` (spotbugs) calls `android_sdk_jars`.
- `jvm_check_aspect` lists `jvm_android_sdk_aspect` in `requires`. After #14404, `kotlin/private/quality/kotlinc_check.bzl` does the same.
- `tools/testing/consumer/cold_start_test.rs`: `UPSTREAM_REGISTERED` keeps `rules_android+` for every case.

## Fix
1. Move `JvmAndroidSdkInfo` and `android_sdk_jars` to a load-free `java/private/quality/jvm_info.bzl`.
2. Move `jvm_android_sdk_aspect` to `android/private/quality/android_sdk.bzl`, together with the `@rules_android` load and the SDK toolchain. Give android/lang.json a quality entry that runs this aspect before the JVM aspects when a workspace has Android targets.
3. The javac, kotlinc and spotbugs paths read `JvmAndroidSdkInfo` through `required_aspect_providers` instead of `requires`.
4. Add a test showing that an `android_library` still gets android.jar on its javac and kotlinc classpath. Remove `rules_android+` from java.txt once #14357 lands.

issues.body:
## Where

`.github/workflows/reusable-consumer.yml` has validate, checks, advisory-snapshots, security-audit and dx-ci jobs (`:66,122,434,492,551`) and `permissions: contents: read` (`:49-50`). No job runs `dx deploy`. The deploy README shows `GH_RELEASE_LIVE=1 GH_RELEASE_APPROVED=1 dx deploy --apply //pkg:github_demo` typed by hand (`deploy/rules/README.md:414`), `npm_deploy(provenance = "required")` needs an OIDC identity (`:130`), and `docs/github-ci.md` has no release section. A consumer that wants to publish from CI writes the workflow from scratch; the starter `ci.yml` (`cli/adopt/src/scaffold.rs:355-363`) does not mention it.

## Fix

- `.github/workflows/reusable-release.yml` (`workflow_call`, meant for `on: push: tags: ['v*']`): inputs `deployables` (JSON list of labels, default: every `dx_deployment` tagged `release` found with `bazel query 'attr(tags, "release", kind(dx_deployment, //...))'`), `platforms`; `permissions: contents: write, id-token: write, attestations: write, packages: write`; `secrets: inherit`.
- Steps: checkout the tag, `dx deploy <label>` (dry run) for each deployable, then `dx deploy --apply <label>` with `<REG>_LIVE=1` and `<REG>_PUBLISH_APPROVED=1` set from the tag event, in the order the list gives. A failed deployable stops the rest and the summary names the ones already published.
- `dx init` writes `.github/workflows/release.yml` calling it (next to `ci.yml` and `dx-update.yml`); `input_validation.rs` covers the new inputs; a `docs/github-ci.md` release section.

## Done when

- A starter consumer with a `github_deploy` tagged `release` publishes a draft release when `v0.1.0` is pushed, with the dry run visible in the job log before the live run.

issues.body:
Part of #12607. The lua rules layer must name no dx-layer target, or the in-tree `rules_lua` module cannot resolve its labels. After the core rules move into `lua/private/lua.bzl`, one such label is left: the core `lua_test` pulls luacov in through a private attribute. The load guard does not see it because it only reads `load()` calls.

## Where

- `lua/private/lua.bzl:121`: `_collect` adds `ctx.attr._coverage` to the deps.
- `lua/private/lua.bzl:222-226`: `_coverage` defaults to `//lua/private/coverage:libs`, which is dx layer (`@dx_luacov`, `@dx_luacov_reporter_lcov`, `dx_coverage.lua`).
- `lua/private/runtime/launcher.cc:23,262`: the launcher starts a module named `dx_coverage` when the entry file lists it.
- `tools/ci/rule_set_loads_test.rs`: only `load()` labels are checked. A `Label()` or attribute default in a rule-set file that names a non-rule-set package or a `@dx_*` repo passes.

## Fix

- The core `lua_test` has no `_coverage` attribute. Core executables return a provider with their entry data (main rlocation, owning repo, module map), so a wrapper can write its own entry file.
- The dx test forwarder in `lua/private/defs.bzl` writes `<name>.luaentry` itself under `bazel coverage` only: the upstream entry data plus the modules of `//lua/private/coverage:enabled`, with their runfiles. Outside coverage it keeps symlinking the upstream entry. Luacov sources stay out of `InstrumentedFilesInfo` (`.dx/bazelrc/correctness.bazelrc:36` sets `--instrumentation_filter=^//`, so they must not be in `deps`).
- The launcher hook name `dx_coverage` is documented as the public coverage hook of the rule set in `lua/private/providers.bzl` next to `LUA_ENTRY_FORMAT`.
- `rule_set_loads_test` gets a `foreign-label` kind: a label string in a rule-set file whose package is not a rule-set package of that language, or whose repo starts with `dx_`. Current hits (php, qt) go in the shrink-only allowlist.

Tests: `bazel coverage //lua/tests/...` gives the same LCOV records as befor

issues.body:
## Problem
`release.yml` has never run, and neither has `publish-dry-run.yml`. The dry run also skips the parts most likely to break: `actions/attest`, `gh attestation verify`, `gh release upload` and the post-upload `dx install` check. The first real tag would be the first time these run.

## Where
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:190-305` (upload job: attest, verify, upload, install check)
- `.github/workflows/publish-dry-run.yml:28-155` (no attest, verify or upload)
- `gh run list -R devhusdk/rules_dx --workflow release.yml` and `--workflow publish-dry-run.yml` show no runs

## Fix
- Run `release.yml` end to end on a fork with a throwaway tag and matching `DX_VERSION`, through draft, attest, verify, upload and `dx install`.
- Fix what breaks, and record the run in `RELEASING.md` (or #1862).
- Run `publish-dry-run.yml` once on main.

## Done when
- A fork run of `release.yml` succeeds and its release holds the ten dx assets, the manifest, the bundle and the source archive.
- `gh attestation verify` passes against that fork release from a clean machine.
- `publish-dry-run.yml` has a green run on main.


Related: #4861 (RELEASING.md). Needs a fork, tags and GitHub Actions runs, so an agent cannot start it.

issues.body:
Part of #13149. Found while planning #14273.

`docs/design/tool-prebuilts.md` (Licences) says every redistributed asset ships the upstream licence text. The native tools the release cells build ship none: `dx-capnp-*` (MIT), `dx-flatc-*` (Apache-2.0), `dx-thrift-*` (Apache-2.0), and, once #14273 lands, `dx-ldoc-main-*` (links Lua, MIT, whose notice lives in `lua.h`, and LuaFileSystem, MIT). `dx-oapi-codegen-LICENSE` and the tree-sitter `Library.licenses` are the precedent.

## Where

- `tools/ci/producers/src/release_cell.rs:17` `NATIVE_TOOLS` carries no licence labels; `write_library_license` (`:252`) only handles `Library`.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:124` (per-cell tool loop), `:155-157` (licence lines), `:206` (manifest line count).
- `tools/ci/release_tools_workflow_test.rs:456-461`, `tools/ci/fill_pins/tests/fill_pins_test.rs:44` (manifest companions).
- Licence file exports: `lua/private/luafilesystem.BUILD.bazel`, plus the capnproto, flatbuffers and thrift repo BUILD overlays.

## Fix

- Give each `NATIVE_TOOLS` entry its upstream licence labels (same shape as `Library.licenses`) and write `dx-<tool>-LICENSE` from one cell only (linux-x86_64), so the five cells do not each upload a copy.
- Lua ships no LICENSE file: ship the copyright block from `lua.h`, through a checked-in or extracted file.
- List the `dx-<tool>-LICENSE` files in the dx manifest in `release.yml`, bump the line count, and update the workflow and fill_pins tests. fill_pins already accepts LICENSE companions.

issues.body:
## What

`//tools/testing/consumer:cold_start_test` (merged in #14335 for #14332) fails on linux_x86_64. Evidence run 44857712024: `go_fetches_only_its_cold_start_list` and `rust_fetches_only_its_cold_start_list` both panic at `tools/testing/consumer/cold_start_test.rs:149`. The two unit tests pass.

## Where

- `tools/testing/consumer/cold_start/go.txt`, `tools/testing/consumer/cold_start/rust.txt`: the lists are stale.
  - go: "no longer fetched" for aspect_rules_js+, aspect_rules_ts+, rules_dx++dx_pins+rules_{d,elixir,erlang,fortran,haskell}, rules_dx++toolchain+julia_toolchains, rules_m4+, rules_m4++default_toolchain_ext+m4.
  - rust: "new fetch" for rules_go++go_sdk+io_bazel_rules_nogo and many rules_rust++i2+rrc__* crates (thiserror-1.0.69, autocfg, icu_*, ...).
- Both cases: foreign fetches of rules_android+, rules_cuda+, rules_kotlin+, rules_scala+ (rust also rules_dx++ocaml+dx_ocaml_toolchains). These are the real regressions the test guards.

## Fix

1. Find why a go-only or rust-only consumer fetches rules_android+, rules_cuda+, rules_kotlin+, rules_scala+ (and ocaml for rust). Stop those fetches; don't add them to the lists.
2. Check whether the rust case fetches rules_go++go_sdk+io_bazel_rules_nogo because the go case ran first on the same server/repository cache (`tools/testing/nested/src/record.rs:139-181`), or because rust really needs it.
3. Regenerate go.txt and rust.txt from a CI evidence run, then set the measured time in `tools/testing/nested_smoke.txt` (currently 60).

Proof: evidence.yml on linux_x86_64 with scope `//tools/testing/consumer:cold_start_test`, `--test_timeout=2400`.

issues.body:
Part of #14055. With \`--//cli/prebuilt:guard_view\`, \`bazel run //tools/testing/consumer:in_graph_prebuilt_guard -- --langs julia\` on main reports:

\`\`\`
julia: compiles cc_binary rule @@rules_dx++dx_pins+julia_src//:flisp (cbc5e80)
julia: compiles cc_binary rule @@rules_dx+//julia/private/runtime:libjulia-internal.so.1.13.4 (3046191)
julia: compiles cc_binary rule @@rules_dx+//julia/private/runtime:libjulia-internal.so.1.13.4 (86fbb58)
\`\`\`

So every Julia consumer on linux_x86_64 builds the Julia runtime from source, and julia stays in \`GUARD_PENDING\`.

## Where
- \`julia/private/runtime/BUILD.bazel\` (\`:stock\` flag, \`:source_runtime\`, \`:source_toolchain\`, the \`libjulia-internal\` \`cc_binary\`).
- \`julia/private/runtime/julia_src.BUILD.bazel\` (\`flisp\`), the \`julia_src\` archive in \`MODULE.bazel\` \`dx_pins\`.
- \`cli/prebuilt/tools.bzl\` (\`TOOLS\`), \`tools/testing/consumer/fixtures.bzl\` (\`GUARD_PENDING\`).
- Related: #13965, #13448, #14104.

## Fix
- Ship the source-built \`libjulia-internal.so\` for linux_x86_64 as a release-cell prebuilt in the \`dx_prebuilt\` hub, and have \`:source_julia\` take the hub file under \`guard_view\` and in consumers, so neither \`flisp\` nor the library compiles there.
- Move \`julia\` from \`GUARD_PENDING\` to \`IN_GRAPH_GUARD_LANGS\`.

Done when \`in_graph_prebuilt_guard --langs julia\` prints \`julia: 0 compiled rules_dx binaries\`.

Closes #14332

Merges `go_cold_start_test` and `rust_cold_start_test` into one literally named nested target, `//tools/testing/consumer:cold_start_test`. It has one `#[test]` per language (`go_fetches_only_its_cold_start_list`, `rust_fetches_only_its_cold_start_list`). Each test runs its own `Case`, so each language gets a fresh workspace and output base on the shared server. `nested_smoke.txt` drops from 9 lines to 8, and the guard can now read the target name. Before this change it reported both loop targets as "no nested test left". `NESTED_CAP` and the allowlist are unchanged.

- `tools/testing/consumer/BUILD.bazel`: one `nested_bazel_test`. `DX_COLD_START_LISTS` replaces `DX_COLD_START_LANG` and `DX_COLD_START_LIST`.
- `tools/testing/consumer/cold_start_test.rs`: adds the shared helper and two per-language tests, plus the new unit test `every_cold_start_list_has_foreign_fragments`.
- `tools/testing/consumer/cold_start/{go,rust}.txt`: the header now names the new target.
- `tools/testing/nested_smoke.txt`: `//tools/testing/consumer:cold_start_test 60`. 60 is the declared small timeout; the target has not been timed yet.

## Verification
- `bazel test //tools/ci:test_budget_test`: no nested-list lines remain. The test still fails, on 27 `no-size ... make the test small` lines, all in files this PR does not touch (core/tests, flatbuffers, qt, ...). That failure already exists on main.
- `bazel run //tools/testing/consumer:cold_start_test -- growth_shrinkage every_cold_start_list`: 2 passed.
- `tools/dx check --apply --affected`: no findings in the touched files. 22 warnings, all in untouched files.

Every macos_arm64 evidence run fails at "Validate workflow inputs" before any test runs:

```
ERROR: Analysis of target '//tools/ci/producers:producers_bin' failed; build aborted: MODULE.bazel.lock is no longer up-to-date because the usages of the extension '@@rules_go+//go:extensions.bzl%go_sdk' have changed. Please run `bazel mod deps --lockfile_mode=update` to update your lockfile.
```

Seen in runs 44837783268, 44837787074 (PR #14292) and 44837721553 (quality-objc-curated).

## Where
`MODULE.bazel.lock`, `moduleExtensions["@@rules_go+//go:extensions.bzl%go_sdk"]` on origin/main (47d92489d8): only `os:linux,arch:amd64` has the current `usagesDigest` (`sVl7lycX...`). `os:osx,arch:aarch64`, `os:linux,arch:aarch64`, `os:windows,arch:amd64` and `os:windows,arch:aarch64` still have the old one (`g9Q8VSWe...`). `git log -S` puts the linux-only refresh at 44fc0dd81d (#13812).

## Fix
- Run lock-refresh.yml on a branch from main so it regenerates the non-linux_x86_64 go_sdk entries (tools/ci/lock_merge.sh), and merge the result.
- Make the stale-entry guard from #11010 fail when the per-platform go_sdk `usagesDigest` values disagree, so a linux-only refresh can't land again.

agent_prs.title: quality: regal lint refuses URL capabilities and runs remotely (closes #14277, part of #14095)

issues.body:
Part of #14095 and #13209. `regal lint` stays in `PENDING` because a bound Regal config can make it read the network or undeclared files. Since Regal v0.26.0, `capabilities.from.url` fetches a capabilities JSON over http(s), and `capabilities.from.file` reads a path that the action may not declare as an input. The runner passes the bound config to regal unchanged, so neither case is caught. `REGAL_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1` already stops the update check.

## Where

- `core/quality/runner/src/real/config_tools.rs:32-66`: the `regal` `ToolDef` stages `.regal/` and runs `commands::regal_lint` with the bound config, without reading it.
- `core/quality/adapter/src/commands.rs:3027-3039` `regal_lint`.
- `core/quality/adapter/src/commands.rs:3190-3300`: `kubeconform_config` already refuses remote schema locations. Follow this pattern.
- `rego/private/quality/rego.bzl:13-19`: the regal tool entry, which sets `REGAL_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK`.
- `core/quality/execution_requirements.bzl:160`: `("regal", "lint")` in `PENDING`.

## Fix

1. Add `regal_config_error(config, bytes)` to the adapter. It parses the YAML and returns an error when `capabilities.from.url` is set, or when `capabilities.from.file` is absolute or climbs out of the config's directory with `..`. Call it in the regal `ToolDef` before the spawn, and fail with that message. Add adapter unit tests for url, absolute file, `..` file, an allowed relative file and a config with no capabilities section.
2. Move `("regal", "lint")` from `PENDING` to `REMOTE_QUALIFIED`. Add a check in `core/quality/execution_requirements_tests.bzl` that the regal lint stage returns `{}`. Add regal to the list in `docs/remote-execution.md`. Note in the regal config docs that URL capabilities are refused.

agent_prs.body:
Closes #11151

The last item of #11151: `tools/testing/hermetic/consumers/cuda/consumer.bazelrc` (`common:windows --@my_dx//cc:compiler=msvc`) is deleted. On Windows, CUDA code compiles and links with msvc without any consumer flag.

## Design
- `cuda_host_transition` (cuda/private/toolchain/transition.bzl) now also writes `//cc:compiler` from the forward rule's `host_compiler` attr. That attr is `msvc` on `@platforms//os:windows` and empty elsewhere; empty keeps the current compiler, so Linux and macOS are unchanged.
- `cuda_binary` and `cuda_test` are now forward rules (`_cuda_binary_forward`, `_cuda_forward_test`). Their upstream edge applies `cuda_host_transition`, so on Windows the whole executable builds and links with cl.exe: the host `.cc` sources, the nvcc compile and every CUDA dep. MSVC STL objects are never linked by clang-cl + libc++ (the `lld-link: undefined symbol ... std::__1::basic_string ... greet` failure in run 44290568436).
- On Windows, `cuda_library` and `cuda_objects` are compatible only under `//cc:compiler=msvc` (`//cuda/private/toolchain:windows_msvc`). A plain `cc_binary`/`cc_test` under the default llvm compiler can't take one, so a mixed link fails analysis instead of failing at link time.
- The cuda fixtures (`saxpy`, `cublas`, `rdc`, `cuda_app`) link through `cuda_binary` instead of `cc_binary`.
- `CUDA_COMPATIBLE_WITH` drops the `cell_windows_*_msvc` groups.
- The CUDA test forwarder and `_cc_forward_test` share the coverage attrs and toolchains through `CC_TEST_COVERAGE_ATTRS`/`CC_TEST_COVERAGE_TOOLCHAINS` in `cc/private/defs.bzl`.
- The conformance runner also mirrors runfiles for `<name>_upstream_upstream`, because the native binary of a `cuda_test` sits two forward layers down and its RUNPATH points there.

- `cuda/private/gpu/gpu_guard.cc` prints the arm64 registers (`X0`-`X3`, `Sp`) on Windows arm64, where `CONTEXT` has no `Rcx`. It now builds there because CUDA targets no longer need `//cc:compiler=msvc`.

issues.body:
A cross \`dart compile exe\` (for example linux x64 to linux arm64) calls dartdev's \`SdkCache.resolveVersion\` with the SDK's \`revision\` file even when the toolchain's \`sdk_cache\` already holds the target's \`gen_snapshot\` and \`dartaotruntime\`. rules_dart 0.9.1 does not list \`revision\` in the \`aot_compile\` SDK file set. Where only declared inputs exist, such as remote execution, the action fails with:

\`\`\`
Invalid argument(s): Channel "stable" requires valid revision.
#0      SdkCache.resolveVersion (package:dartdev/src/sdk_cache.dart:100)
\`\`\`

Seen in evidence run 44232005167 (linux_x86_64, \`//dart/tests/conformance:hello_upstream\`). rules_dx carries \`patches/rules_dart/cross_revision.patch\`, which adds \`revision\` to \`aot_compile\`. Consumers that cross-compile Dart remotely need the same fix until rules_dart ships it. Then drop the patch.

Part of #13722, follows #14064. The lock resolvers that `setup.hubs[].resolver` names in `lang.json` are `rust_binary` targets with no release asset. A consumer compiles one on its first `dx update` or `dx generate` for that ecosystem. #14064 leaves them out of the guard roots because every guard would fail on them today.

## Where

- Run by `cli/update/src/backend/resolver.rs:4` (`dx update`) and `cli/cli/src/exec/generate.rs:156` (`dx generate`)

issues.body:
On linux-x86_64, building `//rust/private/quality/tools:deadnix` with `release-tools.yml`'s flags and no cache fails at link time:

```
bazel build --remote_cache= --disk_cache= --@rules_rust//rust/settings:extra_rustc_flag=-Ctarget-feature=+crt-static //rust/private/quality/tools:deadnix
...
"-static-pie" ... "-no-pie" ...
clang++: error: cannot specify 'nopie' along with 'static-pie'
```

With `+crt-static`, rustc asks for `-static-pie`, and the hermetic LLVM cc toolchain's link flags add `-no-pie`. The `tools` job only passes today when the remote cache already holds the outputs. Because of this, `//tools/testing:determinism_check` (which builds without caches) can't run on that job.

## Where
- `.github/workflows/release-tools.yml:52` (`flags` for `linux-*`)
- The `-no-pie` link flag in the hermetic LLVM cc toolchain (`llvm+` toolchain config)

## Fix
- Make the crt-static Rust link consistent: either have the toolchain drop `-no-pie` when the link is `-static-pie`, or switch the release flags to a non-PIE static link (`-Crelocation-model=static`) and check that the `readelf` INTERP check still passes.
- Then add `bazel run //tools/testing:determinism_check -- --bazel "$(command -v bazel)" --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/determinism-rust" "${flags[@]}" //rust/private/quality/tools:deadnix //rust/private/quality/tools:selene //rust/private/quality/tools:topiary //rust/private/quality/tools:progenitor` inside the `tools` job's `linux-*)` arm, plus its row in `JOB_DETERMINISM` (`tools/ci/release_tools_workflow_test.rs`).

Part of #11411 and #11416. The #11411 first slice replaces `patches/rules_rust/rust_lld_msvc_libpath.patch` with `patches/llvm/msvc_link_lib_env.patch`. That patch makes llvm's clang-cl toolchain set `LIB` on MSVC link actions to the hermetic CRT, Windows SDK and libc++ dirs. Unpatched rules_rust 0.75.0 already turns cc link env `LIB` into `-LIBPATH:` (`rust/private/rustc.bzl` `get_linker_and_args`, bazelbuild/rules_rust#3256), so rust-lld finds `kernel32.lib`. Consumers get unpatched BCR llvm, so the patch has to go upstream.

## Where
- `patches/llvm/msvc_link_lib_env.patch`, `MODULE.bazel` llvm `single_version_override`, `patches/README.md` llvm rows
- `cli/adopt/src/overrides.rs` llvm entry, `families/{jvm,beam}/third_party/rules_dx/`

## Fix
- Open the hermetic-llvm PR with the patch content, and link it in the `patches/README.md` row and on #11416.
- When a BCR llvm release includes it, bump `llvm` in `MODULE.bazel` and the adopt override, then delete the patch, its BUILD export, its family copies and its README row.
- Check: `//rust/tests/fixtures/native_call:native_call_bin_link_windows_test` passes on windows_x86_64 with no llvm or rules_rust patch for this.

## What
- `core/toolchain.bzl`: `is_sha256` and `digest_problems`, an iterative walker that checks every `sha256` (a digest or a dict of digests) and `urls` (non-empty list of `https://` urls) at any depth. `pin_checks` uses `is_sha256`.
- `core/tests/pins_tests.bzl`: one `digests and urls` check per PINS, DATA and ARCHIVES entry; the shallow sha256/https checks go.
