- Deleted the dead `deploy/private/{release,pins}/repos.bzl` stubs and their BUILD and allowlist entries (allowlist shrinks by 3 lines).

## Why this closes the umbrella
The remaining items keep their own acquisition: LDC, OTP, GHC, OCaml and PHP cells, msix, appimage and cuda already use `cell_repo`, `pins_hub`, `pinned_archive` and `pins.json`; what is left is fetch logic specific to one language (7z + addon overlay + deb closure for D, a license gate used only by msix, appimage must run itself to extract). agent_prs.body:
Closes #11186

This is the last slice. The cc windows_x86_64 item was done in #13479. zig on Windows/macOS moved to #14150, rules_erlang patch 08 upstreaming moved to #14151, and Apple and msix stay pending.

## Problem
nvcc hands the host side of `greet.cu` to clang as `/tmp/tmpxft_*_greet.compute_120.cudafe1.cpp`. Clang source-based coverage ignores the `#line` markers in that file, so every hit was filed under the temp file and `coverage_test` failed with `no SF: for greet.cu`.

## Change

agent_prs.body:
## Linked Issue

Closes #14143

## Changes

- `dx_testing` fork guard now has three sides. `forking()` (new) is for tests that only spawn. These tests share the guard with each other and never run during a `holding()` test. `holding()` tests share with each other and never run during a spawn. `spawning()` stays exclusive, for tests that hold a lock and also spawn. Peers can't join a running group while another side is waiting, so no side starves. Pure state tests and a threaded test cover this.
- Every `cli/process` test that starts a child now takes `forking()`: 104 tests. I found them by running each test under `strace -f` and checking for fork/vfork clones, then added the Windows-only spawners by reading the code. The 7 tests that hold a lease and spawn keep `spawning()`.
- 12 slot-pool and group-lease tests that hold file locks take `holding()`. This includes `a_read_only_slot_file_locks_exclusive_and_reports_contention`, which drops a lock and expects it free.
- The existing `spawning()` callers in `cli/atomic_fs`, `cli/setup` and `deploy/private` are unchanged, and their tests still pass.

Making every spawning test exclusive would have serialized about 40s of tests inside the 60s `small` timeout. The shared `forking` side keeps the run at about 20s.

## Verification

`tools/dx check --apply` ran on the touched files: formatting was applied and no findings were reported.

Tested: `//cli/process:dx_process_test --runs_per_test=30` (30/30 passed), `//tools/testing:dx_testing_test --runs_per_test=10`, `//cli/process:test_srcs_split_test`, `//cli/atomic_fs:dx_atomic_fs_test`, `//cli/setup:dx_setup_test`, `//deploy/private:dx_deploy_tools_test`. All passed.

issues.body:
Part of #14080, follows the PR that gives `dx_subcommand` `path_args` and `data` and moves the java resolver to `dx java_lock`. The csharp, dart, haskell and swift lock resolvers are still `rust_binary` targets that read their pinned tool through `$(rlocationpath ...)` env vars, so every consumer compiles them on its first `dx update` or `dx generate` for that ecosystem.

## Where
- `csharp/private/tools/lock/BUILD.bazel:28` (`DOTNET`, `PAKET`), `src/main.rs`, `Cargo.toml` `[[bin]]`
- `dart/private/tools/lock/BUILD.bazel:20` (`DX_DART`), `src/main.rs` (uses `@rules_rust//rust/runfiles`)
- `haskell/private/tools/lock/BUILD.bazel:29` (`DX_CABAL`, `DX_GHC`, data `//haskell:ghc_files`), `src/main.rs`
- `swift/private/tools/lock/BUILD.bazel:28` (`SWIFT`), `src/main.rs`
- `cli/cli/src/multicall.rs`, `cli/cli/src/main.rs` (`run_as_tool`), `cli/cli/BUILD.bazel` (`:dx` deps)

## Fix
- Move each `main.rs` body into its lib as `pub fn run_process(args: &[String]) -> i32`, reading its tools with `dx_lock::tool_paths` (`--dotnet`/`--paket`, `--dart`, `--cabal`/`--ghc`, `--swift`) and passing the rest to `dx_lock::run_process` (dart: its own `--dir`/`--check` loop).
- Replace each `rust_binary(name = "lock")` with `dx_subcommand(name = "lock", subcommand = "<lang>_lock", path_args = {...}, data = [...])`, keeping its `target_compatible_with`; delete `src/main.rs`, its `[[bin]]` and `exports_files` entry; repin `cargo-bazel-lock.json`.
- Add `csharp_lock`, `dart_lock`, `haskell_lock`, `swift_lock` to the dx multicall and its tests.

Done when: no `rust_binary` is left in the four lock packages and `bazel run //<lang>/private/tools/lock:lock -- --check --dir=<dir>` runs through `dx <lang>_lock`.

issues.body:
Part of #13209. Vale on AsciiDoc and reST runs a converter (asciidoctor, rst2html) found on its PATH. Those converters are runfiles launchers, and the slice that qualifies vale keeps any stage with runfiles launchers local-only.

## Where

- `core/quality/execution_requirements.bzl` `dx_stage_execution_requirements`: the `run_tools` rule that keeps converter stages local.
- `core/quality/runner/src/real.rs:146-165`: `own_runfiles_manifest` sets `RUNFILES_MANIFEST_FILE` for `rst2html` (`ALWAYS_OWN_MANIFEST`) even when the manifest file is missing. Bazel does not stage the runfiles manifest for remote actions, so the launcher would look up a file that is not there.
- `core/quality/families/core.bzl:131-148`: `_vale_hook` passes the converters as `run_tools` and `path_tools`.
- `javascript/private/quality/bin/BUILD.bazel` `asciidoctor` (js_binary) and `core/quality/tools/python/BUILD.bazel` `rst2html` (py_binary).

## Fix

1. In the runner, set `RUNFILES_MANIFEST_FILE` only when the manifest beside the binary exists; otherwise set `RUNFILES_DIR` to `<binary>.runfiles`. Add a runner unit test where the manifest is missing.
2. Lift the `run_tools` rule for the vale converters (keep it for other runfiles launchers until each is checked), add unit tests that vale stages with converters lose `no-remote-exec`, and update `docs/remote-execution.md`.

issues.body:
Part of #13722, follows #14077. Consumers compile the `rules_dx` Rust binary `@rules_dx//dx/tool_resolve` from source to find the pinned Gitleaks. The `dx audit` hint tells users to run it locally, and the reusable consumer workflow runs it in CI. #14077 roots it in the prebuilt guards and allowlists `@@rules_dx+//dx/tool_resolve:tool_resolve` with a reason that points here.

## Where
- `cli/audit/src/secrets.rs` (`resolve_command()`, the hint printed by `cli/exec_audit/src/lib.rs`)
- `.github/workflows/reusable-consumer.yml` (step "Resolve hermetic Gitleaks": `bazel run @rules_dx//dx/tool_resolve -- --label @rules_dx//core/quality/artifacts:gitleaks ...`)
- `dx/tool_resolve/BUILD.bazel` (marked "Maintainer runnable", but users run it); `cli/tool_resolve` (the library, which the prebuilt `dx` already links)
- `cli/families/src/lib.rs` (`TOOL_RESOLVE` in `COMMAND_TARGETS`), `tools/testing/consumer/prebuilt_guard_allowlist.txt`

## Fix
- Do the resolve through the prebuilt `dx`, for example with a hidden `dx` subcommand that prints `DX_GITLEAKS_BIN=<path>` using `dx_tool_resolve`. Point the `secrets.rs` hint and the reusable-consumer step at it, so no consumer builds `dx/tool_resolve`.
- Remove `TOOL_RESOLVE` from `dx_families::COMMAND_TARGETS` and drop the allowlist line. The stale check in the guards then confirms nothing compiles it.
- Keep `dx/tool_resolve` as a maintainer-only target, or delete it if nothing else runs it (`tools/ci/tool_resolve_test.rs`).

Done when: the go and java prebuilt guards and the in-graph guard pass with no `dx/tool_resolve` allowlist line.

issues.body:
Part of #13722. The prebuilt guard runs `cquery 'deps(...)'`, which follows rule attributes only. The aspects that `dx check` and `dx docs` apply on the command line are not followed, so a rules_dx tool that only an aspect reaches can be built from source and the guard does not notice. Examples: `_javac_check`, `_kotlinc_check` and `_scalac_check` on `jvm_check_aspect`, and `_java_extract` and `_jvm_convert` on `real_jvm_docs_aspect`.

## Where
- `tools/testing/consumer/prebuilt_guard_test.rs` (the single `cquery --output=label_kind` call)
- `java/private/quality/jvm_check.bzl:436-466` (`jvm_check_aspect` tool attrs)
- `tools/docs/jvm/aspect.bzl:31-45` (`real_jvm_docs_aspect` tool attrs)
- The aspects `dx check` and `dx docs` apply, for every language (find them where the CLI builds its `--aspects` list)

## Fix
- First check whether the pinned Bazel's `cquery` honours `--aspects`. If it does, add the `dx check` and `dx docs` aspects to the guard's cquery. If it does not, run `aquery --aspects=<same list> 'deps(<roots>)' --output=jsonproto` and map each action's owner to a target.
- Fail on any compiled `rules_dx+` binary those aspects reach that `prebuilt_guard_allowlist.txt` does not name. Use the same rules as the cquery pass.
- Keep each guard at 60 s or less (`tools/ci/test_budget_test`).

Done when: pointing `_javac_check` back at `@rules_dx//java/private/quality/tools/javac_check` makes `java_prebuilt_guard_test` fail.

Part of #13808

- `write_bcr_source_for_archive` returns `Result<String, BcrError>`. The new `BcrError::Hash { path, source }` covers the archive digest. The write goes through `path_io::write_scratch` into `BcrError::Io`. Both `io::Error::other` wraps are gone.

issues.body:
Follow-up to #14044. Part of #13181.

## Where

- `gazelle/rust/lang_resolve.go:41-49` resolves only `use runfiles::` to a built-in label. A `use prost::`, `use prost_types::` or `use tonic::` next to a `rust_prost_library` resolves through the user's `@crates` hub, or not at all, so it can pick a prost or tonic that differs from the one `rules_rust_prost` links into the generated crate, and the derive and trait do not match.
- In this repo the root `BUILD.bazel` (`# gazelle:resolve rust prost ...`) and `tools/docs/protobuf/extract/BUILD.bazel:1` (`prost_types`) carry `gazelle:resolve` directives only to work around this.

## Fix

- When the root MODULE.bazel depends on `rules_rust_prost`, resolve `prost`, `prost_types` and `tonic` to `@rules_dx//rust:prost`, `:prost_types` and `:tonic` by default, the way `runfiles` resolves to `@rules_rust//rust/runfiles`. A `gazelle:resolve` directive still wins.
- Add a `gazelle/rust/testdata` case: a crate that uses `prost::Message` on a `rust_prost_library` type gets `@rules_dx//rust:prost` with no directive.
- Drop the two in-repo `gazelle:resolve` directives above and check `tools/dx generate` leaves BUILD files unchanged.

issues.body:
Found while planning #13961. `release_tool inventory` only accepts license words that ship inside a crate (LICENSE*/COPYING*/NOTICE* at the crate root, or `_BUNDLED_TEXTS`). When a crate ships none, the only way out is a license.toml `[[exception]]`, and the NOTICE then says "ships no license text; declared license: ...". For MIT and BSD crates the copyright and permission notice is still not reproduced. Each exception also expires after a year and has to be renewed. license.toml already has `[[inventory]]` entries with `text` (vendored words, see cli/audit/src/license_policy.rs:191), and `dx audit license` honors them. The release inventory ignores them.

## Where
- deploy/private/release/inventory.bzl:95-180, `_shipped_inventory_impl` and `_shipped_inventory` (only `_lock` and `_licenses` are inputs; vendored texts never reach the action)
- deploy/private/release/src/inventory.rs:347 `join`, :387 `read_crate_texts` (reads only aspect texts; `policy.inventory` is unused)
- license.toml, the cargo `[[exception]]` entries (allocative ... strong_hash, cxx-qt, cxx-qt-gen)

## Fix
- Add a `vendored_texts` label_list attr to `_shipped_inventory`, defaulting to a new `//:license_texts` filegroup, and pass its paths to the action.
- In `join`, when a crate has no aspect texts and a `[[inventory]]` entry with `set = "cargo"`, a matching package, `versions` and `text` exists, read that file as the crate's words. Fail if the `text` path is not among the inputs.
- Vendor upstream words for the MIT/BSD crates (cxx-qt: KDAB/cxx-qt LICENSES/MIT.txt and Apache-2.0.txt at the v0.10.0 tag), replace their exceptions with `[[inventory]]` entries, and add an inventory.rs unit test plus an `inventory_file_tests` case with `texts_contain`.

The Apple family asks for the most `MODULE.bazel` typing of any family: `apple/README.md` has 7 `use_extension`, 6 `use_repo` and 6 `register_toolchains` lines. Swift on macOS needs none.

## Where

- `apple/README.md` repeats this block four times (probe, iOS libraries, simulator apps, Swift apps):
  ```python

issues.body:
In record mode (`--config=nested_record`), a nested test binary that fails on windows_x86_64 writes no `test.outputs/nested_cache` record. Linux and macOS write theirs. In evidence.yml run 44480178184 (branch `issue-13353-nested-rerecord`):
- `release_consumer_smoke_test`: 2 of 3 cases passed on every host. The linux and macOS artifacts have `release.txt` with `release_bcr` and `release_candidate` locks. The Windows artifact has none.
- `examples/adopt-polyglot:consumer_test` (red on Windows because of #13788): no Windows record.
- `nested_bazel_harness_test` passed on Windows and was recorded.

So a re-record merged with `nested_cache_update --from` loses the Windows-only URLs of every set whose Windows test is red. `lock-refresh.yml` with `nested=true` skips the merge whenever any record test fails.

## Where
- `tools/testing/nested/src/lib.rs:1305` `release_at_exit` registers the C `atexit` hook, and `:1323` `release` calls `finish_record` (`:1360`). That hook is the only place the record gets written.
- When a test fails, the libtest harness exits through `std::process::exit(101)`. On Windows that is `ExitProcess`, which most likely skips the CRT `atexit` table of the executable. A passing binary returns from `main`, so the hook runs.

## Fix
- Write the record without depending on `atexit`. For example, flush it from the `Drop` of a recorded case, which also runs during panic unwinding: rewrite `<set>.txt` and the stem locks from every case recorded so far, so the last flush wins. Keep the `atexit` flush as a fallback.
- Test: a record-mode unit test that runs a failing case and asserts that the record files exist. Then an evidence.yml windows_x86_64 run with `--config=nested_record` where one failing case still uploads its record.
issues.title: nested: record mode writes no cache set when a test binary fails on Windows

issues.body:
Follow-up to #13828, part of #13181. #13828 narrows the maintainer runnables and root filegroups. The two `core/` packages still default every rule target to public, so their test fixtures show up as `@rules_dx//core/quality:*` and `@rules_dx//core/modules:*` labels.

## Where

- `core/quality/BUILD.bazel:36` `package(default_visibility = ["//visibility:public"])` makes these public: the policy fixtures (`quality_family`, `workspace_policy`, `policy_subject`, `dx_generated_policy` at `:72`-`:176`), `fixture_real_rust_converters` (`:583`), `no_converters` (`:589`), the `linux_x86_64`/`windows_x86_64` config_settings (`:651`, `:659`), the test_suites (`:716`-`:785`), `corpus_vale_config` (`:810`) and `unsupported_tool_platform` (`:913`).
- `core/modules/BUILD.bazel:10` does the same for `lang_projections_generated` (`:133`), `all` (`:219`) and the corpus targets (`:247`, `:271`).
- Consumer files only load `.bzl` files from these packages (`.dx/BUILD.bazel:4`, `cli/generate`). `exports_files` and each `.bzl` file's `visibility()` control those loads, not `default_visibility`.

## Fix

- In both packages, set `package(default_visibility = ["//:__subpackages__"])`.
- Run `bazel build --nobuild //...`. Any in-repo edge that breaks gets a narrow explicit `visibility`. For example, `lang_projections_generated` needs the five packages that read its `generated/*` outputs: `cli/ecosystems`, `cli/families`, `core/quality/testdata`, `gazelle/common` and `tools/testing/conformance`.
- Leave `exports_files` as it is. It stays public whatever the package default is.
- Run `bazel run //tools/api:update` and check that `api/labels.txt` loses no user label.

Done when: no rule target in `core/quality` or `core/modules` is public. Size S.

issues.body:
`dx init` writes `.github/workflows/release.yml` only when a BUILD file declares a deployment (#9427). The check is a text search for the bare rule call, so a repo that uses only the `*_deploy` macros (`npm_deploy`, `github_deploy`, `oci_deploy`, ...) never gets `release.yml`, though every one of those macros creates a deployment target. Most users only call the macros.

## Where

- `docs/cli/commands/init.md:226`, `docs/github-ci.md:29`: describe the gate.

## Fix

- Count a BUILD file as declaring a deployment when it loads `@rules_dx//deploy:defs.bzl` (or `//deploy:defs.bzl`) and calls a loaded symbol that is `deployment` or ends in `_deploy`. issues.body:
Part of #13206.

## Where

- `core/stage.bzl:5` `stage_closure` declares one symlink per schema file it is given.

- Remove the capnproto, thrift and flatbuffers lines from `tools/ci/aspect_to_list_allowlist.txt`.

issues.body:
`issue-labels` removes `blocked` as soon as a named pull request merges. Several issues wait on a merged PR *and* a release that carries it, written `Blocked on: <PR URL> (merged and in a <module> release)` (#6593, #6632, #6659). The bot cannot tell the difference: on 2026-11-17 it unblocked #6593 when bazelbuild/rules_rust#4380 merged, but the latest rules_rust release (0.75.0, 2026-10-26) does not carry it, so the issue was picked up for work it cannot do yet.

## Where
- `.github/workflows/issue-labels.yml:79-113`: the unblock step counts a PR as done when `.pull_request.merged_at != null` (`:105`).
- `tools/ci/producers/src/blocker_refs.rs`: `refs()` prints `<owner/repo> <number> <ref>` and drops the rest of the line.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md:232`: documents `Blocked on:` without the release form.

## Fix
- `blocker_refs.rs`: when the `Blocked on:` line contains the word `release`, print a fourth column `release` on each line for an `owner/repo` other than the local one. Add unit tests next to the existing ones in that file: with and without the word, local `#N` never gets the column.
- `issue-labels.yml`: read the fourth column. For a `release` ref that is a merged PR, it is done only when the repo's latest release contains the merge commit: `tag=$(gh api repos/$repo/releases/latest --jq .tag_name)`, `sha=$(gh api repos/$repo/pulls/$num --jq .merge_commit_sha)`, done when `gh api repos/$repo/compare/$tag...$sha --jq .status` is `behind` or `identical`. Any API failure means not done.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md:232`: document `Blocked on: <PR> (merged and in a <module> release)` and that the label stays until a tagged release has the commit.
- After it lands, put `blocked` back on #6593 if rules_rust still has no release with bazelbuild/rules_rust#4380.

## Done when
- A `Blocked on:` line that says `release` keeps `blocked` until the upstream's latest GitHub release contains the merge commit; the unit tests in `blocker_refs.rs` cover the `release` column.

A relative `extends:` in an npm-fetched profile manifest resolved against the unpacked package directory in the global cache (`<cache>/npm/<scope>/<name>/<version>/`). A path such as `../../core/1.0.0` could therefore load another package that was already in the cache, and `../core` failed with a generic "no markspec.yaml" message.

This takes option 1 from the issue:

- A relative `extends:` that stays inside the package still resolves. A package can ship its parent profile in a subdirectory (option 3).
- A path that leaves the package root is `PROFILE-LOAD-001`. The message tells the author to publish the parent as its own package and extend it with an `npm:` specifier (option 2).

`loadChain` now accepts `runNpm` and `npmCacheRoot` options, as it already accepts `runGit`, so the npm tier can be tested without a registry.

Docs updated: spec annex §B.11, the profiles guide, and ADR-008.

## Problem

Follow-up to #1002. A profile fetched as an npm package cannot extend a
sibling profile by a relative path:

```yaml

extends: "../core"
```

The npm resolver unpacks only the requested package, and the package root is
the profile directory. A relative `extends:` that leaves the package root
points at a directory that is not in the cache, and the load fails with
`PROFILE-LOAD-001`.

#1002 fixes the git form by resolving the relative path inside the same
repository at the same tag. The npm form has no equivalent: a package has no
"repository" around it in the cache.

1. Reject a relative `extends:` that leaves the package root, with a specific
   diagnostic that tells the author to use an `npm:` specifier for the parent.
2. Publish the parent as its own package and document `npm:` parents as the
   only supported form.
3. Bundle the parent inside the child package (a `../` path that stays inside
   the package after packing).

#1002, #585

issues.body:
## Problem

`markspec fmt` silently drops text from some entry bodies that contain a caption or a figure. This is the same class of bug as #989: the body AST builder (`core/ast/build.ts`, `mapMdastNode`) detects the node on the flattened text and stores decoded or partial fields, and the emitter re-writes the body from those fields. The ADR-015 `astEquivalent` guard compares against the same lossy AST, so it does not see the loss.

Known cases:

1. **Multi-line caption.** `CAPTION_RE` (`/^(Figure|Table|...):\s+(\S.*)/`) captures up to the first newline only. In `Table: first line\nsecond line kept.`, the second line is dropped.
2. **Link in a caption.** The caption text is the flattened text, so a link keeps its text and loses its URL.
3. **Figure title.** `FigureNode` stores only `alt` and `path`. In `![alt](p.png "Title")`, the title is dropped.
4. **Entities in captions, figures and math.** These nodes store decoded text (`&` becomes `&`). This changes source bytes but not meaning.

On `main` these losses are silent. With #1005, the formatter detects them, keeps the original body and reports MSL-F900.

## Fix

Build caption and figure nodes from the verbatim source slice, as #1005 does for definition lists, so the emitter writes back every line, link and title.

## Acceptance criteria

- `markspec fmt` keeps every line of a multi-line caption, the URL of a link in a caption, and the title of a figure.
- `fmt` is idempotent on these inputs, and `markspec check` reports no MSL-F010 and no MSL-F900 on the result.
- Existing caption detection and position (above or below) are unchanged.

Related: #989, #1005.

issues.body:
## Problem

A monorepo holds several profiles that share a parent:

```text
profiles/
├── core/     shared attributes, labels, delivered corpus
├── a/        extends: "../core"
└── b/        extends: "../core"
```

A consumer that references `profiles/a` by local path resolves the chain. A
consumer that references it by git subpath does not:

```yaml
profiles:
  - "git+https://host/org/repo.git/profiles/a#v1.0.0"
```

```text
error[PROFILE-LOAD-001]: .../.markspec/cache/<hash>/profiles/core/markspec.yaml:1
profile specifier '../core' cannot be resolved: no markspec.yaml at ...
```

The sparse clone contains only the requested subpath, so the sibling
directory is absent from the cache. Annex B §B.11 says that a local specifier
is "relative to the declaring file" and does not exclude this case.

Reproduced with markspec 0.13.0 using a `git+file://` source.

## Current workaround

Name the parent by a full specifier pinned to the same tag:

```yaml
extends: "git+https://host/org/repo.git/profiles/core#v1.0.0"
```

This resolves, but each child manifest must carry its own repository URL and
release tag, release tooling must rewrite them on every release, and a local
edit of the parent is not visible to the child until a tag exists.

## Proposed behaviour

When a manifest fetched from a git source declares a relative `extends:`,
resolve it inside the same repository at the same ref, by adding the parent
path to the sparse checkout. Reject a path that leaves the repository root.

The npm form has the same gap, because the package root is the profile
directory. That case may need a separate decision.

## Related

#585 (`imports:` fan-in block): its `local:` entries would meet the same
limitation for a git-fetched profile.

became `Term : first line`. With this change, `fmt` keeps every line, and `fmt --check` and `check` (MSL-F010) agree with `fmt` on these inputs.

## Why

1. `buildBodyAst` (`core/ast/build.ts`) detected a definition list on the flattened paragraph text, where `:` and `\:` are already decoded to `:`. The detection regular expression keeps only the first line of the definition (`(.+)$` with `/m`). The verbatim split then found no literal `\n:` and the code fell back to the truncated flattened match. A comment said that this fallback could not happen.

## How

- **A. Detection on the verbatim source.** A paragraph is a definition list only when the flattened check matches and the verbatim source also holds a literal marker (a line that starts with `:` and whitespace, after a term line). An encoded or escaped colon is prose, so such a paragraph stays a paragraph. The truncated fallback is removed. `splitVerbatimDeflist` splits at that marker and keeps every other character, so a multi-line definition after a literal colon keeps all its lines. The paragraph types this accepts are a subset of what `main` accepts.
- **B. Text-loss guard.** New `bodyKeepsEveryWord` (`core/formatter/text_loss.ts`): the emitted body must hold every word (Unicode letters or digits) of the original body text at least as many times. The comparison is case-insensitive (modal keywords are lowercased) and ignores

Closes #935.

## What

An entry whose trailer holds an Id-like line with the wrong spelling (`id:`, `Id :`, and in a `.feature` header also `ID:`) no longer gets a second `Id:` from `markspec fmt`. `markspec check` reports the line with a new error, MSL-I009.

## Why

The trailer key grammar requires `Id:`. A line such as `# id: 01…` in a `.feature` header, or `id: 01…` in a Markdown trailer, was not read as the entry's Id. `fmt` then stamped a second Id, and `check` reported nothing about the malformed line.

## Decision

`fmt` never stamps an Id on an entry that holds an Id-like line, and it does not correct the key: the author fixes it by hand. Keys must start with an uppercase letter. In Markdown and source entries, `fmt` still canonicalises `ID:` to `Id:`. A `.feature` header has no such rewrite (ADR-038), so `# ID:` there is also an Id-like line.

## How

- New MSL-I009 (error, identity family), reported at the Id-like line. It is documented in `language.md`, the core data model doc and the diagnostics skill.
- Markdown and source entries: the formatter skips Id stamping when the trailer holds an Id-like line.
- `.feature` headers: `core/parser/feature_file.ts` records the Id-like line (`Entry.idLikeLine`) and reports I009. `core/formatter/feature_file.ts` stamps no Id, and the LSP format path uses the same function.
- MSL-I003 for such an entry says to correct the Id-like line instead of "run fmt".
- The data model doc now states the key-case rule exactly.

## Tests

Parser and formatter unit tests for `id:`, `Id :` and `ID:`. The e2e test `tests/e2e/id_like_trailer_test.ts` runs `check` and then `fmt` twice on Markdown, a `.rs` doc comment and `.feature` headers (above `Feature:` and above `Scenario:`), and checks that the file is unchanged.

agent_prs.body:
Closes #928.

## What

An entry that holds a nested entry-shaped list item (`- [ID] Title` inside another entry) keeps its own trailer and `Id:`. The nested item gets a new warning, MSL-P024, and `markspec fmt` leaves the entry unchanged.

## Why

The parser only reads top-level list items, so a nested `- [ID]` item is body text of its parent. Trailer detection took the last `Key: Value` run of the whole entry, which was the nested item's trailer, so the parent silently took the child's `Id:`. The formatter's shared trailer detection made the same mistake.

## Decision

From the discussion on #928 (D1-D4): nested entries stay unsupported, the parent keeps its own trailer, the nested item gets a parse-family warning, and `fmt` leaves the entry unchanged.

## How

- `Entry.nestedEntryLines`: the line ranges of every nested entry-shaped item, at any depth, taken from the list-item positions (a wrapping plain list item is removed with it). It is not serialized.
- These lines are removed before the trailer search, in the parser and in the formatter (`findAttributeBlockRange`). A `Key: Value` paragraph below the nested item counts as the parent's trailer only when the parent has no trailer above the item.
- MSL-P024 (warning) is reported once per nested item. MSL-P020 is not reported for the same lines.
- `fmt` skips an entry that holds a nested item, apart from the existing tab-marker conversion.
- For such an entry without an `Id:`, MSL-I003 says to move the nested entry to the top level first.
- Docs: `language.md`, the core data model table, and the diagnostics skill.

Closes #982.

## What

Keep the Deno module cache when an e2e test overrides `HOME` for a child `deno run`.

## Why

The default Deno cache path is under `HOME` (`~/Library/Caches/deno` on macOS, `~/.cache/deno` on Linux). A test that sets `HOME` to a temporary folder therefore spawns `deno` with an empty cache. The child then downloads every jsr and npm dependency again, which takes about 33 s per spawn instead of 0.2 s. On a local machine the pre-push `just check` stalled in `tests/e2e/mcp_install_test.ts`.

## How

- `tests/e2e/helpers.ts`: a new `realDenoDir()` returns `DENO_DIR` when it is set, and otherwise the `denoDir` from `deno info --json`. It is computed once per process. `markspecInDir` sets `DENO_DIR` whenever its overrides contain `HOME`.
- `tests/e2e/mcp_install_test.ts`: `runMcpInstallE2e` sets `DENO_DIR` before it overrides `HOME`.

Only two tests override `HOME` for a child `deno`: the MCP install tests, and the cargo-classification test in `self_upgrade_test.ts`, which is covered by the `markspecInDir` change.

## Verification

- `mcp_install_test.ts`: 18 passed in 4 s.
- `just check`: passed (5806 passed, 0 failed) in 5 min 12 s. Before this change, it stalled in this test.

issues.body:
## Problem

E2E tests that spawn `deno run` with `clearEnv: true` and a temporary `HOME`
make the child Deno process use a cold module cache. Deno stores its cache in
`DENO_DIR`, which defaults to `~/Library/Caches/deno` on macOS and
`~/.cache/deno` on Linux. Both paths are under `HOME`. A temporary `HOME`
therefore points to an empty cache, and every spawn downloads all jsr and npm
dependencies again.

## Evidence

- `tests/e2e/mcp_install_test.ts` (`runMcpInstallE2e`) and
  `tests/e2e/self_upgrade_test.ts` (the cargo-classification test, through
  `markspecInDir` with a `HOME` override) set `HOME` to a temp directory.
- One spawn takes 33.3 s with the cold cache and 0.2 s with `DENO_DIR` pinned
  to the real cache directory.
- The pre-push `just check` stalls for minutes because of this.

## Fix

Add a shared helper in `tests/e2e/helpers.ts` that returns the real Deno cache
directory (`DENO_DIR` from the environment, else `denoDir` from
`deno info --json`, computed once). Set `DENO_DIR` in the child environment of
every test that overrides `HOME`.

agent_prs.body:
Closes #955.

Since #938 the language server publishes traceability diagnostics, and a closed buffer is parsed again from disk only when the startup project walk indexed the file. A file created after startup was removed from the index on close, so links to its entries showed a false MSL-L006 until a restart.

- New core predicate `isDiscoverable` (`core/discovery`), built on the same rule helpers as `discoverFiles`: relevant extension, hidden and build-output directories, the `.gitignore` chain, `exclude:`, `inheritGitignoreFrom`, and the walk's file/directory entry-kind check (a symbolic link or a missing path is not discoverable).
- `ProjectContext.closeFile`: a file the walk did not index is kept, parsed from disk and added to the walked set when the project owns it and `isDiscoverable` is true. Otherwise it is removed, as before. A buffer reopened during the discovery check or the read keeps its own entries.
- The limitation is removed from the `closeFile` doc comment and ADR-038 item 11.

Out of scope (D6): files created on disk outside the editor and never opened.

Tests: predicate cases compared with the walk (gitignored, excluded, hidden, wrong extension, negations, inherited `.gitignore`, symlinks, missing paths); ProjectContext close cases (kept, links resolve, excluded, missing, not owned, reopen during the check); e2e create → save → close with no MSL-L006.

agent_prs.title: fix(lsp): keep a file created after startup in the index when its buffer closes

issues.body:
Since #938 (PR #951) the language server publishes traceability diagnostics. On buffer close, a file that the project walk indexed at startup is parsed again from disk (decision D6 on #938). A file **created after the editor started** is not in the walked set, so closing its buffer removes its entries from the index. Every link pointing into that file then shows a false MSL-L006 (or MSL-T014) until the editor restarts or the project is re-indexed.

The limitation is documented in `ProjectContext.closeFile` and ADR-038 item 11.

Possible fix: add a file to the walked set when it is saved inside a project folder that discovery would include (respecting `.gitignore` and `exclude:`), or watch Markdown/source/`.feature` file creation and re-run discovery for that path.

Acceptance: create a new file in the editor, save it, close it; links to its entries stay resolved (no MSL-L006), with an e2e test.
issues.title: LSP: closing a file created after startup drops its entries until the next re-index

The Markdown quick fixes in `lsp/code_actions.ts` now pick the offending line inside the trailer block of the diagnosed entry, never a line of another entry:

agent_prs.body:
Closes #932.

The lazy-load graph test was skipped on Windows. The cause, found with diagnostic draft #954 on the Windows runner: the test passed the entry to `deno info --json` as a file **path** (`d:\a\...\core\mod.ts`). Deno reads the `d:` drive letter as a URL scheme, so the graph held a single module of kind `external` with no dependencies. The dynamic-import guard found no edge, and the static check walked from a root that matched nothing, so it would have passed without reading any import.

- Pass the entry as a `file://` URL (`new URL("../mod.ts", import.meta.url).href`). The Windows skip is removed.
- New guard: the root module must have kind `esm`. A graph that did not resolve the entry now fails instead of passing vacuously. Passing a drive-letter path on macOS reproduces the Windows failure and fails this guard.
- The stale comments about the cause are corrected.

The Windows CI job of this PR is the check that the test now runs and passes there.

issues.body:
The LSP never publishes traceability diagnostics (MSL-L006, MSL-T014, and the other Stage 4 trace rules), for any file type, with or without a profile. `markspec check` does publish them for the same project.

Cause: `WorkspaceIndex.validateAll` (packages/markspec/lsp/workspace.ts) calls core `validate()`, which runs only structural, reference and typl checks. MSL-L006 is emitted only by `validateTraceabilityForEntry` (core/validator/traceability.ts), whose only caller is Stage 4 of `core/validator/pipeline.ts`, which runs only when a profile is given. The LSP never calls the pipeline; the profile it passes to `validateAll` reaches only `suppressDeclaredAttrR010`, `applyCorpusPostPass` and `validateUxilFamily`.

Effect: an editor shows no warning for a `Satisfies:` value that names a display ID that does not exist, while `markspec check` reports it.

agent_prs.title: docs: Gherkin spec section, AST section and guide chapter

issues.body:
**Epic** · label `epic:gherkin`

## Summary

Make Gherkin a structured part of MarkSpec, in two distinct cases that share one parser and one AST:

- **Gherkin AST.** `FeatureNode` is extended with a structure parsed by `@cucumber/gherkin` (Feature, Background, Rule, Scenario, Scenario Outline, Examples, steps, doc strings, data tables, tags). It supports Given/When/Then steps and `*` action steps, including both in one scenario, and Gherkin's spoken languages (`# language: fr`). Step keywords are normalised (`given | when | then | and | but | step`); the raw text stays the source of truth for `fmt`.
- **Case A — Gherkin inside an entry.** A fenced `gherkin` / `feature` block in an entry body is content of its host entry, not an entry of its own. The host's type decides its role: acceptance criteria in a requirement, verification procedure in a test entry. No ID and no trailer of its own; a trace link can address one scenario with a locator (see Decisions).
- **Case B — Gherkin as the entry.** In a `.feature` file, a Feature, Rule or Scenario preceded by a `# [ID] Title` comment and a git-style trailer (#914) is a first-class entry. The display-ID prefix gives the type through the profile, so the same syntax expresses tests (`SWT_`, `SIT_`, …) or requirements (`SRS_`, …). The entry body is the parsed scenario.

## Example — Case A: Gherkin embedded in a MarkSpec entry

````markdown
- [SRS_BRK_0010] Emergency braking on a stationary obstacle

  When a stationary obstacle is detected within 40 m at a speed of
  60 km/h, the braking module shall bring the vehicle to a stop before
  the obstacle.

  ```gherkin
  Scenario: Stop before a stationary obstacle
    Given the ego vehicle drives at 60 km/h
    When a stationary obstacle appears 40 m ahead
    Then the vehicle stops before the obstacle

  Scenario: Brake-system self-test before the drive
    * power on the ECU
    * run the brake self-test
    Then the self-test reports no fault
  ```

      Id: 01J...
      Sati

Closes #941.

Part of #915 (slice "Case B: VS Code language registration + syntax highlighting"). Decisions D1–D7 are recorded on #915 and in the ADR-038 amendment "VS Code client for `.feature` files".

## What changes

- The VS Code client sends `.feature` buffers to the language server. It selects them by file pattern (`**/*.feature`), so this works whichever extension owns the language id. The file watcher now covers `**/*.{md,feature}`.
- The extension contributes the language `feature` (alias Gherkin) with a comment-only language configuration (`#`). It never contributes `cucumber`.
- A Gherkin TextMate grammar (`source.feature.markspec`) colours English keywords, tags, doc strings, tables, `<param>`, and MarkSpec headers (`# [ID] Title`) with their `# Key: value` trailers. The header ID pattern is the same as the core parser's.
- An injection grammar colours MarkSpec headers inside the grammar of "Cucumber (Gherkin) Full Support" (`text.gherkin.feature`).
- The server starts only in a workspace with `.markspec.yaml`, or when one is created later. Contributing a language makes VS Code activate the extension for any `.feature` file, so `activate()` now checks for a MarkSpec project first.

## Coexistence with Cucumber extensions

- The official Cucumber extension (language `cucumber`) has no TextMate grammar, so MarkSpec headers get no colour there. Its users should set `"files.associations": {"*.feature": "cucumber"}` so its language server attaches; MarkSpec still gets the file through the pattern selector. Documented in the VS Code guide and the extension README.
- With "Cucumber (Gherkin) Full Support" installed, both extensions contribute a grammar for `feature` and VS Code uses the last one registered. Headers are coloured in both cases.

issues.body:
## Symptom

Under full `just build` load, `lsp: Markdown parse diagnostics survive the cross-file publish (#939)` (`tests/e2e/lsp_feature_test.ts`) times out waiting for "cross-file diagnostics for bad.md". It passes when the file runs alone.

## Root cause

`openDocument` identified the cross-file publish by its client arrival time: it waited until the latest `publishDiagnostics` arrived at least 1000 ms after the previous one. The server sends the cross-file publish at least 1000 ms after the last parse publish (debounced validation), but the client stamps arrival times in `LspTestClient.handleMessage` when it reads stdout. When the test process is slow to read (CPU load), the parse publish and the cross-file publish are read in the same chunk or close together, so the measured gap is below 1000 ms. No later publish follows, so the condition never becomes true and the wait times out.

## Fix

Use message order instead of wall-clock gaps. Every cross-file run (`ProjectContext.publishAllDiagnostics`) ends with a `workspace/codeLens/refresh` request sent after its publishes; parse-stage publishes send none. The test now waits until a refresh request arrived after the latest publish for the file (`LspTestClient.latestPublishIsCrossFile`). No server change.

issues.body:
In the LSP, parse-stage diagnostics disappear about 1 s after a document is opened or edited. This affects Markdown files (for example MSL-P001) and `.feature` files (MSL-B069, MSL-B062).

Cause: `onDidOpen` and the debounced parse publish the parse diagnostics through `publishFileDiagnostics` (server.ts). About 1 s later, `ProjectContext.publishAllDiagnostics` publishes only `index.validateAll()` output for every tracked file, and sends `[]` for files with no cross-file diagnostics. `validateAll` calls core `validate()`, which does not re-emit parser diagnostics, and `WorkspaceIndex.parseAndUpdateFile` does not store them. So the cross-file publish replaces the parse diagnostics.

Reproduction: open `a.md` containing `- [] Title`. The latest publish shows `MSL-P001` at 300 ms and `[]` at 2.8 s.

Fix plan: store parse diagnostics per file in `WorkspaceIndex`, include them in the cross-file publish, and include the cached cross-file diagnostics in the per-file parse publish. Being fixed on branch feat/gherkin-lsp-feature (#915 LSP slice), because the `.feature` LSP support depends on it.

A `.feature` file can define entries. A comment header `# [ID] Title` (with optional prose and a trailer, as in #914) directly above a Feature, Rule or Scenario makes that node an entry.

agent_prs.title: feat(core): read MarkSpec entries from .feature files

issues.body:
## Problem

MarkSpec carries Gherkin in fenced `gherkin` code blocks inside markdown entries. But executable acceptance / qualification tests are commonly written as plain Cucumber **`.feature`** files (e.g. `spec/<feature>/<name>.feature`, with step definitions). Today the executable `.feature` and the traceable MarkSpec test entry (SQT / CQT) are **two separate artifacts kept in sync by hand** — duplication and drift risk.

This is acute for the SEED / FastTrack BDD/TDD ("Smart-UI") path, where the requirement and its test are meant to be colocated and the Given/When/Then doubles as the proof. The shipped colocated convention already embeds MarkSpec entries in `///` / `/**` doc comments; `.feature` files are the natural extension.

## Proposed solution

Let markspec **read `.feature` files directly** and synthesise Gherkin test entries:

- Each `Scenario` / `Scenario Outline` → a test entry; the `Feature` → the parent grouping.
- Resolve trace links from scenario / feature **tags** — e.g. `@CQT @CREQ_LIGHT_0001` ties the scenario to the requirement it verifies (a `Verifies` edge) and can carry the entry's type and id.
- The `.feature` file becomes the **single source of truth**: the executable artifact *is* the entry, extending the colocated-in-code convention to `.feature` files.
- `markspec compile` / `check` ingest `.feature` alongside `.md` / `.rs` / `.kt`, so the scenarios join the traceability graph and contribute coverage.

## Alternatives considered

- **Richer Gherkin-in-markdown support** — improve authoring and validation of fenced `gherkin` blocks so a separate `.feature` isn't needed. Complementary, but does not remove the executable-vs-entry duplication for teams that run Cucumber on `.feature` files. Could ship alongside.
- **Reconcile outside markspec** (convention / external tooling) — brittle, drifts, and keeps the traceable test outside the graph.

## Context

Raised from SEED / FastTrack (`@ampere/seed`); sibling of #582 (authoring-stance metad

agent_prs.body:
Closes #914.

## Problem

An entry could only carry its attributes in the indented trailer block. Source doc comments often use the `git interpret-trailers` shape, an unindented final paragraph of `Key: Value` lines. The #916 rule (PR #923) already reads that paragraph as the trailer, but Markdown gave no sign that it is not the canonical layout.

## Change

- Markdown: a git-style trailer (final paragraph after a blank line, every line `Key: Value`, holding an `Id:` line or only core keys) raises the new warning `MSL-P023` at the first trailer line. `markspec fmt` rewrites it to the indented form and keeps the Id. A run directly under prose keeps the #916 `MSL-P020` warning; the two never fire for one block.
- Source files: git style and indented trailers give the same entry, with no diagnostic.
- LSP: quick fix for `MSL-P023` indents the trailer.
- Docs: `language.md` §1.3 names the git-style form and `MSL-P023` inside the existing #916 text; data-model §4.1 and the diagnostics skill list the code.

## Tests

- Parser tests per shape (git-style -> P023 only; run under prose -> P020 only; indented -> none; non-core keys and non `Key: value` lines stay body).
- `trailer_agreement_test.ts` gains four git-style Markdown shapes plus an exact fmt output test: fmt never mints a new Id or drops an attribute.
- Source tests for Rust and Java; e2e `check`/`fmt` tests; LSP quick fix test.
- Each new code path was mutation-checked. Bare `check` and `fmt --check` on a `git archive` of origin/main give identical output with main and with this branch.

## Not built

The criterion "`markspec fmt` on a source file stamps a missing `Id:` in git style" is not built: `fmt` does not stamp Ids in source files at all, and ADR-029 formatting is Markdown-only. Follow-up: #925.

agent_prs.title: feat(core): accept git-style trailer blocks

issues.body:
## Goal

Accept a git-style trailer block as the attribute block of an entry. Source doc comments use it as a valid alternative to the indented trailer. Markdown accepts it so the entry still parses, warns about it, and `markspec fmt` rewrites it to the canonical indented form.

## Syntax

The trailer is the last paragraph of the entry, separated from the body by a blank line. Every line of that paragraph has the form `Key: value`, with no indentation required — the same shape `git interpret-trailers` reads.

```rust
/// [SRS_AEB_0030] Time-to-collision calculation
///
/// The decision module shall compute time-to-collision as range divided
/// by closing velocity.
///
/// Id: 01J...
/// Satisfies: SYS_AEB_0012
```

Rules:

- Only the final paragraph can be a trailer. A `Key: value` line in the middle of the body (for example `Example: ...`) stays body text.
- When any line of the final paragraph is not `Key: value`, the whole paragraph is body text.
- A continuation line starts with whitespace (git rule).
- The existing 6-space indented trailer stays valid everywhere.

## Behaviour per format

| Format | Parse | `check` | `fmt` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Source doc comments | accepted | no diagnostic | keeps the author's style; stamps `Id:` in that style |
| Markdown | accepted | new warning: trailer is not indented | rewrites to the indented 6-space form |

## Detection rule (same for Markdown and comments)

The parser on `main` already reads trailing `Key: value` lines as attributes, with any key and no empty line required, which drops body prose (#916). This story replaces that with one stricter rule. The last paragraph is a trailer only when all of these hold:

1. It is a paragraph of its own, with an empty line before it. In Markdown it is a direct child paragraph of the entry's list item in the CommonMark AST.
2. Every line is `Key: Value`, or a continuation line that starts with whitespace.
3. It contains an `Id:` line, or every key is a core recognized t

agent_prs.body:
Closes #916.

## Problem

`splitBodyAndAttributes` took every trailing `Key: value` line as an attribute, with no empty line, indentation or key check. Body prose ending in `Status: draft` or `Note: …` was removed from the body without a diagnostic, and `fmt` moved it into the trailer.

## Change

- New `findTrailerStart` in `core/parser/attributes.ts`, used by both the parser (`splitBodyAndAttributes`) and the formatter (`findAttributeBlockRange`). A trailing run is a trailer only when:
  - it is the indented block (all lines indented ≥4 columns), as before; or
  - it is the final paragraph after an empty line (or the start of the content), every line is `Key: Value` or a whitespace-led continuation, and it holds `Id:` or uses only recognized core trailer keys (the detection rule of #914).
- `RECOGNIZED_TRAILER_KEYS` moves from `parser/markdown.ts` to `parser/attributes.ts` (same set, now shared).

## Tests

- 8 unit tests in `attributes_test.ts` for each rule branch. The old test that expected `Id:` directly after prose to be an attribute now expects body text.
- e2e `trailing_key_value_prose_test.ts`: `fmt` on both reproduction entries keeps the prose in the body (fails on `main`).
- Corpus: bare `check` and `fmt --check` give byte-identical output with `main`'s code and this branch. `just check` passes.

agent_prs.title: fix(core): keep trailing Key: value prose in the entry body

issues.body:
## Problem

`splitBodyAndAttributes` (`packages/markspec/core/parser/attributes.ts`) detects the attribute block line by line. It walks back from the end of the entry and takes every trailing line that matches `ATTR_LINE_RE` (`/^[A-Z][A-Za-z-]*: .+\\?$/`) as an attribute. It does not require an empty line before the run, does not check indentation, and accepts any capitalised key.

As a result, body prose that ends with a `Key: value` line is removed from the body without a parse diagnostic.

## Reproduction

```markdown
- [REQ_0001] Debounce

  The driver shall debounce the input within 5 ms.
  Status: draft

- [REQ_0002] Retry

  The client shall retry a failed request 3 times.

  Rationale: the link drops for up to 1 s.
  Note: see the field report.
```

| Entry      | Result today                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `REQ_0001` | `Status: draft` is taken out of the paragraph. `markspec fmt` writes an indented block directly under the prose line, which CommonMark reads as a lazy paragraph continuation, not as an indented code block. |
| `REQ_0002` | Both lines become attributes. `check` reports only MSL-R010 (unknown attribute). `fmt` moves both lines into the indented trailer.                                                                            |

MSL-P020 and MSL-P021 do not fire, because the lines are consumed as attributes before those checks run. The ADR-015 AST-equivalence gate does not catch it either: the attribute lines are removed from the body on both sides of the comparison.

`docs/spec/language/language.md` §1.3 says the attribute block is the trailing indented code

Closes #919. Closes #917.

## Problem

Two commands fail in the compiled `markspec` binary but work from source:

- `markspec self-upgrade` (and `markspec lock` with an HTTP(S) upstream) fail with `Requires net access`. The binary was compiled with `--allow-net=127.0.0.1`, which covers only the `desk --serve` loopback listener.
- `markspec doc build` fails with `typst: file not found … lib.typ`. Typst runs as a native addon that reads the real file system, so it cannot see files embedded in the binary.

## Changes

- `scripts/compile_binary.ts`: compile with plain `--allow-net`. A fixed host list is not possible: `lock` fetches upstream URLs declared in the user's `project.yaml`.
- `cli/commands/doc.ts`: when `Deno.build.standalone` is true, `stageTypstPackage` copies the embedded Typst package to a temporary folder next to the source document and removes it afterwards. The Windows cross-drive case is unchanged.
- CI `compile-smoke` job: three new steps against the compiled binary: `doc build` produces a non-empty PDF; `self-upgrade --check` reaches the GitHub API; `lock` fetches a snapshot from an HTTP server on `127.0.0.2`, an address outside the old allowlist.

## Verification

Local binaries compiled before and after the change:

| Command | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `doc build t.md` | `file not found … lib.typ` | `t.pdf` written (7.5 KB) |
| `self-upgrade --check` | `Requires net access`, exit 2 | `0.12.1 (up-to-date)`, exit 0 |
| `lock` with HTTP upstream | `MSL-L213 … Requires net access` | exit 0, `1 registries` |

The local `lock` "after" run used `127.0.0.1` because macOS has no `127.0.0.2` alias; the CI step uses `127.0.0.2` on Linux. `just check` passes.

## Notes

- The `self-upgrade` CI step calls the GitHub API without a token, so a shared runner can hit the unauthenticated rate limit.

issues.body:
## Problem

`markspec self-upgrade` fails in the released binary:

```text
Error: failed to reach https://api.github.com/repos/driftsys/markspec/releases/latest: Requires net access to "api.github.com:443", specify the required permissions during compilation using `deno compile --allow-net`
```

Reproduced with the released 0.10.3 and 0.12.1 binaries (macOS arm64). Users cannot upgrade with the documented command (`docs/guide/cli.md`, "self-upgrade") and must download the release by hand.

## Cause

`scripts/compile_binary.ts` compiles with `--allow-net=127.0.0.1`, which covers only the `markspec desk --serve` loopback listener. `self-upgrade` needs `api.github.com` and the release download hosts (`github.com` and its redirect target for release assets).

## To check

`markspec lock` fetches upstream snapshots over the network (ADR-031). Check whether it is affected in the compiled binary in the same way.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `markspec self-upgrade` reaches the GitHub API and downloads the release from the compiled binary.
- [ ] `markspec lock` with a remote upstream works from the compiled binary, or the issue records that it is not affected.
- [ ] A test or CI step runs these commands against the compiled binary, so a narrowed permission list is caught.

mkdir t && cd t

Addresses the "smarter MSL-R014 diagnostic" item from #215 (the `MSL-R014` code in that note is stale; enum-value conformance is reported on `main` as **MSL-A004** via the value-types registry).

## Change

When an enum-typed attribute value is rejected only because of letter case, the validator now suggests the declared spelling:

```
value 'Approved' is not in declared enum [draft, approved, deprecated]; did you mean 'approved'?

The match is case-insensitive against the declared values and suggests their exact spelling, so it also covers mixed-case enums (`inprogress` → `InProgress`). A genuine unknown value still gets the plain "not in declared enum" message with no hint.

- case-only mismatch suggests the declared spelling (the #215 `Approved` → `approved` example);

Follow-up from #871 (#860). Since #871, `markspec lock` in a nested project reads sync mappings from `.markspec/sync/` in each folder from the outermost project root down to the project root; a deeper mapping replaces one for the same `system`. Two gaps remain:

agent_prs.title: fix(lsp): apply the enclosing project's .gitignore to nested projects

issues.body:
Follow-up from #856 / #867.

## Context

#867 made the CLI's bare `check`, `lint` and `fmt` apply the `.gitignore` files of the enclosing (outermost) project when they walk a nested project. The walk passes `discoverFiles` the opt-in option `inheritGitignoreFrom` (`packages/markspec/cli/helpers.ts`, around lines 595 and 630). Without it, a walk that starts at the nested root does not see the repository's `.gitignore`.

## Gap

The LSP does not pass this option. `ProjectContext.indexProject` (`packages/markspec/lsp/project_context.ts`, around line 402) calls `discoverFiles(this.root, io, { exclude })` for every context, including nested ones that the registry finds below the primary root.

Example: the repository root holds `project.yaml` and a `.gitignore` with `generated/`. A nested project `sub/` holds its own `.markspec.yaml`. The CLI skips `sub/generated/*.md`. The LSP indexes those files for the `sub` context, so their entries appear in completions, references and workspace symbols, and their diagnostics are published.

The `discoverProjectRoots` documentation (`outermostOf` in `packages/markspec/core/discovery/projects.ts`) already describes this inheritance as the rule for nested walks.

## Task

- For a nested context, pass `inheritGitignoreFrom: <outermost project root>` to `discoverFiles` in `indexProject`, as the CLI does. Keep the primary context's walk unchanged.
- Add an LSP test for the example above: a file under a directory that only the enclosing project's `.gitignore` excludes is not indexed for the nested context.
- Check whether `findNestedProjectRoots` in the registry needs the same rule, so a config inside an ignored folder of the enclosing project is not treated as a root.
issues.title: LSP: nested projects ignore the enclosing project's .gitignore

agent_prs.title: fix(book): share one display-ID grammar with the LSP

issues.body:
## Context

Found during review of PR #830 (MarkDesk shell with open and read paths, epic #826). The static book renderer links display IDs in prose, and its token grammar differs from the LSP grammar.

## Problem

In `packages/markspec/book/site/mod.ts`, the ID-token pattern requires a token to start and end with an alphanumeric character and treats `/` and `.` as token characters. Results:

- `SYS_A/SYS_B` (two known IDs joined by `/`) is read as one unknown token, so neither ID is linked.
- IDs that end in `_`, `-` or `.` (for example a profile pattern such as `REQ-{n:3d}-`) never link.

The LSP grammar (`DISPLAY_ID_TOKEN_RE` in `packages/markspec/lsp/hover.ts`) accepts these IDs. The two grammars disagree.

## Goal

Make one grammar decision and share it between the book renderer and the LSP, so a display ID is recognised the same way in both.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded on how `/`, `.`, `_` and `-` behave inside and at the ends of a token (for example: split on `/`, allow trailing `_` and `-`).
- [ ] One shared definition lives in `core/` and is used by `book/site/mod.ts`, `lsp/hover.ts`, `lsp/rename.ts` and `lsp/highlights.ts` where they define the same token.
- [ ] `SYS_A/SYS_B` links both IDs when both are known.
- [ ] An ID ending in `_`, `-` or `.` links when it is a known display ID.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the cases above and a prose false-positive case (a known ID next to punctuation).

## Pointers

- `packages/markspec/book/site/mod.ts`
- `packages/markspec/lsp/hover.ts` (`DISPLAY_ID_TOKEN_RE`)
- `packages/markspec/lsp/rename.ts`, `packages/markspec/lsp/highlights.ts`
- `packages/markspec/core/mod.ts` (library boundary)

issues.body:
## Summary

`install.sh` verifies the release tarball with `shasum`, which is a Perl script (bundled with Perl's `Digest::SHA`) — reliably present on macOS but not part of a minimal Alpine/busybox userland, which ships `sha256sum` (a busybox applet) instead. Since the goal of #639 was to make `curl … | sh` work on Alpine/busybox, the script now parses and starts correctly there but can fail later at the checksum step with `shasum: not found`.

## Where

`install.sh` — `(cd "$tmpdir" && shasum -a 256 -c "$tarball.sha256")`. (Unchanged by #639, which only fixed shell syntax; flagged because it sits in the same happy path the PR's goal targets. Not verified live — no Alpine container available in review.)

## Fix direction

Prefer `sha256sum` when available, fall back to `shasum`:

```sh
if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sha256sum -c "$tarball.sha256"
else
  shasum -a 256 -c "$tarball.sha256"
fi
```

Or confirm via an actual Alpine CI job that `shasum` is guaranteed present and drop this note.

## Related (optional, #639)

The new `sh-installer` CI guard runs `shellcheck -s sh install.sh` only (static). It would catch a bashism but not a POSIX-legal logic regression (e.g. dropping a `|| { …; exit 1; }` guard). Consider a cheap functional smoke step under `dash`/`busybox ash`.

agent_prs.title: refactor(core): remove the unused source-file formatter

issues.body:
## Problem

`formatSource` in `packages/markspec/core/formatter/source.ts` replaces every doc-comment line with `[object Object]`. For example, a Rust doc comment becomes:

```rust
/// [object Object]
/// [object Object]
/// [object Object]
fn brake() {}
```

## Cause

Commit `9080877f` (#409, LineMap for source-file doc-comment entries) changed the return types of two parser helpers in `core/parser/source.ts`:

- `stripLineCommentPrefix` now returns `PrefixStripResult` (`{ text, prefixWidth, rule }`), not a string.
- `stripBlockCommentPrefix` now returns `BlockStripResult`, not `string[]`.

`formatter/source.ts` was not updated. It still pushes the return values into a `string[]`:

- line 123: `currentLines.push(stripLineCommentPrefix(child));`
- line 131: `lines: stripBlockCommentPrefix(child.text),`

## Why CI did not catch it

No file imports `core/formatter/source.ts`. It is not in `core/mod.ts`, the CLI, the LSP, or the MCP server, and it has no test file. The type-check targets in `just check` do not reach it, so its type errors go unreported:

```text
$ deno check packages/markspec/core/formatter/source.ts
TS2345 [ERROR]: Argument of type 'PrefixStripResult' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string'.
TS2740 [ERROR]: Type 'BlockStripResult' is missing the following properties from type 'string[]': length, pop, push, concat, and 35 more.
Found 2 errors.
```

## User impact

None today. `markspec fmt` formats Markdown files only (ADR-029), so `markspec fmt src/lib.rs` leaves the file unchanged and never calls `formatSource`. The LSP also returns no edits for source files.

## Options

1. Delete `core/formatter/source.ts`, because nothing uses it and ADR-029 limits `fmt` to Markdown.
2. Fix it: use `.text` from `PrefixStripResult`, the lines from `BlockStripResult`, add a unit test, and add the file to the type-check targets.

Whichever option is chosen, check whether other modules exist that nothing imports and that no type-check target reaches.

## Accep

issues.body:
## Summary

A **malformed** `markspec.lock` is invisible to `markspec doctor` — it reports the lockfile "present", skips the entire drift block, and exits 0 — while `markspec check`'s equivalent gate hard-errors (`MSL-L001`) on the exact same file. This is the one case `doctor` gives zero advance warning for, undermining the "proactive onramp so a stale/broken lockfile is surfaced before `check` blocks on it" purpose of #658/#682.

## Where

`packages/markspec/cli/commands/doctor.ts` — when `parseLockfile` fails, `lockfilePresent = true` but `parsedLock = undefined`; the `if (parsedLock)` guard then skips the drift block, and the text/JSON output shows only `{ present: true }` with no diagnostic. `core/gates/mod.ts` (`lockfileDriftGate`) instead returns `lockParse.diagnostics` (severity `error`) → `check` exits 1.

## Failure scenario

A project's `markspec.lock` gets corrupted (bad merge, truncated write, stray edit). `doctor` says "healthy" (exit 0); the next `check` run hard-fails with `MSL-L001`. `doctor` never warns.

## Fix direction

When `lockfilePresent && !parsedLock`, surface a low-severity `doctor` diagnostic (e.g. `lockfile-unparseable`) forwarding `parseLockfile`'s code/message, without necessarily promoting the exit code.

## Related debt (from same review)

- `doctor`'s drift walk shares `collectProjectEntries`, so a transient read failure silently skews its edge count/hash (see the collector issue).
- Drift detection is coarse (hash + counts only; no per-edge add/remove/retarget diff) despite the lockfile carrying a per-edge ULID ledger — worth a follow-up.
- No e2e test covers corpus-blindness (`!e.origin`) or source-file edge-parity for `doctor`'s drift check specifically.

issues.body:
## Summary

`markspec fmt` unconditionally loads the dprint-markdown WASM formatter before the file loop, even when no target file is Markdown. This works against the "single binary, lazy loading" principle and makes a Markdown-only dependency failure abort a command that had nothing to do with Markdown.

## Where

`packages/markspec/cli/commands/fmt.ts` — `loadMarkdownFormatter()` (via `loadMarkdownFormatterOrExit`) is called before the loop, regardless of `files.some(isMarkdown)`. ## Failure scenario

`markspec fmt src/main.rs` (a purely source-file, explicit-arg invocation) pays WASM-load latency and, if the plugin fails to load, exits 1 — even though the command never needed the Markdown pass.

## Fix direction

Hoist the load to just before it's first needed, or gate it on `files.some(isMarkdown)`.

## Related test debt (#670)

No test exercises `<!-- dprint-ignore -->` (documented in ADR-029 as a supported per-block opt-out), the `80 − indent` width-budget math for a body with nested list content, raw-HTML blocks through the whole-document pass, or a BOM-prefixed document. issues.body:
## Summary

`FENCE_RE` toggles the "inside fenced code" state on **any** line starting with ≥3 backticks or tildes, ignoring CommonMark fence char/length matching. A shorter ` ``` ` fence nested inside a longer ` ```` ` fence is (per CommonMark §4.5) literal content, but it is treated as a close — so a fenced illustrative example can be rewritten as if it were live content. This is the exact data-corruption class #668/#679 set out to prevent, triggered by fence *length/marker* mismatch instead of fence *absence*.

## Where

`packages/markspec/core/util/fence.ts`:

```ts
export const FENCE_RE = /^\s*(```|~~~)/;
```

Consumed by `walkProseLines` and `isLineFenced`, and inline-duplicated in `packages/markspec/core/refs/mod.ts` (main loop + `\`-continuation loop). This shared util now backs live user actions: `canonicalizeRefs` (#679) **and** LSP rename/highlight (#685).

## Failure scenario (verified by running `canonicalizeRefs`)

A ` ```` ` block wrapping a nested ` ``` ` block whose content includes a trace-attribute-shaped line: the inner ` ``` ` is still inside the outer fence per CommonMark, but the current toggle treats it as a close, so the line gets healed/rewritten. This repo's own docs (`docs/spec/language/language.md`, `docs/guide/typl.md`, `docs/spec/language/typl.md`) already use nested ` ```` `/` ``` ` examples — a latent landmine. `FENCE_RE` also accepts a mismatched marker type (a ` ``` ` opener "closed" by a stray `~~~`) and any leading whitespace (a genuine 4-space indented code block whose text starts with 3 backticks is misdetected).

## Fix direction

Track the currently-open fence's marker char and length; only toggle closed on a line with the same char and length ≥ the opener's. Fix once in `core/util/fence.ts` (`walkProseLines`/`isLineFenced`) and ensure `canonicalizeRefs`'s two inline copies pick it up (or delegate to the shared util). Add tests for: tilde fences, longer opener with nested shorter fence, mismatched marker types, and indented w

agent_prs.title: fix(core): apply exclude: after every .gitignore in project discovery

issues.body:
## Summary

`project.yaml` `exclude:` does **not** actually take precedence over `.gitignore`, contradicting its own documented semantics ("Applied after `.gitignore` rules"). In the common case where the project's own `.gitignore` also lists a directory, a `project.yaml` `exclude:` (or a `!negation`) is silently overridden — the documented escape hatch fails with no error and no warning.

## Where

`packages/markspec/core/discovery/mod.ts` — `discoverFiles`/`walk`. The initial rule list is `[...BUILTIN_SKIP_RULES, ...excludeRules]`, and `walk()` then appends each directory's own `.gitignore` rules **after** that inherited set at every recursion level:

```ts
const active = raw !== undefined && raw.length > 0
  ? [...rules, ...parseGitignore(raw, relDir)]   // rules = [BUILTIN, exclude]; .gitignore appended last
  : rules;
```

Under last-match-wins, whatever is appended last wins, so `.gitignore` (root or nested) overrides `exclude:` — the opposite of the docstrings in `mod.ts`, `core/model/mod.ts` (`ProjectConfig.exclude`), `docs/guide/cli.md`, and ADR-027.

## Reproduction (verified by two independent reviewers)

- `exclude: ["secrets/"]` + root `.gitignore` containing `!secrets/` → `secrets/a.md` is discovered anyway (`exclude:` loses).
- This repo's own `.gitignore` already lists `dist/`, `build/`, `target/`, so a `!dist/` in `project.yaml` `exclude:` cannot re-include `dist/` — violating issue #661's acceptance criterion.

Also (related, lower severity): an explicit `markspec check <dir>/` invocation passes no `exclude:` to `discoverFiles` at all (`cli/helpers.ts`), so after #664's built-in build-dir skip, `exclude:` has *no* override channel for explicit-directory invocations.

## Fix direction

Thread `excludeRules` through `walk()` as a separate layer, applied **after** each level's merged `.gitignore` rules when computing `active`, so `exclude:` is the highest-precedence layer at every level (matching the docs). Add a regression test: `exclude:` overrides

issues.body:
## Summary

`MSL-P020` (misplaced trailer) still false-positives on ordinary body prose that starts with a generated-origin relation keyword (`Contains:`, `Caused:`, `Affected-by:`, `Mitigates:`, `Used-by:`, `Derives:`, `Superseded-by:`, `Allocated:`, …) as a lead-in — the same false-positive class #654/#655 set out to fix, just with a different trigger-word set.

## Where

`packages/markspec/core/parser/markdown.ts` — the `RECOGNIZED_TRAILER_KEYS` allowlist unions in the full `UNIVERSAL_ATTRIBUTE_KEYS`, which includes 15 `origin: "generated"` (computed-only) inverse-relation keys (see `packages/markspec/core/model/attributes.ts`). These are never legitimately hand-authored — the compiler generates them, and `MSL-A030` already rejects them if typed by a human — yet they remain in the recognized-trailer set, so a prose line beginning with one still trips `MSL-P020`.

## Reproduction (verified on current `main`)

```markdown
- [STK_0096] Contains prose lead-in

  The system shall support the modes below.

  Contains: three subassemblies and a wiring harness.

      Id: 01HGW2Q8MNP3RSTVWXYZABCDEF
```

→ `error[MSL-P020] … trailers block is not the final indented code block …`, exit 1. Same for `Caused:`, `Affected-by:`, `Mitigates:`, `Allocated:`, `Used-by:`, `Derives:`, `Superseded-by:`.

## Fix direction

Exclude `origin === "generated"` keys from `RECOGNIZED_TRAILER_KEYS` (core already exposes `attributeSpec(key).origin`, used at `validator/mod.ts` for MSL-A030), keeping the deliberate `Verified-by` exception. This aligns the set with the LSP's own `TRAILER_KEYS` (`lsp/completions.ts`), which already omits every generated-origin key except `Verified-by`. Add an e2e case with a generated-origin key as body prose.

Incomplete fix in #655 (`fix(core): flag only recognized trailer keys as misplaced trailers (P020)`).

issues.body:
## Summary

The shared `collectProjectEntries` helper silently skips any discovered-but-unreadable file, changing `lock` / `compile --frozen` / `fmt` from hard-fail to **silent partial-success** — and breaking the lock↔check parity the shared collector exists to guarantee.

## Where

`packages/markspec/core/collect/mod.ts`:

```ts
const content = await io.readFile(file);
if (content === undefined) continue;   // swallows ENOENT/EACCES/race, drops the file's entries + edges
```

`DiscoveryIO.readFile` returns `undefined` on any read error. Before #684, `lock.ts`'s private `collectEntries` used `Deno.readTextFile` with no try/catch — an unreadable file **threw** and crashed the command (loud failure). Now it is silently omitted.

## Failure scenario (reproduced)

A requirements file becomes momentarily unreadable (permission glitch, a build tool relocking it, a dangling symlink, or a file deleted between `discoverFiles`' listing and the collector's read). `markspec lock` now succeeds and writes a `markspec.lock` silently missing that file's edges — exit 0, no warning. Meanwhile `check`'s bare-mode loop still hard-fails on the same file (`Deno.readTextFile` in try/catch → `console.error` + exit 1). So `lock` (the pinner) and `check` (the checker) no longer walk the same effective file set — the "phantom drift / missed drift" class this collector was unified to prevent. A traceability tool silently mis-pinning its lockfile is an integrity gap.

`doctor`'s drift walk shares the same helper, so a transient read failure can also silently skew its edge count/hash (surfaced separately in the #682 review).

## Fix direction

Have `collectProjectEntries` surface skipped files (e.g. return `{ entries, skipped: string[] }` or an `onUnreadable` callback), and have `lock`/`compile --frozen`/`fmt` treat a non-empty skip list as fatal (matching `check`). If silent skip is intentional for some commands, document it and add a regression test. No test in `core/collect/mod_test.ts` curr

issues.body:
## Summary

The LSP `onRenameRequest` handler — the one that actually performs the workspace-wide mutation — is missing the fenced-cursor guard that #685 added to `onPrepareRename` and `onDocumentHighlight`. A rename initiated on a display ID inside a fenced illustrative example will rename every **real** project-wide occurrence of that ID, one the user never intended to touch.

## Where

`packages/markspec/lsp/server.ts` — `onRenameRequest`. `onPrepareRename` and `onDocumentHighlight` both gate on `isLineFenced(document.getText(), params.position.line)`, but `onRenameRequest` does not.

## Failure scenario

A fenced illustrative example reuses a real entry's display ID (exactly the situation #680 describes in this repo's own spec/guide docs). An LSP client sends `textDocument/rename` directly on that fenced cursor — the LSP spec does not mandate `prepareRename` be called first even when `prepareProvider: true` (plausible for scripted/agent-driven clients, or editors that don't chain prepare→rename). `onRenameRequest` extracts `oldId` via fence-blind `displayIdAtPosition`, resolves it to the real entry, and builds a `WorkspaceEdit` renaming every genuine occurrence across the project. `findIdOccurrencesInFile`'s new fence-awareness correctly leaves the sample text itself untouched, but every real declaration/reference elsewhere is renamed.

## Fix direction

Add `if (isLineFenced(document.getText(), params.position.line)) return null;` to `onRenameRequest`, mirroring `onPrepareRename`. Note: no `server.ts` request handler has direct test coverage today — consider a handler-level regression test.

Gap in #685 (`fix(lsp): fence-aware rename/highlights`).

_Found in post-merge review of PRs merged 2026-06-26 → 07-03._

issues.body:
## Summary

The published project-config JSON schema omits `exclude`, a real, actively-validated `project.yaml` field (ADR-027). The schema therefore does not fully describe the very file that cites it — including this repo's own `project.yaml`, which sets `exclude:` and points its `$schema` at this schema.

## Where

`schemas/project/v1.json` — the `properties` object lists `category`/`description`/`repository`/`license` (which `parseProjectConfig` doesn't even consume) but not `exclude`, which **is** parsed and type-checked in `packages/markspec/core/config/mod.ts` and is a first-class field on `ProjectConfig` (`packages/markspec/core/model/mod.ts`). The regression test `packages/markspec/core/config/project_schema_test.ts` (hardcoded key list) also omits `exclude`, so CI doesn't catch the gap.

## Failure scenario

A contributor edits `project.yaml` in an editor with JSON-Schema-backed YAML tooling: `exclude:` gets no autocomplete and no hover docs, and a project.yaml authored from the schema's property list never discovers the `exclude:` feature exists — despite it being a documented, working CLI feature used in this repo.

## Fix direction

Add to `schemas/project/v1.json`:

```json
"exclude": {
  "type": "array",
  "items": { "type": "string" },
  "description": "Gitignore-syntax patterns excluded from project file discovery."
}
```

and add `"exclude"` to the expected-key list in `project_schema_test.ts`.

Gap in #630 (`fix(docs): serve /schemas/ landing page and fix project.yaml $schema URL`).

Closes #859.

## Problem

`markspec fmt` ended an entry at a lazy continuation line (a paragraph line indented less than the list item content). The formatter then treated the trailer as being outside the entry and wrote a second `Id:` trailer.

## Change

- The parser records `Entry.endLine`, the last line of the mdast list item.
- `findItemEnd` takes an optional `itemEndFloor` and starts its indentation scan at that line, so a lazy line inside the item no longer ends the item early. The ADR-029 prose pass and `removeEmptyTrailerLines` pass `Entry.endLine`.
- In the entry pass, the formatter adds its own line-count change to `endLine`, so the floor stays correct after a wrapped title is joined onto one line.
- This branch is rebased on #876. The item indent comes from `contentColumn(...)`, so a wide list marker (`-   [ID]`) and a lazy line in the same entry are both handled.
- `desk/proposals_test.ts`: the `previewBody` expectation is now `Old body lazy.`, because the lazy line is part of the body.

A Codex review (`gpt-6.1-sol`) gave Spec PASS. It reproduced one Minor finding: the `findItemEnd` doc comment described the old scan. The second commit fixes it. ## Context

Found while implementing #837 (MarkDesk first prompt feature). Reproduced on `main` at `729c5bf`.

## Problem

`markspec fmt` duplicates an entry's trailer, including its `Id:` line, when the entry body has a CommonMark lazy continuation line: a paragraph line that is indented less than the body indent but still continues the paragraph.

Input `lazy.md`:

```markdown
- [SYS_BRK_0001] Brake request

  The system shall apply the brakes when the pedal
lazy continuation line.

      Id: 01M684SWWG8YV437XGYAX63E0Q
      Satisfies: STK_BRK_0001
```

Run `markspec fmt lazy.md`. It prints an MSL-F012 info line for line 7. The output then holds the trailer twice:

```markdown
- [SYS_BRK_0001] Brake request

  The system shall apply the brakes when the pedal

      Id: 01M684SWWG8YV437XGYAX63E0Q
      Satisfies: STK_BRK_0001
lazy continuation line.

      Id: 01M684SWWG8YV437XGYAX63E0Q
      Satisfies: STK_BRK_0001
```

The lazy line moves out of the entry, and a second `Id:` with the same ULID appears in the file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `markspec fmt` on the input above keeps exactly one trailer, and keeps the lazy line in the entry body. Re-indenting it to the body indent is acceptable.
- [ ] A regression test in `packages/markspec/core/formatter/` covers this input.
- [ ] `markspec check` on the formatted output reports no duplicate `Id:`.

## Pointers

- `packages/markspec/core/formatter/mod.ts` (body range: `findItemEnd`, `findAttributeBlockRange`)
- #837 works around this in the desk preview by checking the formatted current body against the raw body.
