agent_prs.body:
Fixes #8237

Auto-claim stopped firing for users on Twitch's newer chat layout.

Twitch's claimable-bonus component now has two render paths, chosen by an `isOneChat` prop that the points summary passes down. The classic path still renders a `ScCoreButton` wrapping `.claimable-bonus__icon`, so auto-claim keeps working there. The OneChat path renders an overlay button whose `InjectLayout` wrapper overwrites the button's `className`. That leaves the button with only styled-components hashes, so there's no `.claimable-bonus__icon` for our observer to match and nothing gets clicked. The only way to tell it apart is its localized `aria-label`.

In both layouts, Twitch mounts a fresh `.tw-transition` div around the claim button inside `[data-test-selector="community-points-summary"]` when a bonus becomes available. So the module now:

- observes `.tw-transition` and ignores anything outside the points summary
- takes the button inside it and confirms through the React tree (new `twitch.getClaimableBonus`) that it belongs to the claimable-bonus component, so reward/popover buttons in the summary are never clicked
- skips the error state (this replaces the old `ScCoreButtonDestructive` check) and dedupes on the button, because nested transitions can emit together on first mount

### Verification

- Read the live Twitch bundle to confirm the two render paths and that the summary is the only call site.
- On a live channel (Chrome, store build loaded, auto-claim off), I faked an available claim on the real component (`getClaim` override, `onClick` stubbed so nothing went to Twitch) and ran a page-side copy of this callback behind a MutationObserver that mimics `src/observers/dom.js`. Result: exactly one click per claim in both classic and OneChat layouts, over two cycles each. The errored state was not clicked, and the "Bits and Points Balances" button never resolved to the claim component.
- **Not verified:** a natural bonus claimed end to end by the dev bundl
agent_prs.title: fix: auto-claim bonus points in the newer chat layout

agent_prs.body: Fixes #8192 With **Autoplay offline channel video** disabled, going from an offline channel to a live one through the sidebar left the live stream paused and muted until a page refresh. agent_prs.body:
BetterTTV runs its own read-only GraphQL queries through Twitch's Apollo client, and `client.query` defaults to `cache-first`, which writes every result into Twitch's normalized cache.

The emote menu's `BTTVAvailableEmotesForChannel` query fires on every `channel.updated`, whether or not the BetterTTV emote menu is ever opened, and selects `channel { self { availableEmoteSets } }` without `id`. Twitch keys `ChannelSelfEdge` on `id`, so Apollo can't identify our copy and writes it inline over Twitch's `{__ref: "ChannelSelfEdge:<id>"}`. Everything Twitch cached on that entity (`availableEmoteSetsPaginated`, `communityPoints`, predictions, unban requests, weekly visit rewards) is orphaned, every watched query reading through `channel.self` goes `partial` and refetches, and until those land Twitch's native emote picker has no available emote sets, so channel emotes read as locked. Twitch's chat recently moved to `availableEmoteSetsPaginated` on that entity, which is why a query unchanged since 2022 started biting.

The same hazard exists in other queries we send (`/followed` selects `user.self` without an id, the chatbot lookup selects `user.channel` without an id, the mod card writes an inline `relationship`), so this defaults `graphqlQuery` to `fetchPolicy: 'no-cache'` rather than patching selections one at a time. Our queries never need Twitch's cache, and callers can still pass a policy explicitly.

**Verification** (live Twitch popout chat, Apollo 3.8.7): polled `Channel:<id>.self` in Twitch's cache while running the emote query through Twitch's client. With the default policy it flips from a ref to an inline object at ~500ms and Twitch refetches six queries (`AvailableEmotesForChannelPaginated`, `ChannelPointsContext`, `ChannelPointsPredictionContext`, `WeeklyVisitRewardsQuery`, `LastUnbanRequest`, `CommunityPointsAvailableClaim`). With `no-cache` the ref is untouched and nothing refetches. Not reproduced: the persistent locked state the reporter sees on an accou
agent_prs.title: fix: keep graphql queries out of twitch's apollo cache

agent_prs.body:
Twitch lets Tier 2/3 subscribers post GIPHY GIFs in chat, but the selector only exists in the native emote picker. This adds a GIFs mode to the BetterTTV emote menu.

Closes #8210

**What**
- A segmented emote/GIF toggle next to the emote menu search input, shown only where Twitch's gif picker is available for the channel.
- Everything the picker needs — the GIPHY api key, content rating, allowlist/enabled flags, the channel's `hasGifs` products, the viewer's sub tier, the current cooldown, and the send handler — is read from Twitch's own mounted gif picker controller via its React props (`twitch.getGifPickerController`), so BetterTTV issues no config query or send mutation of its own.
- GIF mode reuses the search input (`Search GIPHY` placeholder): trending by default, search with a 300ms debounce, a responsive multicol masonry (min two columns, more as the menu widens) capped at 40 results. The one request we make is the GIPHY REST fetch for the grid, using the channel's key from the controller, content rating capped at `pg` to match the native picker.
- Clicking a gif sends it through Twitch's own `onSelectGif` handler (their mutation, their cooldown recording, their tracking). The cooldown turns each tile's Send pill into a disabled ring countdown (against a 30s capacity), seeded from the controller's persisted per-channel cooldown so it survives a reopen or reload. Viewers below Tier 2, and the temporarily-unavailable state, render like the emote list's empty-search state.
- Availability, results, loading and cooldown live in a zustand store (`gif-picker-store`), driven from event handlers (menu open, mode switch, debounced search) rather than effects.
- Extracted a shared `EmptyState` component from EmoteList's inline empty-search markup (its `No results...` string is now i18n'd as a side effect).

**Verification**
The UI and flows (toggle, trending, search, send, cooldown pill, gating, dark theme) were verified live on Twitch popout/standard chat during devel

## 문제 / 우선순위
사용자 실플레이 제보: 멀티플레이에서 게스트 동기화가 여전히 이상합니다. Devin PoC의 최우선 조사·수정 대상으로 등록합니다.

- 서비스: https://game.cocy.io/arpg/
- 제보일: 2026-10-30 (KST)
- 분류: 버그 / 높은 우선순위

## 재현 조사 절차
1. 별도 브라우저/기기에서 방을 생성하고 다른 플레이어가 게스트로 참가합니다.
2. 정상 출정 후 양측에서 이동·공격·스킬 사용을 수행합니다.
3. 호스트/게스트 역할을 바꾸어 반복합니다.
4. 동일 tick 기준 호스트 권위 상태, 게스트 수신 snapshot, 실제 적용 상태, 보간/예측 상태, 최종 화면에 사용하는 위치·액션·HP를 구분해서 비교합니다.
5. 정상 네트워크뿐 아니라 현실적인 지연·지터 및 포커스 전환/재접속 경계를 확인합니다.

위 절차는 조사 시나리오이며 특정 조건에서 재현 확정했다는 뜻은 아닙니다.

## 기대 동작
게스트가 호스트의 전투 상태를 일관되게 적용·표시하고, 지연 이후에도 수렴해야 합니다. 입력 예측 및 보간은 허용하되 지속적인 어긋남·이전 상태 잔존을 만들지 않아야 합니다.

## 실제 동작
사용자가 게스트 싱크 불일치가 지속된다고 제보했습니다. 재현 로그와 원인 분석은 후속 증거로 보강할 예정입니다.

## 완료 조건
- [ ] 실제 불일치 사례의 최소 재현 절차와 호스트/게스트 비교 증거 확보
- [ ] 수신 패킷 불일치인지, 적용·예측·보간·렌더 경로 문제인지 구분하고 원인 설명
- [ ] 호스트/게스트 양방향 역할 및 지연·지터 조건에서 수정 확인
- [ ] 회귀 테스트 추가: **host sent == guest received만 검사해서 완료 처리하지 않기**
- [ ] 게스트 실제 적용/표시 상태의 수렴 및 입력 반응 검증
- [ ] 정산·저장·재접속에 부작용 없는지 확인

## 작업 범위
이 이슈는 게임 기능 추가나 밸런스 변경 요청이 아닙니다. 재현되지 않았다면 그 한계를 명시하고, 사용자 제보를 패킷 parity 검사만으로 종결하지 마세요. 실사용자 저장 데이터는 사용하지 말고 격리된 테스트 계정/저장 fixture를 사용하세요.


## 추가 조사 증거 (2026-10-30)
독립 Node CoopSession/네트워크 어댑터 테스트에서 **단방향60ms, 손실0, 지터0** 조건을 적용했습니다. 같은 tick 기준 적용 snapshot843개의 호스트 위치/HP 불일치는0이지만, 게스트 `session.view()` 표시 좌표가 피격·회피 구간에서 연속 **60.632px, 60.264px** 점프했습니다. 0ms 대조군의 prediction snap은0입니다.

- 다음 점프: frame647, snapshotTick320, predictionTick325, reason=gross, distance59.601px, smoothing window0ms

The Alpha Strike **Add Units** search form has a new **Filter By Special Abilities** row, next to the faction filter and laid out the same way:

issues.body:
Reported on Discord (#bug-reports, "MUL will try to load all 8k entries into list").

## What happens

On **Alpha Strike → Roster → Add Units**, a search that matches most of the bundled Master Unit List locks the page. The easiest way to hit it: leave **Search Terms** empty and set **Unit Lists** to *MUL 2.0 + MUL 1.0 leftovers*. The page tries to show all 8,700+ units at once and stops responding.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open https://heysporky.github.io/battletech-tools/ → Alpha Strike → Roster → Add Units.
2. Clear the **Search Terms** box.
3. Change **Unit Lists** to *MUL 2.0 + MUL 1.0 leftovers* (changing Type, Era, Role or Tech does the same).
4. The browser freezes while it builds the results table.

## Cause

`CONST_MUL_API_ENABLED` is `false`, so every search goes to the bundled data (`getCachedMULSearchResults`). Unlike the old live MUL request, that path has no minimum search length, so an empty term matches everything. `_AddUnitsPage.tsx` then renders every result as its own `<tbody>`, with two rows and several buttons per unit, all in one pass.

Filtering 8,700 records is fast. Rendering them is what locks the page.

## Fix

Paginate the search results so only one page of rows is ever rendered, with page controls and a "showing X–Y of N" count. Start again from page 1 whenever the results or the sort change.

agent_prs.body:
Fixes #95.

## The bug
`AlphaStrikeUnit.setStructure()` wrote its value to `armor`:

```ts
public setStructure( nv: number ) {
    this.armor = nv;      // now: this.structure = nv;
}
```

## Why this is a bug and not a misleading name
- `structure` is its own field on `AlphaStrikeUnit`. The structure track (`currentStructure`) is built from it, and the BV conversion reads it. Armor and Structure are separate values on an Alpha Strike unit (*ASCE* p.25).
- `setArmor()` sits directly above it and already sets `armor`. With the bug, the two setters did exactly the same thing, so `structure` had no setter at all.
- It has been this way since the pair was added together in dc4d7899 ("Start of AS unit editor..."). The two bodies are identical, which points to a copy-paste slip, not a deliberate alias.
- Nothing overrides it: no class extends `AlphaStrikeUnit`.
- Nothing calls it, directly or through a dynamic `"set" + field` lookup. So no saved data or user-visible behavior depends on the old result, and the fix can't break anything.

## Change
- `setStructure()` now sets `structure`.
- Two regression tests in `alpha-strike-unit.test.ts`: each setter changes only its own value. The `setStructure` test fails on `master` (`expected 3 to be 7`) and passes with the fix.

## Verification
- `npx vitest run --project unit`: 297 passed, 0 failed.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: 0 errors.
- ESLint on both changed files: clean.

agent_prs.body:
Fixes #69

## What

`BattleMech._getSpeedFactorModifier()` now uses the TechManual p. 316 Speed Factor formula for every speed:

- Speed Factor MP = Run MP + round(Jump MP / 2)
- Speed Factor = (1 + (MP - 5) / 10) ^ 1.2, rounded to two decimals

This replaces the 25-branch if/else chain. The chain was right for MP 0-25, but above 25 it computed `1 + x^1.2` instead of `(1 + x)^1.2` and didn't round half the Jump MP. The implementation matches MegaMek's `BVCalculator.offensiveSpeedFactor` / `offensiveSpeedFactorMP`.

## Why it's safe

- The formula gives exactly the TechManual table values for MP 0-25, so nothing changes below 26 MP.
- I compared the old and new code for every Run 0-45 × Jump 0-30 combination. They differ only where Speed Factor MP ≥ 26.
- I imported all 508 bundled SSW mechs before and after the change, and every Battle Value is identical (the fastest bundled mech is MP 25).
- 20-ton mech with Walk 18 (Run 27, MP 27): Speed Factor goes from 3.58 to 4.04 and BV from 167 to 176.

One file changed, +12 / −57.

issues.body:
## Summary

`BattleMech._getSpeedFactorModifier()` (`src/classes/battlemech.ts`) returns the wrong Speed Factor for any unit whose Speed Factor MP is above 25, so the Battle Value of very fast custom units is too low.

## Canon

TechManual p. 316 (BV 2.0, offensive Speed Factor):

- Speed Factor MP = Run MP + round(Jump MP / 2)
- Speed Factor = (1 + (MP - 5) / 10) ^ 1.2, rounded to two decimals

The TechManual's Speed Factor Table is this same formula evaluated for MP 0-25. MegaMek implements it the same way in [`BVCalculator.offensiveSpeedFactor` / `offensiveSpeedFactorMP`](https://github.com/MegaMek/megamek/blob/main/megamek/src/megamek/common/battleValue/BVCalculator.java).

## What the code does

For MP 0-25 the if/else chain returns the table values correctly. Above 25 it falls back to

```ts
return +(1 + Math.pow(((this.getRunSpeed() + (this.getJumpSpeed() / 2) - 5) / 10), 1.2)).toFixed(2);
```

which computes `1 + x^1.2` instead of `(1 + x)^1.2` and also skips the rounding of half the Jump MP. The result is lower than the MP 25 value, so the factor goes *down* as the unit gets faster:

| Speed Factor MP | Current | Canon |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 25 | 3.74 | 3.74 |
| 26 | 3.44 | 3.89 |
| 28 | 3.72 | 4.19 |
| 30 | 4.00 | 4.50 |
| 40 | 5.50 | 6.08 |

## Reproduce

Mech Creator: 20 tons, Walking MP 18 (Run 27). Speed Factor MP = 27: the app uses 3.58 where canon is 4.04, so BV is 167 instead of 176.

None of the 508 bundled SSW mechs are affected (the fastest has MP 25); this hits custom builds, which the creator allows up to 20 Walk / 20 Jump.

## Proposed fix

Replace the chain with the single canonical formula (it reproduces the MP 0-25 table exactly). PR to follow.

## Summary

Closes the fail-open production configuration gaps from issue #125 by adding fail-fast guards in `config.MustLoad()` plus deployment documentation. The app now refuses to start in production with insecure settings, instead of silently shipping a long-lived credential over plain HTTP or accepting a brute-forceable signing secret.

### Changes
- **Secure cookies enforced in production** (`config/config.go`): when `ENVIRONMENT == "production"` and `SECURE_COOKIES != "true"`, `MustLoad` panics. The refresh cookie and OAuth-state cookie inherit `Secure` from this flag, so this prevents transmitting them over plain HTTP. In non-production it logs a `slog.Warn` so local/dev configs keep working.
- **JWT secret strength validated** (`config/config.go`): `JWT_SECRET` shorter than 32 bytes panics in production, warns elsewhere. 32 bytes matches the 256-bit HS256 key and the HKDF-derived 32-byte OAuth-cookie AES key, so a weak secret no longer degrades both signing and cookie encryption.
- **CORS wildcard + credentials rejected** (`config/config.go`): any `*` entry in `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` panics, since the server sets `AllowCredentials: true` and the Fetch spec forbids combining a wildcard origin with credentials.
- **Proxy/RealIP trust documented** (`main.go` `rateLimiter` comment + `.env.example`): rate limiting and request logging key on `X-Forwarded-For` via `ctx.RealIP()`, so the deployment note instructs running behind a reverse proxy that strips client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For`. Per the issue, the `RealIP` trust config is left as a documentation concern (out of scope for code).
- **`.env.example`**: documented the JWT length requirement, the CORS wildcard rejection, the production secure-cookie requirement, and the reverse-proxy deployment note.

### How it satisfies the issue
Acceptance criteria:
- [x] Production startup fails on insecure cookie / weak secret config — `MustLoad` panics in both cases when `ENVIRONMENT=production`.
- [x] CORS cannot combin
agent_prs.title: fix: enforce secure-by-default production config (#125)

issues.body:
## Severity: High 🟠 — Security (fail-open production config)

Several security controls default to the insecure value and are **never enforced in production**:

1. **Secure cookie flag off by default.** `secureCookies := os.Getenv("SECURE_COOKIES") == "true"` (`config/config.go:104`) defaults to `false` with no tie to `Environment == "production"`. The 30-day refresh cookie (`auth.go:37`) and OAuth state cookie (`oauth.go:77`) derive `Secure` from it. A prod deploy that forgets the var transmits a long-lived credential over plain HTTP.
2. **JWT secret strength unvalidated.** `config/config.go:72-75` only checks non-emptiness; a weak `JWT_SECRET=secret` is accepted and used for HS256 signing **and** the HKDF-derived OAuth AES key → brute-force / token forgery feasible.
3. **Deployment trust assumptions (review):** CORS is set with `AllowCredentials: true` and origins straight from env with no guard against `*` (`main.go:102-107`); all rate limiters key on `ctx.RealIP()` (`main.go:123,143,179`), which trusts `X-Forwarded-For` by default — bypassable if exposed without a trusted proxy stripping that header.

### Fix
- In `MustLoad`, force `secureCookies=true` (or panic) when `Environment == "production"`; at minimum log a loud startup warning.
- Require `JWT_SECRET` to be ≥32 bytes (at least in production).
- Document/validate the proxy assumption for `RealIP`; reject `*` origin when `AllowCredentials` is true.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Production startup fails (or loudly warns) on insecure cookie / weak secret config.
- [ ] CORS cannot combine `*` with credentials.


---

The spreadsheet reader can misdetect a valid comma-separated CSV as semicolon-separated when quoted text cells contain several semicolons.

## Problem

`_sniff_delimiter` scored each candidate as `(rows with modal width) * (modal width)`. A wrong delimiter producing 4 fields on 2 rows scored 2×4=8, beating the correct delimiter producing 2 fields on 3 rows (3×2=6).

## Solution

Change scoring to use a tuple `(consistency, modal)` where:
- `consistency` = number of rows with the modal field count
- `modal` = the most common field count

This prioritizes consistency across rows first, then uses field count as a tiebreaker. The correct delimiter now scores (3, 2), which beats the wrong delimiter's (2, 4).

## Testing

Verified with the reproduction case from the issue:
```python
data = b'id,note\n1,"a;b;c;d"\n2,"e;f;g;h"\n3,"i;j;k;l"\n'
book = parse(data, "example.csv")
# Now correctly detects comma delimiter
```

### Description

In `lib/crewai/src/crewai/a2a/auth/server_schemes.py`, `SimpleTokenAuth` and `APIKeyServerAuth` both allow empty credentials to pass authentication and compare secrets with `!=` instead of a constant-time comparison:

1. `SimpleTokenAuth(token="")` coerces `""` into `SecretStr("")`, which is truthy (`if self.token:` succeeds), so `_get_expected_token()` returns `""`. Similarly, when `AUTH_TOKEN=""` is set in the environment, `os.environ.get("AUTH_TOKEN")` returns `""` (not `None`). In both cases `expected is None` is `False`, and `await auth.authenticate("")` succeeds and returns `AuthenticatedUser(token="", scheme="simple_token")`.
2. `APIKeyServerAuth(api_key="")` accepts an empty API key at construction, so `await auth.authenticate("")` returns `AuthenticatedUser(token="", scheme="api_key")`.
3. Both schemes compare the incoming credential against the expected secret using `!=` rather than `hmac.compare_digest`.

async def main() -> None:
    os.environ["AUTH_TOKEN"] = ""
    print(await SimpleTokenAuth().authenticate(""))
    print(await SimpleTokenAuth(token="").authenticate(""))
    print(await APIKeyServerAuth(api_key="").authenticate(""))

### Description

`CrewJSONEncoder` turns enum values into `str(member)`, so a field like `Status.DONE` (value `"done"`) gets saved as `"Status.DONE"`. The kickoff task outputs storage uses this encoder, so a task output with an enum field is stored in a form that can't be loaded back into its own pydantic model.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import json
from enum import Enum
from pydantic import BaseModel
from crewai.utilities.crew_json_encoder import CrewJSONEncoder

class Status(Enum):
    DONE = "done"

class Result(BaseModel):
    status: Status

saved = json.dumps(Result(status=Status.DONE), cls=CrewJSONEncoder)
print(saved)                       # {"status": "Status.DONE"}
Result.model_validate_json(saved)  # ValidationError
```

### Expected behavior

The enum should be saved by its value (`{"status": "done"}`), the same as pydantic's own `model_dump_json()`, so it round-trips.

See above.

macOS

3.13

1.15.43 (current `main`)

N/A

Venv

  Input should be 'done' [type=enum, input_value='Status.DONE', input_type=str]

In `CrewJSONEncoder.default`, return `obj.value` for `Enum` instead of `str(obj)`. UUID and Decimal can keep using `str()`.

`RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter` in `crewai_tools/rag/chunkers/base_chunker.py` duplicates separators when `keep_separator=True` (the default for the built-in chunkers). issues.body:
A call to an Anthropic model with more than three files fails with a 400 from Anthropic before any answer:

```
anthropic.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'invalid_request_error',
'message': 'A maximum of 4 blocks with cache_control may be provided. Found 5.'}}
```

Inside an agent, crewai also marks the system prompt for caching, so four files are enough to fail; a direct `LLM.call` fails at five.

**Reproduce** (crewai 1.15.43, any Claude model):

```python
from crewai import LLM
from crewai_files import ImageFile

llm = LLM(model="anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5")
llm.call([{"role": "user", "content": "How many images?",
           "files": {f"img{i}": ImageFile(source="any.png") for i in range(5)}}])
# 400: A maximum of 4 blocks with cache_control may be provided. Found 5.
```

**Cause.** `crewai_files/formatting/anthropic.py`, `AnthropicFormatter.format_block()`, adds `"cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}` to every file block. Anthropic allows at most four cache breakpoints per request, and `AnthropicCompletion._format_messages_for_anthropic` already places its own on the system prompt and on the last block of each marked user message.

**Fix.** Stop stamping file blocks. The provider's breakpoint on the marked message's last block caches everything before it, files included.

## Related issue

Fixes #7912. Supersedes #7926 (@kimnamu's PR, which this builds on: its geo-prefix stripping, the `in.`/`ca.` prefixes and Nova 2 Lite come from there).

## Summary

`BedrockCompletion.supports_multimodal()` matched a fixed list of model names, so Claude 5 models and any Claude or Nova model behind a non-`us.` inference profile (`eu.`, `apac.`, `jp.`, ...) were refused `input_files`. Bedrock now strips one geo prefix and decides Claude support by major version, the same check #9215 gave the Anthropic provider, so Haiku 5 and future families need no change.

- `claude_supports_vision()` moves to `llms/providers/utils/common.py`; the Anthropic and Bedrock providers both call it (Bedrock can't import the Anthropic module without the `anthropic` SDK).
- Non-Claude vision models (GPT-6, Nova Lite/Pro/Premier/2 Lite) are matched after the geo prefix is stripped, so the `us.`/`global.` duplicate rows are gone.
- `_REGION_PREFIXES` gains `in.` and `ca.`, which also fixes the context window for those profiles (from #7926).
- No public API change.
- Out: application inference profile ARNs still return `False`; the Anthropic file limit (more than ~3 files) is a separate PR.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

New cases cover Claude 3/4/5 behind every geo prefix, Nova and Nova 2 Lite, and stay `False` for Claude 2/Instant, Nova Micro, gpt-oss and Llama. 17 of them fail with the source change reverted. `tests/llms` + `test_llm.py`: 1392 passed. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy` clean on changed files. ## Description

`crewai/llms/providers/bedrock/completion.py` checks whether the provider stopped because
it hit the token cap, and warns:

```python
if stop_reason == "max_tokens":
    logging.warning("Response truncated due to max_tokens limit")
```

No other provider does. In crewai 1.15.16 that check exists at four sites, all in
`bedrock/completion.py` (683, 1121, 1285, 1723). Grepping the published wheel for any
equivalent branch elsewhere returns nothing:

```
$ grep -rnE 'stop_reason *== *"max_tokens"|finish_reason *== *"length"|== *"MAX_TOKENS"' crewai/
crewai/llms/providers/bedrock/completion.py:683
crewai/llms/providers/bedrock/completion.py:1121
crewai/llms/providers/bedrock/completion.py:1285
crewai/llms/providers/bedrock/completion.py:1723
```

So on Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Gemini, `openai_compatible` and Snowflake, a response cut
off mid-sentence is handed back to the agent as if it were a complete answer. The agent
then reasons over a partial result, or parses it and fails, with nothing distinguishing
"the model was interrupted" from "the model answered badly".

and the `finish_reason` crewAI puts on its own `LLMCallCompletedEvent`:

agent_prs.body:
Closes #8068 (part of #8065).

## What this adds
`create_jev_noul_guardrail(question, threshold, *, client=None, model=None, question_name="output_passes")` in `crewai_tools.tools.jev_noul_guardrail`. It returns a callable task guardrail that asks TypeSafe's Jev model one Noul question about the task output (`state=output.raw`) and compares Jev's probability with the threshold.

- **Pass:** probability `>= threshold` returns `(True, output.raw)`, so the output is kept unchanged. A probability equal to the threshold passes; this is documented.
- **Reject:** returns `(False, reason)`. The reason includes the question, the probability and the threshold, and it goes back to the agent through the task's existing `guardrail_max_retries` loop. The guardrail adds no retry loop of its own.
- **Missing or malformed answers never pass:** no answer under the question name, a non-Noul answer, a missing value, a non-number or bool, NaN or infinity, or a value outside [0, 1] all reject with an explicit reason.
- **SDK failures stay explicit:** exceptions from `system_one` (authentication, network, API, response validation) propagate unchanged. They never count as a pass and are not turned into a retry.
- **Config validation:** the threshold must be a finite real number in [0, 1] (bools and strings are rejected), and the question and question name must be non-empty. Invalid config raises `ValueError` when the guardrail is created.
- **Client:** pass any client with a compatible `system_one` method (a `SystemOneClient` protocol; `TypeSafeClient` satisfies it under mypy). With no client, a `typesafe_sdk.TypeSafeClient` is created from the `TYPESAFE_*` env vars for each check and closed in a `finally` block.
- The guardrail only reads Noul probabilities. Choice confidence is not used, so the two are not treated as interchangeable.

## Design notes
- **A function, not a callable class.** `LLMGuardrailStartedEvent` calls `inspect.getsource()` on callable guardrails that are not `LLMGuar

issues.body:
## Goal

Implement a callable guardrail that asks Jev one Noul question about a task output and uses a caller-configured threshold to accept or reject it.

**Difficulty:** Medium. **Estimated effort:** 3–5 days.
**Skills:** Python, SDK mocks, callable guardrails, and error handling.

[Official Noul documentation](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul) defines the answer as the probability that the question is true. It has no separate Choice-style confidence field. Question wording should make “true” mean the output satisfies the guardrail.

## Scope and dependencies

Build in the Jev integration package using the official TypeSafe SDK and shared client configuration where available. Compose with CrewAI's existing callable-guardrail interface; do not add a Jev provider to `BaseLLM` or change default guardrail behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Implement the Python callable with a configurable question/instruction, model/client, and finite probability threshold in [0, 1].
- [ ] Evaluate the task's output using one named Noul question and compare its answer to the threshold. Document the equality boundary.
- [ ] Return the existing guardrail success/rejection tuple shape, preserving the original output on success and supplying a useful rejection reason.
- [ ] Missing, malformed, non-finite, or out-of-range answers cannot accept the output. SDK failures remain explicit and cannot become success.
- [ ] Respect the existing task guardrail retry mechanism rather than adding another unbounded retry loop.
- [ ] Add mocked behavioral tests for accept/reject, threshold boundaries, missing answer, and SDK failure.
- [ ] Include one opt-in task example. Required tests use no API keys or paid calls.
- [ ] Preserve SDK probability semantics; do not treat low Choice confidence as the same thing as a Noul rejection.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

[FlexAI](https://flex.ai) serves ~30 open-weight models (chat, embedding, vision, image, speech, transcription) behind an OpenAI-compatible API at `https://api.flex.ai/v1`.

Today a CrewAI user can reach it only by passing the endpoint by hand on every `LLM(...)` call:

agent_prs.body:
`create_crew()` accepts a `provider` parameter that callers use to pre-select
a model provider. Inside the function a `for provider, env_keys in
ENV_VARS.items()` loop reuses that same name, which means the parameter value
is silently overwritten by the last key iterated from `ENV_VARS`. Any logic
after the loop that inspects `provider` sees the wrong value.

The fix renames the loop variable to `env_provider` and updates the one
reference to it inside the loop body (`existing_provider = env_provider`).
The parameter name is unchanged and its value is preserved for the entire
function lifetime.

### Feature Area

Other: CLI evaluation workflow.

### Is your feature request related to an existing bug?

NA. This is a usability extension to the recently introduced `crewai eval` command.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add `crewai eval --no-open` to print the evaluation report URL and continue waiting for and printing the verdict without launching a browser. Keep the existing behavior unchanged when the flag is omitted, and allow the flag alongside `--run EXECUTION_ID`.

This is useful over SSH, in CI, and in terminal-only environments where the URL needs to be copied or surfaced in logs but opening a browser is unwanted or impossible.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Automatically detecting a headless session would be more brittle and could change behavior unexpectedly. Redirecting stdout does not prevent `webbrowser.open()` from running.

The current CLI prints the URL and then calls `webbrowser.open()` whenever AMP supplies a URL; only the internal daemon-mode check suppresses the browser. This proposal is intentionally limited to an explicit opt-out.

Yes, I'd be happy to submit a pull request.

Different authored tool names can collapse to the same provider-facing identifier: for example, `WebSearch` and `web_search` both sanitize to `web_search`, and distinct names with the same first 64 characters collide after truncation. ## Summary

Add deterministic collision resolution for sanitized tool names. Apply the resolved names consistently when tools are advertised and when tools are dispatched.

## Rationale

`sanitize_tool_name` can map different original names to the same sanitized name. Existing collision paths include ASCII case normalization and over-length truncation. The non-ASCII fallback added in #7625 also uses a truncated hash, so it can collide in principle.

Current consumers can expose duplicate names or overwrite an earlier tool when a dispatch map uses a sanitized name as its key.

## Affected areas

- `lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/string_utils.py`
- `get_tool_names`
- Tool dispatch-map construction in `lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/tool_utils.py`
- Related native function-calling schema generation and regression tests

## Required changes

- Define one deterministic collision-resolution step for a collection of tools.
- Preserve the current sanitized name when it is unique.
- Add stable, deterministic suffixes for colliding names.
- Keep every resolved name within the 64-character provider limit.
- Use the same resolved names for advertised tool names and dispatch-map keys.
- Do not rely only on increasing the hash length or on `convert_tools_to_openai_schema` duplicate handling.

## Acceptance criteria

- Distinct tools that sanitize to the same base name receive distinct resolved names.
- Resolution is stable for the same tool collection and ordering.
- Resolved names satisfy provider naming and length constraints.
- `get_tool_names`, generated schemas, and tool execution dispatch use matching resolved names.

## Related issue

Fixes #7534

## Summary

On the LiteLLM fallback path, streamed `tool_calls` deltas are accumulated per `index` and rebuilt into `ChatCompletionDeltaToolCall` objects for the caller. The reassembly had two defects:

- **Dropped call ids.** `AccumulatedToolArgs` had no `id` field and neither accumulation site captured `tool_call.id`, so every rebuilt call carried `id=None`. The executor then writes `tool_calls[].id = null` / `tool_call_id = null` into the message history, which breaks call/result correlation and fails provider-side validation on the next turn.
- **Doubled arguments on the async path.** `_ahandle_streaming_response` replayed the rebuilt calls into `_handle_streaming_tool_calls` with the same accumulator that already held the complete arguments; `+=` produced `{"a":1}{"a":1}`, `json.loads` always failed, and the tool call was silently dropped — so `acall(..., available_functions=..., stream=True)` never executed the tool and returned `""`.

issues.body:
### Description

When `LLM.stream=True` on the LiteLLM fallback path (`LLM(..., is_litellm=True)`, i.e. any model not routed to a native SDK provider), streamed `tool_calls` deltas are accumulated per `index` and rebuilt into new `ChatCompletionDeltaToolCall` objects. The reassembly is wrong twice:

1. **The wire `id` is never copied.** Every rebuilt call returns `id=None`. The agent executor extracts that id (`extract_tool_call_info` → `getattr(tool_call, "id", ...)`) and writes the assistant turn as `tool_calls[].id = null` plus `tool_call_id = null` on each `role="tool"` result. The next LLM request then carries null ids — providers that require string ids (e.g. OpenAI: `messages[].tool_calls[].id`, `messages[].tool_call_id`) reject it, and tool results can no longer be correlated to their calls.
2. **The async path double-appends the arguments.** After the stream ends, `_ahandle_streaming_response` replays the rebuilt calls into `_handle_streaming_tool_calls` passing the *same* `accumulated_tool_args` dict that already holds the complete arguments. The handler does `accumulator.function.arguments += tool_call.function.arguments`, producing `{"a":1}{"a":1}`, so `json.loads` always fails and the tool call is silently dropped — `acall` returns the accumulated text (`""`) instead of executing the function whenever `available_functions` is provided.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
llm = LLM(model="gpt-4o-mini", is_litellm=True, stream=True)

# stream chunks: first delta carries id + name + half the args,
# second delta carries the rest of the args (litellm.types.utils objects)
result = llm.call("weather?", tools=[get_weather_schema])
assert result[0].id == "call_abc123"   # actual: None

result = await llm.acall(
    "weather?", tools=[get_weather_schema],
    available_functions={"get_weather": fn},
)
# actual: fn is never called and result == ""
```

## Problem

Fixes #6735.

When `response_model` is set on a streaming call, `_handle_streaming_response` runs the
`InternalInstructor.to_pydantic()` / `model_dump_json()` conversion **inside** the `try`
that wraps chunk consumption. The `except Exception` below that `try` exists to salvage a
partial response from a stream that broke mid-flight — it returns `full_response` whenever
there is text to return.

As a result, a conversion failure is routed through the salvage path: a caller who asked
for a `BaseModel`-shaped result gets the raw prose back, with **no exception** and no signal
that conversion was attempted and failed.

A conversion failure is not a broken stream. The stream completed successfully; the output
just didn't match the schema. Routing it through the salvage path conflates the two.

Wrap the `response_model` conversion in its own `try`/`except` that raises a dedicated

method. Genuine mid-stream breaks still fall through to the salvage path unchanged.

currently perform any `response_model` conversion (it returns `full_response` directly), so there

Closes #7668

## Summary

- The JSON Schema spec does not require a `"type"` key on every node — a schema with an `"items"` key can only describe an array, and one with `"properties"` can only describe an object, even without an explicit `"type"`. This is legal, spec-compliant JSON Schema that some MCP servers rely on (observed in practice with Atlassian's remote MCP server, but the gap is generic: it affects any MCP/A2A source that omits `"type"` this way, not just one integration).
- `_json_schema_to_pydantic_type` (`pydantic_schema_utils.py`) had no inference for this: when `type_` was `None` it fell straight through to `return Any`, even when `items`/`properties` made the real shape obvious. That silently drops validation for the field (anything is accepted) and, worse, when the schema round-trips back out via `generate_model_description`/`model.model_json_schema()`, an `Any`-typed union member serializes as an empty `{}` — which the pre-existing `schema == {}` branch in `ensure_type_in_schemas` then relabels `{"type": "object"}`, even when the original node was really an array. The tool schema shown to the LLM ends up wrong, not just permissive.

issues.body:
### Description

JSON Schema does not require a `"type"` key on every node — a schema with an `"items"` key can only describe an array, and one with `"properties"` can only describe an object, even without an explicit `"type"`. This is legal, spec-compliant JSON Schema.

crewAI's shared schema-conversion utility (`lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/pydantic_schema_utils.py`), used to turn *any* MCP tool or A2A JSON Schema into a Pydantic model, doesn't account for this:

- `_json_schema_to_pydantic_type` falls through to `return Any` whenever `json_schema.get("type")` is `None`, regardless of other structural keywords present. A field described as `{"items": {"type": "string"}}` (no `"type": "array"`) becomes Python `Any` in the generated Pydantic model — no validation, and the real shape is lost.
- Because the field is now `Any`, when the schema is later regenerated for the LLM via `generate_model_description`, that union member serializes back out as an empty `{}`. The existing `ensure_type_in_schemas` has a branch that turns any empty `{}` inside `anyOf`/`oneOf` into `{"type": "object"}` — correct for a genuinely empty schema, but wrong here: an array field ends up advertised to the model as a generic object.

This is a gap in crewAI's shared JSON-Schema-to-Pydantic conversion utility, not something specific to one MCP server — any MCP or A2A schema source that omits `"type"` on a node with `items`/`properties` triggers it.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Call `create_model_from_schema` (or go through the standard MCP tool path: `MCPServerAdapter`/`CrewAIToolAdapter.adapt`, or crewAI's native `MCPToolResolver`) with a JSON Schema where a field's `anyOf` contains a member that has `items` (or `properties`) but no explicit `"type"`, e.g.:
   ```python
   schema = {
       "type": "object",
       "properties": {
           "fields": {
               "anyOf": [
                   {"items": {"type": "string"}},
                   {"type": "null"},
               ],

## What

Two path-containment security tests in `lib/crewai-tools` create a symlink in

- `tests/utilities/test_safe_path.py` — `test_rejects_symlink_escape`
- `tests/tools/test_file_writer_tool.py` — `test_blocks_symlink_escape`

Wrap each `os.symlink()` call: if it fails with `WinError 1314`, `pytest.skip`

issues.body:
### Description

When an MCP tool returns more than one content block, CrewAI hands only `result.content[0]` to the agent and drops the rest. If the first block is not text (an image, say), the agent gets the pydantic repr of that block, base64 data included, and the text after it is lost.

The same first-block logic exists in three places on main (c6e500ab):

- `MCPClient._call_tool_impl` ([client.py#L623-L629](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/blob/c6e500ab3730ccf3badb640c6e0170e5c6aa3882/lib/crewai/src/crewai/mcp/client.py#L623-L629)). This is the path for `mcps=[MCPServerStdio(...) / MCPServerHTTP(...) / MCPServerSSE(...)]` and AMP references, through `MCPNativeTool`.
- `MCPToolWrapper._execute_tool` ([mcp_tool_wrapper.py#L182-L187](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/blob/c6e500ab3730ccf3badb640c6e0170e5c6aa3882/lib/crewai/src/crewai/tools/mcp_tool_wrapper.py#L182-L187)). This is the path for plain `mcps=["https://..."]` URLs.
- `MCPNativeTool._extract_content` ([mcp_native_tool.py#L150-L163](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/blob/c6e500ab3730ccf3badb640c6e0170e5c6aa3882/lib/crewai/src/crewai/tools/mcp_native_tool.py#L150-L163)). Today this is only a fallback, because `MCPClient` already returns a string, but it has the same logic.

`MCPServerAdapter` in crewai-tools already keeps every text block ([mcp_adapter.py#L61-L74](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/blob/c6e500ab3730ccf3badb640c6e0170e5c6aa3882/lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/adapters/mcp_adapter.py#L61-L74)), which suggests that dropping blocks in the native paths is not intended.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Save this MCP server as `server.py`:

```python

### Description

`LanceDBStorage` treats memory scopes as hierarchical paths (`/crew/sales/agent`),
and the documented contract for a scoped view is "root path and below". But the
SQL predicates used for scope filtering on the read/query paths are naive
string prefixes:

- `search()` builds `scope LIKE '<prefix>%'`
- `_scan_rows()` builds `scope LIKE '<prefix>%'` — shared by `list_records()`,
  `get_scope_info()`, `list_categories()`, `count()`, and the
  categories/metadata branch of `delete()`

`LIKE '/app%'` matches not only `/app` and `/app/sub` but also the sibling scope
`/apple` (and `/appendix`, `/app2`, ...). Two consequences:

1. **Cross-scope leakage on reads.** `search`, `list_records`, `get_scope_info`,
   `count`, and `list_categories` for scope `/app` all include records stored
   under `/apple`. `Memory.recall(query, scope="/app")`, a `MemoryScope` rooted
   at `/app`, and a `MemorySlice` containing `/app` can therefore surface
   memories belonging to a different agent/crew scope — the exact isolation the
   scope mechanism exists to provide.
2. **Over-deletion on filtered deletes.** `delete(scope_prefix="/app",
   categories=[...])` scans `/apple` rows too and deletes matching records in
   the sibling scope.

The inconsistency is visible inside the same file: `reset()` already uses a
path-boundary-aware predicate (`scope >= '<prefix>' AND scope <
'<prefix>/\uffff'`), and the Qdrant edge backend filters on a `scope_ancestors`
payload field, so both correctly exclude `/apple` when operating on `/app`.
Only the LIKE-based paths are wrong.

A secondary inconsistency: `search()`/`_scan_rows()` never normalize a missing
leading slash (`scope_prefix="app"` produces `LIKE 'app%'`, which matches
nothing because every stored scope starts with `/`), while `delete()` and
`get_scope_info()` do normalize. The unescaped prefix is also interpolated raw
into the SQL string, so a scope containing `'` breaks the query and `%`/`_` act
as LIKE wildcards.

`Prompts._build_prompt` has two code paths: the default one joins the i18n slices selected in `task_execution` (`role_playing`, plus `tools`/`no_tools`, plus exactly one task slice: `task`, `native_task`, or `task_no_tools`). The custom-template path (taken when both `system_template` and `prompt_template` are set) ignores which task slice was selected:

- `{{ .System }}` is filled with every component except the literal `"task"`, so `native_task` and `task_no_tools` are *not* excluded — the selected task slice leaks into the system section.
- `{{ .Prompt }}` is always filled with the hardcoded `"task"` slice regardless of the selection.

The `"task"` slice contains ReAct-only instructions: *"use the tools available and give your best Final Answer, your job depends on it!"* and a `Thought:` seed. The result:

- An agent with **no tools** (`task_no_tools` selected) is told to "use the tools available" and gets a `Thought:` ReAct scaffold — the exact thought-leakage problem the `use_system_prompt` path was fixed for.

**Summary.** `land.sh` names a task's run directory `$STATE_DIR/$(date +%F)-t$n` (templates/loop/land.sh:285 and :375). The name carries the date and the task number but not the plan or the run, so two runs on the same day that reach the same task number share a directory: a second plan's task 1, or a retry of the same task after the switch was flipped. The new run writes `gen-0.*`, `check-0.log`, `skeptic-0.*` over the old ones, and the old run's other files (`gen-1.*`, `skeptic-1.*`, `merge.log`) sit beside them looking like this run's output. Nothing in the loop reads the stale files today, so this is a forensics defect, not a landing defect: `morning` and a human reading the directory cannot tell which run produced which file.

**Versions.** nightshift 0.1.3 (`templates/loop/land.sh`, same lines in 0.1.2 as stamped in ambient's `loop/.nightshift`). macOS 26.6.2, bash 3.2 from `/bin/bash`.

The bar: state as a materialized view over the runtime own ordered log **plus checkpoints** — a separate durable event log is not required.

Two runtimes clear it. `agentic-pekko` uses real Pekko Persistence (`EventSourcedBehavior` + journal) and has a test proving the transcript survives entity restart while brain invocations stay flat. `agentic-clj` uses real Datomic with working `as-of` time travel.

**The flagship Flink runtime does not.** `enableCheckpointing`, `CheckpointingMode`, `setStateBackend` and `CheckpointedFunction` appear **zero times** in the framework — only in a build-excluded demo, and there with the non-durable `HashMapStateBackend`.

Supporting gaps:
- `PollingSource` splits are explicitly stateless (`serialize()` returns `new byte[0]`), so every non-Kafka channel is at-most-once across a restart.
- No sink implements `SupportsCommitter`/`TwoPhaseCommittingSink`.
- Savepoint restore of an A2A bridge stream NPEs (snapshot restored with a null serializer arg).
- Both Flink-state vector memories call `getMapState()` from non-keyed `ProcessFunction`s, so they throw in `open()` and are unreachable through the shipped corpus/retrieval API.

Deliverable: checkpointing configured (or explicitly documented as a caller responsibility), a durable state backend option, sources that actually snapshot offsets, and a test that restarts from a checkpoint and asserts the conversation view is intact.

issues.body:
The suite is large and mostly green (770 tests pass in the main module), but three mechanisms let it report green on untested code.

1. **Fixture-missing skips hide the flagship parity proof.** The cross-runtime parity tests resolve `examples/pipelines/banking.yaml` via a **CWD-relative** path guarded by `assumeTrue`. Under the documented build invocation the path misses and they silently skip — measured: 3/3 and 5/6 skipped. Re-run with the correct working directory, **all 21 parity/replay/CEP tests pass** — so the parity claim is real but unverified by default. The same fail-open pattern exists in the Pekko and Clojure parity tests.
2. **H2 stands in for Postgres**, which is precisely why the invalid-SQL bug in #5 shipped. Needs Testcontainers.
3. **`*IT.java` files are unrunnable in every profile** — no failsafe plugin, and surefires filename filter excludes them before the tag filter applies. Net effect: all Redis/Fluss integration tests have **zero executed coverage**, and no IT exists at all for Postgres, pgvector, Qdrant or Milvus (~2,300 LOC of untested vector-store drivers).

Also worth a sweep: a set of tests assert nothing meaningful — one re-declares the parser regexes locally instead of importing the class under test, one constructs a function and never invokes it, and the config test never sets an env var despite the class existing to resolve them.

issues.body:
Verified defects in shipped code (file:line citations in the tracker).

- **Every validation rejection is read as an approval.** `ValidationFunction` does `response.toUpperCase().contains("VALID")` — and `"INVALID"` contains `"VALID"`. The gate can never reject. Zero tests on the class.
- **The "production default" Postgres store cannot write to Postgres.** Both Postgres stores emit `MERGE INTO ... KEY (col) VALUES (...)`, which is H2-proprietary; PostgreSQL 15 MERGE has no `KEY` clause. Invisible because every test runs H2.
- **Three transient-field NPEs that only fire once a job is distributed** (field initializers do not run on deserialization). One of them makes **robots.txt silently fail open** in any serialized crawler.
- **Unguarded `ServiceLoader` iteration** over the VectorStore SPI throws `NoClassDefFoundError` for any consumer on a default build. The correct guarded pattern already exists 50 lines up in the same file.
- **Guardrail redaction never reaches the transcript.** The raw reply is persisted before guardrails run, and only the returned object is redacted — so blocked content is replayed into the next prompt.
- `docker-compose-session.yml` pins a Flink 1.20.1 image while the project targets 2.2.1; since Flink is `provided`, jobs cannot run on it.
